42.descriptionId: This basic sword won't make a hero out of you, that's for sure.

47.descriptionId: This well-forged sword is ideal for beginners.

53.descriptionId: Forged by a Fencing Master, this sword will make a hero of you if you know how to handle it... However, be careful, the sword comes with a curse - it always falls down a well. Eventually, here or there, it'll fall down a well. Don't even try to avoid wells... you could be in a bloody desert and THIS SWORD WOULD FALL DOWN A WELL. Got it?

58.descriptionId: This sword, soaked in a young Boowolf's tears, is said to bring luck and is supposed to fill warriors with courage on the battlefield. Ah, the naivety of terror.

60.descriptionId: This is an extremely well-forged sword, and will make you a worthy adversary. Your enemies will pant audibly when you enter the arena.

65.descriptionId: The sword Goultard was quenched in the blood of a Dragon Pig. The hero who can resist the sword's powerful stench will find himself climbing the social ladder very quickly indeed.

66.descriptionId: This sword captures the sights, the sounds and the smells of Badoul, the brave, bloodthirsty and above all punctual warrior who one day left his clan due to artistic differences.

67.descriptionId: Sharp and diabolical: these were the wide-eyed words of the succubus who fathered this deadly little minx. Minx? Fathered? Damn, that was the page about Vald's sister. Sorry about that.

68.descriptionId: This amulet increases the wearer's intelligence.

74.descriptionId: This amulet increases the wearer's Strength.

82.descriptionId: This amulet increases the wearer's Vitality.

89.descriptionId: This basic bow won't make a hero out of you, that's for sure.

95.descriptionId: This basic pair of daggers won't make a hero out of you, that's for sure.

101.descriptionId: This ring increases the wearer's Wisdom.

110.descriptionId: This ring increases the wearer's chance.

119.descriptionId: This ring increases the wearer's Agility.

127.descriptionId: These exceptional boots will grant you an extra Movement Point in combat. However, the smell of Bowisse's feet will quickly stop you in your tracks again if you accidentally bring them too close to your nose.

129.descriptionId: These boots are so comfortable that they instantly increase your concentration.

130.descriptionId: These boots are perfect for that special coup de grace.

132.descriptionId: This basic wand won't make a hero out of you, that's for sure.

138.descriptionId: This basic staff won't make a hero out of you, that's for sure.

145.descriptionId: This basic hammer won't make a hero out of you, that's for sure.

151.descriptionId: This basic shovel won't make a hero out of you, that's for sure.

156.descriptionId: This Power Belt will render you particularly powerful during fights but its weight will considerably decrease your Agility.

157.descriptionId: The Gougnole is made of a moon stone that was marinated for 5,000 years in a barrel of beer. This has inevitably endowed it with terrific powers.

158.descriptionId: The Golden Destiny will considerably increase your Vitality and Agility.

159.descriptionId: People say the famous blacksmith Boulgur made this brooch. Yes, the guy who created weapons for the gods.

160.descriptionId: This amulet, cast in a mixture of celestial eggs and milky stardust, must be kept refrigerated.

161.descriptionId: This powerful amulet will certainly make a name for you.

163.descriptionId: A well-carved wand, recommended for beginners.

180.descriptionId: This wand comes from the Syrastass Limbo. The legends say that it can make entire fields of daisies bloom, if asked politely by its bearer.

181.descriptionId: Helle from High in the Sky blessed this wand. It gives its bearer Agility and Vitality in combat.

183.descriptionId: A well-carved staff, recommended for beginners.

188.descriptionId: This staff increases Wisdom. It has one awkward side effect... I'm sure you can guess.

194.descriptionId: This staff increases Vitality and can be eaten if required.

200.descriptionId: The God Rod is a fearsome weapon. Warriors have been known to win battles in their sleep with the aid of this... fearsome weapon.

201.descriptionId: The Hook was found on a corpse, near a huge, decomposing Crocodyl.

202.descriptionId: This sword was blessed by the tears of the angel Raziel. Terribly destructive, it's powerful enough to help you fend off the most fearsome of enemies.

203.descriptionId: If you ever work out how to get this incredible item around your waist, you'll be one of the luckiest heroes in the universe. It used to belong to the strongest and most attractive of the bearded heroes of old.

204.descriptionId: This living staff roamed the darkest corners of Amakna for aeons. Now it sleeps deeply, only waking up every 300 years to move to a different place or to look for a different owner. It favours the stench of small, sweaty tunnels.

206.descriptionId: These well-forged daggers are recommended for beginners.

212.descriptionId: These well-forged daggers will make a worthy adversary of you.

218.descriptionId: Bashers are formidable daggers favoured by assassins who must dispatch the most bloodthirsty of warriors.

219.descriptionId: These Blessdags once belonged to the renowned Ogre 'Dark Hand' who died while fighting a Bimd'Oole paladin. Apparently, his blood animates their twisted blades.

220.descriptionId: The Chakra Style... a pair of daggers that once belonged to the greatest female thief of all time. Chakra was the first to open the doors of the Osaroth Temple and steal the precious relics hidden within.

222.descriptionId: A well-forged hammer, recommended for beginners.

228.descriptionId: This hammer increases its bearer's intelligence.

233.descriptionId: Kaiser was the name of the dastardly Dragon Pig who destroyed Bounkaïda Village many years ago. When the militia got the better of this monster, the smiths used his remains to make weapons. This hammer is one of them.

234.descriptionId: Ragnarok is powerful enough to raise a storm. It can also raise the temper of your friends if you don't know how to use it properly.

235.descriptionId: This hammer once belonged to the guardian of the Door of Hell. He prevented the living from coming in, the dead from going out and the living dead from urinating through the letterbox. Dirty monkeys!

236.descriptionId: Barabas is a fearsome weapon: it allows its wearer to move with stealth and ease and most importantly, to become even deadlier in close combat.

237.descriptionId: Sargasse once belonged to a child with fearsome powers. No one has seen it since it was reportedly traded for a bag of marbles.

239.descriptionId: A well-balanced shovel, recommended for beginners.

245.descriptionId: An extremely well-forged shovel, this tool will make a worthy adversary of you.

250.descriptionId: Halfway between an axe and a shovel, Axel was one of the seven weapons used by the demon Kajlir to overcome the Brotherhood of the Enutrofs, vicious adventurers searching for the Crimson Dofus.

251.descriptionId: Greybeard was the favourite weapon of the demon-dwarf Assan Cehef who terrorised countless villages with his surprise attacks.

253.descriptionId: This belt increases its wearer's Vitality, increasing their chances of surviving a fight.

257.descriptionId: This belt increases its wearer's Strength.

261.descriptionId: This belt increases its wearer's Agility.

267.descriptionId: The Disconcerting Bow is not new by any means, but it can be very useful.

270.descriptionId: Xaver is an efficient bow. It once belonged to the great baker Xavier. Between two batches, he used it to distribute bread to the monsters around his bakery.

271.descriptionId: This hammer is a beautiful, strange and fascinating weapon. Make sure you get nice and close to your enemy before you use it - that's the way Chafers like it, after all!

272.descriptionId: This bow is powerful enough to shoot an arrow to the moon.

273.descriptionId: The Yamato String has thrilled many a monster's heart. It's a fine weapon, able to send an arrow flying to the most oblique spots.

278.descriptionId: A ring set with a rare stone. Do I need to explain the name?

279.descriptionId: If we are to believe one renowned adventurer, this amulet contains a tear from a Gobball, which has the same properties and stench as Gobball Leather tea.

280.descriptionId: Collectors prize this necklace, you will certainly get a good price for it.

281.descriptionId:
This Api restores a few lost Health Points.
Placed on a friend's head, it makes an excellent target. The Api, we mean.

282.descriptionId: This flask restores some Health Points.

283.descriptionId: This flask restores some Health Points.

284.descriptionId: Grind this Salt to a powder and use it to add flavour to your bread.

285.descriptionId: This flour is obtained by grinding grains of wheat. It is an essential ingredient in the making of bread, pancakes, waffles and delicious cakes, but is mainly used for silly children's games.

286.descriptionId: Yeast is an essential ingredient for making bread rise.

287.descriptionId: Extremely rich in protein, this seed is a choice ingredient in the making of tasty bread, but the cultivation of sesame is rather delicate in the Amaknian climate. As a result, it is very rare and expensive.

288.descriptionId: This protein-rich seed gives a peculiar taste and smell to loaves of bread. The only way to find such a seed is to kill a Wild Sunflower... Well, you could always buy one too, I suppose.

289.descriptionId: Since the beginning of time, Wheat has been the staple food of Amakna's inhabitants and Tofus.

290.descriptionId: With or without cream, Mushrooms are very tasty. The easiest way to get some is to kill a Mush Mush.

291.descriptionId: These hairs are different from others. They have magical properties which make them extremely valuable to alchemists.

294.descriptionId: The only thing as solid as a Crackler is a Crackler, that's why this Crackler hunting shovel is made of Crackler Stone.

298.descriptionId: These sandals are made from the feathers of boiled Tofu and the sole from Tofu Beak, a very resistant material. Protracted wearing can render the wearer as daft as a Tofu.

299.descriptionId: Attack is the best defence. With these anti-aggression boots, you will easily send muggers packing. And those guys who come up to you at crossroads to clean your mount's teeth.

300.descriptionId: This seed imparts hallucinogenic properties to bread, ideal for a well-earned brain-holiday after a hard day's fighting.

301.descriptionId: Tofu Feathers are very magical things - just one kilo of them weighs as much as a kilo of steel!

303.descriptionId: Ash Wood is a low-quality wood but it is very common - it grows fast too.

305.descriptionId: They might be a bit worn from all that Cawwot-munching malarkey, but Wabbit Teeth are great for making potions thanks to their rejuvenating properties.

306.descriptionId: This flower loses its toxic properties when properly boiled and dried, and can be consumed in a herbal tea, but it is mainly used to entertain youths in search of romance. Indeed, who has never blown an Evil Dandelion Flower down the neck of a coveted lover? Such beautiful seeds, sweet as the touch of a shaft of sunlight on the dew-damp leaves of a charm tree. Perhaps Iops, who, instead of blowing, tend to suck the seeds and choke miserably in terrible convulsions.

307.descriptionId: These delicate wings have a very distinctive feature – anyone who dares to chew on them will gain spectacular powers of thought. They taste almost exactly like rotten kwak eggs, which is why they are mainly used in wisdom potions.

308.descriptionId: This white shell is nearly unbreakable, but if the best jewellers polish it for generations, they can use its magic properties to make amulets with exceptional powers.

309.descriptionId: These petals are a powerful aphrodisiac and so the ideal present to win over your beloved. Just one thing... it's better not to smoke them... It has the opposite effect.

310.descriptionId: This almost unbreakable bone becomes soft in contact with water, which makes things much easier for alchemists.

311.descriptionId: Water is useful for many things. Make sure it's stagnant and cloudy for maximum taste when brewing beer.

312.descriptionId: Iron is essential to blacksmiths and anyone else who works with metal. Some logical creatures even use it for ironing.

313.descriptionId: Gold is a rare and precious metal. Thanks to its intrinsic qualities, it is essential to the making of powerful and beautiful weapons.

315.descriptionId: Diamonds are a jeweller's best friend, but they require great skill to be worked properly. To find some, you often need to venture into dangerous mines. Good thing Diamonds are forever; you wouldn't want to be doing that twice a year!

316.descriptionId: Glowing vivid green, this magnificent jewel can easily transform a frog into a prince, no kissing required.

318.descriptionId: This staff used to be very handy for Amakna breeders who wanted to keep their flocks of Tabis in one place. It doesn't actually do much, but it is very light. Great for running after Gobballs.

323.descriptionId: This amulet gives the wearer special abilities: they will be possessed by a mysterious aura, which flows through their bodies and increases their physical abilities tenfold.

324.descriptionId: This amulet turns pink when you're feeling perky. Rumour has it that it also increases your chances of finding good items tenfold.

325.descriptionId: Handmade by one of the greatest Sram jewellers, this amulet is made of small skulls carved in bone, helping its wearer escape perilous situations.

326.descriptionId: The Deulegarnoulle Amulet comes from the Nordic regions... It'll increase your summoning powers.

327.descriptionId:
This blade was first forged for the Karne Riders, but it was unfortunately too heavy for those weak goblins. 
It's a very light weapon for normal beings, however, light enough to deliver rapid blows in succession.

328.descriptionId: This strange double-bladed sword was originally used to prune trees and cut through dense forests. The lumberjacks soon realised that it was also an excellent weapon against other creatures.

329.descriptionId: As its name indicates, this bow will help you on your path to consistent victory. A skilled Cra architect without an ounce of imagination later stole the same name for one of his monuments.

331.descriptionId: This is the bow of choice in the region. From what people say, you'll find treasure where its arrows fall. You have to make sure you fire them towards the end of a rainbow, but I still think it's crazy.

332.descriptionId: Joan was a little crazy, always hearing Tabis burping she said... They confiscated her bow - for her own good, mind you - and finally decided to burn her at the stake altogether. She burnt great, she did. Really something else... And I've seen a few burnings, me... I still have her singed kneecap if you want... come... hey! Where... ahhhh!

333.descriptionId: Originally made to be eaten, this baguette became a fearsome weapon when Xavier the Baker left it in the oven for 234 years. Why did he leave it for so long? Well, he reached a point where he'd had enough of making cheese sandwiches, and so he started handing out knuckle sandwiches to the monsters around the bakery instead. He had so much fun, he forgot all about the baguette.

334.descriptionId: This wand once belonged to Liriel, an Eniripsa who died of an overdose of strawberries, after losing his wings in a pain so excruciating that your heart would stop beating if I told you any more. Collectors are surprisingly desperate to get hold of this wand, given that it's said to be cursed.

335.descriptionId: Without their staff, the Bwork Magi are as harmless as Tofus. Need I say more about the power of this weapon?

336.descriptionId: This staff can levitate Cawwots! Mind you, that's not much use in fights.

337.descriptionId: The Bwork Archer Bow is extremely simple to use. It was designed with the Bwork Archers in mind... A bloody Tofu could use it... The catch is that you have to be as strong as a Crackler to string it.

339.descriptionId: This blade once belonged to Metzger the butcher, who used it to cut up bones. A Chafer managed to steal it from him and the blade became a fearsome weapon in his hands. Whole families of shoe salesmen went out of business, not to mention the glove trade... just terrible.

340.descriptionId: These daggers allow you to steal anything and everything, anything from everyone, or everything from anyone, or everyone from any...no that doesn't work... They're great, though.

341.descriptionId: These legendary daggers are a true collector's item for any self-respecting Sram. They are so revered that even some of these rats refuse to steal them.

342.descriptionId: This very special hammer was made of Kwak Beaks. That's why it's so prickly when it knocks you head over heels!

346.descriptionId: According to some legends, this ring protects against bad weather. In reality, this has never been proven because it has never rained in Amakna.

347.descriptionId: This shovel is a very efficient tool for cutting nutsedge, a type of weed. It's also an excellent weapon for taking care of the weeds you'll find in the inns of Amakna.

348.descriptionId: These boots once belonged to a cook who was always in a big rush. He spent his time criss-crossing the land of Amakna looking for celery-tea.

350.descriptionId: Silver is bright, pure and much-coveted by discerning jewellers. Contrary to the myth spread round by the unscrupulous Miners' Association, it has no particular effect on vampires. Unless they're miserly vampires... Or artistic vampires... Do vampires make jewellery? It doesn't... say... here... Anyway, if it's a really nasty vampire who's only out for blood, who has a good job... damn. Do vampires work?... Look, just sell the "bloody" thing or something.

351.descriptionId: This beer will give you back some of your precious Health Points. Let's not forget the old saying, though - 'Sometimes you drink your drink and sometimes your drink drinks you.'

354.descriptionId: This kind of sword is forged for the bodyguards of a renowned and wealthy shopkeeper. Its main use consists of frightening thieves but when murder is required - a tenacious burglar, a fussy customer - you'll find it equal to the task.

355.descriptionId: This ring increases Strength and Chance.

357.descriptionId: This sword symbolises a body part of which Ecaflips are particularly proud. If you don't feel it's hypocrisy to take it, be my guest.

358.descriptionId: The Infernal Tail is really... infernal. If you don't use it properly, it will drive your enemies and teammates completely crazy. Before long, you won't have any teammates left, just enemies. Nobody has ever been known to use it properly, so, well, you've been warned.

359.descriptionId: A long time ago, King Allister gave this ring to Isidor, a smart cat, renowned for his incomparable Agility.

360.descriptionId: Once boiled, these small, hairy, brown ears give off a smell of dead Boowolf. A true delight when stuffed with Royal Jelly.

361.descriptionId: It's the only food a Tiwabbit Wosungwee can eat, which is as good an excuse as any for its severe retardation.

362.descriptionId: This delightfully smooth skin is an excellent ingredient for magic potions.

363.descriptionId: This delightfully smooth skin is an excellent ingredient for magic potions.

364.descriptionId: This delightfully smooth skin is an excellent ingredient for magic potions.

365.descriptionId: In spite of its magical properties, this thin, hairy leg is in short supply - alchemists use it to pat their faces after shaving and never have enough left to sell... Like my mother always said... Don't get dry off your own supply.

367.descriptionId: This egg smells as if it's rotten the second it comes rolling out of the hen's behind. Imagine what it smells like when it is actually rotten.

368.descriptionId: Many greedy adventurers were dreadfully sick because of this delicious jelly. There's a saying that goes "everything is poison, nothing is poison, it's the dose that matters". In the case of Strawberry Jelly, avoid overdosing.

369.descriptionId: Many greedy adventurers were dreadfully sick because of this delicious Mint Jelly. Eaten in moderation, to ease your bad breath for example, it will have soothing properties on the morale of your troops.

370.descriptionId: This delicious jelly is the result of the digestion and fermentation of honey by a Royal Jelly. Inedible in its raw state, it's nevertheless an ingredient of choice for sweets.

376.descriptionId: This tiny, ridiculous wing is not very useful to the Evil Tofu... the only thing it does is blow hot air to knock Moskitos off balance.

377.descriptionId: This venomous thorn protects the Mush Mush in close combat, but, tragically, also means the creature cannot give hugs without killing the hugee. For more important matters, the Mush Mush uses Sporm to reproduce, firing it at his partner from far away.

378.descriptionId: This Sporm is the "precious seed" that allows the Mush Mush to scatter its angry mob wherever it wants, which is everywhere, basically. Be careful, however, as smelly feet and the smell of Bowisse's Boots attract the Sporms.

379.descriptionId: The Crab claw is like a deadly, unbreakable peacock feather... a great source of pride to its previous owner.

380.descriptionId: This is the staple food of Green Jelly, so if you smell mint, don't get the teacups out right away...

382.descriptionId: This dirty nail, which has been dragged about everywhere, was rescued from the streets. It's up to you to give the appendage a second chance.

383.descriptionId: Gobball Horns are as shiny and soft as freshly tanned leather. For some unknown reason, Osamodas love them.

385.descriptionId: This infection-ridden slobber smells so bad because Gobballs never stop licking their filthy wool, which also gives Gobballs atrociously bad breath. A vicious circle.

389.descriptionId: This oil is highly recommended by dieticians because of its high proportion of essential, unsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids...

390.descriptionId: Because of its fruity flavour and its low proportion of saturated fatty acids, Walnut Oil is essential in pastry-making and for flavouring cakes. It can be kept in a closed bottle for a few days only.

391.descriptionId: When harvested, unripe Cashew Nuts can be used to make oil. Once dried, they're also used as toys by simple-minded Iop children.

392.descriptionId: Walnuts can be used to make oil but it's better to consume them dried if you'd rather not suffer their laxative properties.

393.descriptionId: Boars all love Acorns and everyone everywhere wonders why this is. Hey... a haiku.

394.descriptionId: When smothered in chocolate, this little Hazelnut is delicious. It's just a shame chocolate's so expensive in Amakna.

395.descriptionId: This clover is a staple of the Tabi's diet. Nevertheless, breeders are wary of it because of the devastating flatulence it unleashes upon their livestock.

396.descriptionId: Thanks to its delicate taste and aroma, this oil is suitable for any kind of culinary challenge, from frying food to making French dressing.

397.descriptionId: This rare type of oil is what we call a mechanical elixir - it lubricates cogs and hinges so well that it only needs to be applied once. A guy by the name of Billy Wanka tried to make everlasting chewing gum with it once, but many, many children perished. Keep it for your hinges.

398.descriptionId: This strange fruit produces a refined oil when squeezed. What a pity you can't squeeze it because of its shell which is as hard as the sole of Bowisse's Boots.

399.descriptionId: Sesame Oil is obtained from Sesame Seeds and can be distinguished from the others by its rich and delicate taste... toasted Hazelnuts I would say. The only problem is that it smells like grilled Gobball.

400.descriptionId: If you stare for too long at a Barley plant, you'll begin to see minute flaws in its leaves and stem. Enraged by these imperfections, you'll write a letter to King Allister demanding that something be done about them, and not even a Consolation Candy will calm your ire.

401.descriptionId: The flower of the female Hop plant contains all of the active ingredients used in brewing, such as bitter resins and essential oils. The flower of the male Hop plant isn't useful for anything, other than scattering pollen all over the place.

405.descriptionId: The name given to germinated Barley, the most important ingredient in quality beer. Be careful with Malt, it has an enormous capacity for absorbing beer in its germination phase... just like Tot after a hard day hunting Tofus.

406.descriptionId: The main feature of this stomach is that it can easily distend. This greatly simplifies the Wo Wabbit's digestive problems caused by its excessive drinking of fermented Cawwot liquor.

407.descriptionId: There's nothing's better than a Prespic Peak for picking your teeth or creating a new arrowhead.

408.descriptionId: Elite Chafers' teeth are ruined by too much drinking, which is why they use dentures. These dentures cost a fortune because the teeth are made from gold and the foetid breath of Elite Chafers endows said gold with unpredictable powers.

409.descriptionId: For obscure reasons, these red hairs smell very bad when it's raining. The Bwork Magi take advantage of their magic powers nevertheless, which could be of interest to some alchemists.

414.descriptionId: A distinctive feature of this feather is that it is resistant to frost. That's why you never see an Ice Kwak shiver.

415.descriptionId: A distinctive feature of this feather is that it resists flames. That's why Fire Kwaks don't burn.

416.descriptionId: A distinctive feature of this feather is that it resists gusts of wind. That's why you never see Wind Kwaks get blown inside out like an umbrella.

417.descriptionId: The aggressive Mushd is composed of many pieces of mud put together. The only way to get the better of it is to dry it out, which is difficult considering just how moist it is.

419.descriptionId: These ears are pointed, rigid and covered with beautiful striped fur. It's unquestionably some exquisite fur, mainly because it's odourless.

420.descriptionId: With this very sturdy Flax String, you can choose to either make nice, solid seams or to bind your friends' hands and feet to show them who the real guild leader is.

421.descriptionId: The Flax Flower can either be blue or white, according to when the seed is sown. Sipped as an infusion, it endows an uncommon feeling of well-being.

422.descriptionId: This minute seed contains lots of goodness and plenty of flavour. Kwak hunters use these glistening seeds to lure the dozy creatures into traps.

423.descriptionId: There's nothing special about the Flax stem except that it is able to return to its original shape after bending up seven times. And so its fibre is equally flexible.

424.descriptionId: This is the fibre they use to make the finest of cloth... Being quite rare, this stuff is expensive, but always popular with the weavers.

425.descriptionId: The Hemp stem can be used for research into hallucinations but is also used in construction where it serves a very different purpose.

426.descriptionId: This fibre is more resistant than beautiful and can be smoked in your quiet moments of introspection.

427.descriptionId: Hemp Seeds are used to calm down herds of Tabis during the rutting season. All you need to do is toss these seeds on their grazing ground and they'll instantly become less savage.

428.descriptionId: This flower is used to make potions with random effects! These effects range from general paralysis to invulnerability to Wabbit flatulence, an old personal favourite.

429.descriptionId: This rusty arrowhead is made from a rare metal that is only found on these arrowheads.

431.descriptionId: This stone is almost alive, it draws life from the precious stones it contains. Nobody can break it except a Crackler. It'll make a great stone hammer.

432.descriptionId: Grilled Rib Chops are absolutely delicious, but there's not much meat on them.

433.descriptionId: This is a really strange bone... If you crumble it into dust, you can use it for curry powder. Seriously, just add water and hey presto... curry! I know a few unscrupulous chefs who'll be delighted to hear the news.

435.descriptionId: This piece of root has gained a lot of experience accompanying the Treechnid through the undergrowth. That still doesn't explain why it's magic.

436.descriptionId: This staff is carved out of a huge Treechnid Root, and its main use is in close combat. The only problem for the owner is that its roots regenerate when in contact with water... That includes rain, by the way.

437.descriptionId: During puberty, Treechnids are covered with ugly buds full of juicy sap and rich in vitamins. Later, these buds will give birth to new shoots which will give birth to buds.

440.descriptionId: This filthy claw is used to make fearsome weapons.

441.descriptionId: Copper is great for making cheap weapons... It could almost be a substitute for gold... Except it's soft, light, reacts with air and discolours quickly.

442.descriptionId: This metal is often used in the making of decorative items. It's ideal for beautifying your weapons on the cheap.

443.descriptionId: The name "Cobalt" means "Devil's Copper" in ancient Sadida. It's suited to the forging of light and stylish - but lethal - weapons.

444.descriptionId: Tin is a soft and heavy metal, a bit like the Wo Wabbit but worse.

445.descriptionId: Contrary to general opinion, this metal is not used to make gutters but terrifying weapons such as the "Manganesian Sharp"... This implement has bumped off more than a few Tofus at the Bulgur Festivals.

446.descriptionId: When properly tapered, this metal is much appreciated for its sharpness and unusual colour.

447.descriptionId: Coal has no particular magical properties, despite what you might think. However, it does attract lightning, stores it and, worst of all, always frees it at the worst possible time.

448.descriptionId: This sharp stone has cut the throat of more than one careless mole.

449.descriptionId: This wood owes its name to a misunderstanding... A family of lumberjacks living in this forest had a daughter named Bonnie. Bonnie was the only one who knew where to find a rather special type of tree and so this wood was named after her: "Bonnie Wood". Time and poor spelling finally produced the name "Ebony Wood".

450.descriptionId: This heavy mineral doesn't wear or bend, which limits its usefulness to blacksmiths. It is only in working it for a long period that you will manage to extract some precious stones from it.

454.descriptionId: This perfectly-forged axe is the perfect gift for lumberjacks who always blame their tools.

455.descriptionId: This ridiculously small hammer was used by Zokrim the peasant. Every day at dawn, he would work on his useless, meandering fences which still stretch all over his territory like confused spider webs.

456.descriptionId: This axe enables you to easily cut down trees, even the biggest ones. It is, above all, appreciated for its heavy weight which can cut a Bwork into three pieces. The only requirement is that you are strong enough to lift it!

458.descriptionId: Some say the Chafer is sensitive and distinguished, because his amulet carries the skulls of his dead cousins. Others say he's a beastly creature, because it was he who killed them.

459.descriptionId: A handyman could use this plank to make something delightful - a coffin, for example. Just bear that in mind.

460.descriptionId: This high-quality wood is particularly resistant. It's ideal for making things like bludgeons, houses or even boats. But its most vital use is for beer barrels.

461.descriptionId: The wood of the Yew Tree is very strong and flexible. Consistently voted wood of the year by the bow makers of the region, it's also rather difficult to find - the peasants of Amakna destroy any shoots they see because they're poisonous to Gobballs.

462.descriptionId: Though you can kill the Treechnids, their wood never truly dies... this makes it incredibly difficult to work. All the same, killing a Treechnid with an arrow made of the root of one of its brothers will really hit hard, and if they don't die, you can be sure it'll ruin their lives forever! Good show!

463.descriptionId: This magnificent precious stone is made of fossilised tree resin. You can sometimes find a little Moskito inside, trapped for aeons in the sticky sap, which makes the stone even more valuable.

465.descriptionId: Crystal is translucent and beautiful, but extremely brittle. Such is life, nothing is perfect even with precious stones.

466.descriptionId: This precious blue stone is well-adapted to the making of magical weapons, possibly because lazy script writers always use blue to represent mana.

467.descriptionId: The shimmering glow of this precious stone makes it as bright as the Fire Kwak's feathers, but its surface is as cold to the touch as the Ice Kwak's snowballs.

468.descriptionId: Soft of texture, golden of crust and hot out of the oven, this small loaf will increase your Health Points. It's the most popular type of bread and usually the cheapest.

469.descriptionId: This wand makes use of the magic properties of the Treechnid Root. Beware of the side effects of this living wand, it can sometimes turn against its owner.

470.descriptionId: Once a common type of wood, Elm is now much sought-after. A long time ago, a terrible bewitchment called Grafioze was cast by a powerful Bwork Magus of the worst kind, decimating whole forests of it.

471.descriptionId: Maple leaves are well-known for having inspired people of limited imagination to create a flag, and the syrup adds taste to pancakes. As for Maple Wood, we still don't know what to do with it.

472.descriptionId: This wood is affectionately known by lumberjacks as "Hornbeam Wood" because of the tree it comes from. Perhaps if they knew what Sadidas did underneath these trees in the dead of night, they wouldn't be so eager to search them out.

473.descriptionId: The smell of Chestnut Wood sends flies packing. Well, not so much the flies who like Chestnuts... or flies who don't have much of a sense of smell... When you think about it, that probably covers most flies.

474.descriptionId: This type of wood is appreciated in the cabinet-making trade because of its dense texture and the brown-reddish colour it acquires with time.

476.descriptionId: Walnut Wood is often used in the making of furniture.

478.descriptionId: This axe has Woodee the Lumberjane to thank for its name... She knew how to turn on the charm and divert the lumberjacks' attention, running in and stealing all the best trees for herself while they scurried off to pay ridiculous prices for rosebuds, sugarcane and those little snow globes that you shake... as soppy as wells they were.

479.descriptionId: Ivory is always in great demand because of its legendary whiteness. Smiths use the stuff when forging lethal weapons. Collectors value it just as highly. You'll have no problem selling this in Amakna.

482.descriptionId: An Enutrof builder who'd had a few drinks too many at the tavern realised one night that this shovel could do more than dig holes in the ground.

485.descriptionId: When winter comes, the Chafer Lancer never leaves home without his leather briefs... they keep his joints warm and distract his enemies if needs be.

486.descriptionId: This leather is particularly resistant, but smells like a male Boar in rut. That explains why local farmers use it to trap female Boars, who are too stupid to see past such a devious ruse.

487.descriptionId: The Dragon Pig was so keen to transform into a Dragon that he burnt all the stubbly hair from his skin, which partly explains why this leather smells so strongly of pork scratchings.

489.descriptionId: With this Magnifying Glass, you'll be able to analyse the elements of your surroundings. Treasures will be yours!

492.descriptionId: An essential tool for the baker-confectioner profession.

497.descriptionId: An essential tool for collecting ore.

501.descriptionId: This syrupy sap has been tampered with by a renowned alchemist who wanted to liven up Treechnid Roots. I don't need to tell you that you'll have to be careful with this stuff.

502.descriptionId: This axe is the only tool that can cut down enchanted trees. It's the silver bullet of axes.

515.descriptionId: This axe once belonged to the renowned lumberjack, Brouce Boulgoure. He used to be married to Kassiopee Baine, another great lumberjack's daughter. Many's the time this weapon protected him when he was alone in the forest.

519.descriptionId: This powder is made of Flax and Bread. Neither of these ingredients explain its magical properties.

520.descriptionId: This bread is tricky to make since breathing in the fumes from baking typically causes the baker to lose their sense of smell.

521.descriptionId: The most daring Kwaks often dress up as bakers to steal Sesame Seeds. After a long process of costly mistakes, the Kwaks now know to only try such reckless tricks on Iop bakers.

522.descriptionId: This bread is rich in protein but completely tasteless. That's just the way it is - you can't have your bread and eat it too, as the bakers say.

524.descriptionId: This bread, cooked to golden perfection with a delicate flour contains no colourings or preservatives, unlike the Royal Jelly.

526.descriptionId: This multi-cereal bread contains enough fibre to give a dead man the runs.

527.descriptionId: First, Walnuts are toasted and put into the soft centre. Then, the bread is cooked over Walnut Wood.

528.descriptionId: This bread is a quality product for the discerning palate.

529.descriptionId: This flour is milled from Barley grains. It gives a certain lightness to the centre of the bread which has no equal in the land, unless you use occult magic in your bakery.

530.descriptionId: This flour retains all the characteristics of Rye. According to the legend, Rye that sprouts at dawn never ripens. In a typically peasant-style leap of logic, many farmers procreate at dawn in the hope that their future children will never grow old.

531.descriptionId: This flour doesn't rise during baking, which makes for a very dense bread, ideal for when you have to sock a monster on the loaf.

532.descriptionId: This dark cereal can grow under the worst of conditions, it's one of the rare cereals capable of surviving long periods of drought.

533.descriptionId: This type of cereal is used to feed the young Tabis, whose teeth are not sufficiently developed for hard foods. The peasants nevertheless dished it out with a fearful moderation, being well aware of the eye-watering damage wrought by a fibre-fed intestinal tract.

534.descriptionId: This white flour is made by grinding sprouted grains of Barley, which gives a slightly acidic taste to the bread, or, at best, a taste of stale beer. It's great for breakfast on a Sunday morning.

535.descriptionId: This flour lends a delicious beer-like taste to the bread, without having to waste any beer in the process. What a skilled bunch these bakers are, don't you think?

536.descriptionId: This bread, light and soft in the centre, is ideal for people that Single Mother Nature has endowed with a tiny stomach...

537.descriptionId: Generally speaking, when you come across a spud, it means that you either are in the middle of a field or in the depths of a dungeon.

538.descriptionId: These potatoes are peeled, which makes them even more sumptuous.

539.descriptionId: This bread is prepared with Rye Flour, which lends a brown colour to the centre and a delicious, sugary flavour.

543.descriptionId: When properly polished, this stone can make a magnificent Diamond.

544.descriptionId: When properly polished, this stone can make a magnificent Emerald.

545.descriptionId: When properly polished, this stone can make a magnificent Crystal.

546.descriptionId: When properly polished, this stone can make a magnificent Sapphire.

547.descriptionId: When properly polished, this stone can make a magnificent Ruby.

548.descriptionId: This potion will take you back to your last save point.

578.descriptionId: Thou shalt not cast the first stone.

580.descriptionId: You'll recover between 101 and 200 energy points using this potion.

582.descriptionId: You need several cereals to make this flour, which is much appreciated for its quality. You wouldn't think to look at it, would you?

583.descriptionId: This off-white flour takes its name from the peasant woman who discovered it. She enjoyed slapping the men of the village on the backside with her hands covered in flour, the minx.

586.descriptionId: Shika Ingalsse got the idea for this immensely popular flour while knocking Brouce Boulgoure's pets around with sacks of inferior milled cereal. Don't worry, outrage ensued.

587.descriptionId: This flour is a mixture of several types of cereal, which makes it a particularly rich ingredient.

592.descriptionId: This bow once belonged to Ivan Nowe, a foolhardy Cra who had a cruel habit of attacking stray Tofus. This bow first puzzles the enemy before efficiently killing them.

593.descriptionId: This flower is as rare as it is beautiful. It's not surprising when you know that the rampant toads of the region use them to feed their offspring.

594.descriptionId: This flower is beautiful but very rare. It's no surprise - its magic is so powerful that it can even bring people back to life.

596.descriptionId: This small fishing rod is perfect for catching small fish in ponds.

597.descriptionId: Extremely resistant, this net enables you to capture the wildest of mounts, provided you first succeeded to hypnotize or distract it.

598.descriptionId: Grawns are appreciated for their delicate taste and bright pink colour. On the other hand, they are hated for their legendary bad temper and their gomina-style antennae.

600.descriptionId: The Kralove may not look like much, but don't be fooled - behind its sad eyes, a fearsome predator crouches, ready to pounce on an intruding stranger.

602.descriptionId: This red shark is an activist with a strong herd instincts - there is no sense of the individual in their group even if their chief, Stakemoff, is idolised as a hero.

603.descriptionId: The Kittenfish has two unusual characteristics - it has whiskers and it purrs underwater to frighten flying fish.

607.descriptionId: The Muddy Trout is somehow related to the aggressive Salmoon of Moon Island. This trout is delicious both raw and cooked...

610.descriptionId: This delicate but original whitish amulet is made of Crab.

616.descriptionId: This amulet, set with fish scales, is supposed to bring its wearer good luck when he puts out to sea on stormy nights.

617.descriptionId: Many sailors have been impressed by this terrifying amulet. All you have to do is put it on and you'll be a feared warrior.

619.descriptionId: This staff allowed Paile Ingalsse, breeder of Gobballs, to summon the Tofus that kept his flocks safe. After a tragic accident, he discovered that it was also a fierce weapon.

620.descriptionId: Thanks to this sword, the celebrated sailor Mobby Diquerivurs sliced the tentacles off the equally famous Giant Kralove of Moon Island, much feared for his habit of smothering drunken sailors.

629.descriptionId: This delightful hat will make your adventurer the belle of the ball... the masked ball, that is (ha ha ha)!

638.descriptionId: Fishing a Somoon is quite a miracle but don't worry, with this amulet around your neck, there's no such word as "can't".

639.descriptionId: This Amulet of the Depths was found in the submerged shipwreck of the renowned Kralove fisherman, Tom Fawyer, also famous for his lousy jokes at the pirates' bar.

640.descriptionId: Fishermen used this bow to clean the vermin off the coastlines of Amakna... The cowards usually committed the pesticide from the windows of the local bars.

641.descriptionId: This cotton is as soft as the belly fur of a young female Ecaflip, as white as a spring cloud and as delicate as a Tofu feather.

643.descriptionId: The delicacy and suppleness of this string is hard to beat. Silk is the fabric favoured by the Chafers for their fighting underwear.

646.descriptionId: This black hair doesn't show the dirt. This is an advantage that will interest the kind of hero who thinks that a brisk walk through the rain is as good as a bath. They melt when they touch sweat, though.

657.descriptionId: This staff allowed Shika Ingalsse, leader of Gobballs, to summon the Tofus that kept her flocks safe. After a tragic accident, she discovered that it was also a fierce weapon.

658.descriptionId: This staff allowed Gramine Ingalsse, leader of Gobballs, to summon the Tofus that kept his flocks safe. After a tragic accident, he discovered that it was also a fierce weapon.

666.descriptionId: Originally synonymous with culinary failure, this dish is given when it becomes apparent that an error has been made, regardless of its origin.

674.descriptionId: "There's nothing wrong with this axe... Seriously, nothing. Really." The wise words of Brouce Boulgoure, lumberjack extraordinaire. Its Cherry Wood shaft cushions vibrations when you're cutting trees down or splitting Bworks' skulls.

675.descriptionId: This axe doesn't look special, but it gets the job done. Brouce Boulgoure the lumberjack won the Bwork Dwarf tree-cutting championship with this modest tool - that's saying something.

676.descriptionId: This axe's special feature is that it never gets rusty, so don't be surprised when hungry lumberjacks start licking the sweet tree sap from its blade.

677.descriptionId: This cloak once belonged to Zokrim, an old pirate. He must have been rather unlucky.

690.descriptionId: This flour is very strange. It's not made of grain, which explains why it doesn't look like flour. It also explains why it doesn't taste, smell or behave like flour.

692.descriptionId: Made with Flax Flour, this bread is fatty with a brown centre. Although rich in essential oils, it tastes awful.

694.descriptionId: Ignemikahl the Fire Dragon created the Crimson Dofus. I would tell you that it stinks of sulphur... but it stinks of so many other things too.

696.descriptionId: Besides its has-been look, the Slob Headgear is great for those high-noon duels... keeps some sun out of your eyes.

698.descriptionId: The Sortingat Hogwat comes from a famous School of Magic. This lively creature has met the greatest wizards of our time, like Mrs Magoa AlaGale, Mr Doublegore and the renowned Misk'arry Rotter.

699.descriptionId: The Troma is as shady as an eraserhead made of Bherb hairs, and that's saying something (if you don't know what an eraserhead made of Bherb hairs looks like, refer to the great books of the Hen Pens).

701.descriptionId: The Oiram has many fans throughout the World who just love its classy look. This hat once belonged to a plumber who spent his days cleaning pipes. He was quite stylish himself.

702.descriptionId: This demon skull, constructed from various bones, gives its bearer a graceful and elegant look. Even your lover will be sick with envy.

703.descriptionId: This magical hat, which looks like an upside-down wicker fruit basket, is in fact... a magical upside-down fruit basket hat. It will certainly impress the neighbours, especially if they are Bwork Magus apprentices.

704.descriptionId: With this hat made from Chafer leather briefs, the female Bwork Magi won't be able to resist you. That's not a good thing, mind - many are known to wear long, red beards and none are known for their femininity.

705.descriptionId: If what you're looking for is a bit of trauma, you'll find great relief in this magnificent coconut. We remind you that a free straw and many a mouthful of fresh coconut-flavoured goodness are waiting for you inside.

706.descriptionId: Hung 'Short Memory' Lekahurse owned a magnificent crystal ball - his grandpa gave it to him. He wisely decided to hold on to it for the rest of his life. In fact, he put it on his hat which he never took off again, until one day, a jealous breeze took it away. He followed, and the breeze seemed to mock him, suspending the hat in the air, and whipping it away just as his searching fist approached. Not without a sense of decency, the wind took him home for a brief visit once a season and when it sensed the poor man was close to the end, took him to the edge of a cliff, hung the hat there for a moment and down Lekahurse tumbled, at peace at last.

707.descriptionId: With this Minotoror Horn hat, you'll have no problem passing yourself off as a Minotoror if your confidence in your own powers is failing. This trickery only works on simple-minded creatures such as Iops and Tofus.

708.descriptionId: This hat gives whoever wears it a jolly appearance... jolly but incredibly stupid. In life, you can't have it all – as the wearer of this hat clearly demonstrates.

709.descriptionId: This hat once belonged to Lorko, a lumberjack. He challenged the famous Brouce Boulgoure to an elm-uprooting duel in Liroye Merline's clearing.

710.descriptionId: The Korko Klako is a beautifo hato worno by the mo handso Sadido.

711.descriptionId: This magnificent leather mask once belonged to Jouik Krampe, cousin of Zeurg. They were both fond of tight leather clothes. A bit like Captain Chafer, only not as depraved.

712.descriptionId: This hat is so original that you will soon think you're fantastic, unique and on top of the World. It is said that in bygone days, Rakmar Bilgout used it to charm the queen of the Gobballs. He didn't hesitate to cut her throat open afterwards... Nothing to do with the hat I hope.

718.descriptionId:
(Double-tap to learn the spell.)
This scroll will teach you the Leek Pie elementary spell.

719.descriptionId:
(Double-tap to learn the spell.)
This scroll will teach you the Release elementary spell.

720.descriptionId:
(Double-tap to learn the spell.)
This scroll will teach you the Lightning Strike elementary spell.

721.descriptionId:
(Double-tap to learn the spell.)
This scroll will teach you the Summoning of Arachnee spell.

731.descriptionId:
(Double-click to learn the spell)
This scroll will teach Iops the class spell Brokle.

732.descriptionId: This magnificent wedding ring was stolen from Silimelle, a female brewer, during a boozy meal at the inn. See what happens when you accept drinks from strangers?

733.descriptionId: Without any doubt, Ragalde was one of the most foolhardy Iop warriors. With these magic boots, he slew a great number of enemies.

734.descriptionId: This belt is the weapon of choice for crowd control in Amakna prison and at the annual town fair.

737.descriptionId: Greener than a sick Tofu, the Emerald Dofus was created by Aerafal, the Air Dragon. To have created such a green thing, he must certainly have been feeling airsick. That bodes well for its powers, doesn't it?

739.descriptionId: The Turquoise Dofus was created by Aguabrial, the Water Dragon. Isn't it incredible what a Dragon can do with some water?

742.descriptionId: "I am the eggman, I am the Dofus. Waka fu ku." The last words recorded by the renowned axe smith-cum-minstrel, Jon Lemon. Soon after, he was crushed by a giant Tofu egg.

743.descriptionId: The recipe for this brioche was standardised by Xavier the Baker himself. He wanted to make a delicious and light brioche. It's more than he could have hoped for...

744.descriptionId: This cloak is an often underestimated one-of-a-kind. It is made of Green Larva Skin, giving it a most pleasant, rugged appearance.

745.descriptionId: This ingot is made of solid Gold.

746.descriptionId: This rare alloy is used in the making of rare and often lethal items. It is a too-little-known fact that Ebonite, once it has rusted, becomes a dangerous poison.

747.descriptionId: This alloy is incredibly light and is consequently a choice metal for small daggers or short swords.

748.descriptionId: This eccentric alloy is almost magical; it glitters and vibrates at night time, which is enough to frighten a slightly gullible Bwork.

749.descriptionId: Bakelelite is not a solid alloy but correctly sharpened, it becomes as sharp as a Chafer's blade.

750.descriptionId: This strange alloy contains an impressive energy which makes it quite unstable under certain circumstances. The best smiths are mad about Kouartz and use it to create weapons with almost legendary powers.

752.descriptionId: This blood is magic and is an essential ingredient of magic black puddings. The side effects remain unknown.

754.descriptionId: Marinated in pure blood for many long years, this cloak has acquired a ruby red colour that is very pleasing to the eye. This cloak is much favoured during the Al Howin's Day celebrations.

756.descriptionId: In order to avoid being hit in the spots where it hurts, the Vampire sometimes puts on his leather briefs when he goes hunting. The briefs also provide good protection against sunburn.

757.descriptionId: This jelly is especially sticky, like an enraged Sadida's Block. Strangely, it sticks Tofu Feathers together particularly well. You have to wonder what else it could be used for.

758.descriptionId: This cloak can only be worn by the great dispensers of justice... It's not very popular.

759.descriptionId: This magnificent cloak was made with the feathers of the very last Cheeken of Amakna. It's a real rarity that collectors dream of hanging on their living room wall.

760.descriptionId: A Kwaker Vans prototype. Its flavour and quality are surprising, but so is the smell, unfortunately. You'll never get used to it.

761.descriptionId: These Mouse Hairs are very thin and soft - a much sought-after resource in the making of expensive coats for the mistresses of rich Amaknian bankers.

764.descriptionId: This small amulet will delight inexperienced adventurers.

765.descriptionId: This scythe once belonged to Farle Ingalsse himself. It is sharp enough to mow any kind of cereal and any kind of monsters hidden in cereal fields.

766.descriptionId: This amulet increases the damage of inexperienced adventurers.

767.descriptionId: Don't mind its stuck-up name, this ring can only make your hero stronger. Okay, his chin will shrink too, but hey, who cares!

768.descriptionId: This ring influences your fate. You'll be tougher but less lucky. In other words, you improve your chances of living a long time and ruin your chances of living happily.

769.descriptionId: These boots bring good fortune. Unfortunately, they decrease your resistance.

770.descriptionId: This magnificent pair of boots will make you more agile, but they won't help you think.

772.descriptionId: According to what people say, this legendary cloak makes you almost invisible when combined with the fencers' legendary sword, the Dart Onion, and to the legendary hat of the Six Rams of the Rahk Shepherds.

773.descriptionId: This light cloak comes from the Patitalian Country, a place where people communicate with their limbs. This explains the incredible lightness and complete freedom of movement given by the cloak.

774.descriptionId: Coming from the Mount Taigue, this cape ended up poisoning its former female owner... Strangely enough, if you wear it, it will increase your resistance.

775.descriptionId: This cape has been made with infinite care and attention, it allows the wearer to find the enemy's weak point.

776.descriptionId: A certain Mulba used this item to carry half her kitchen with her on a long, difficult quest to find the Seven Crystal Hens which fell from the stars. This cloak will make you strong and brave.

777.descriptionId: The battery cock whose feathers made this cape fought its killers for several days and nights before finally dying of exhaustion. Let me tell you, killing that crazy chicken nearly finished them off too.

778.descriptionId: This authentic bad guy cloak proves you belong to the gang of the diabolic Mori Arty. It is said that his bad luck equalled his astounding intelligence. Only true bad guys can wear it.

779.descriptionId: This cloak looks ordinary... but isn't. It can make its wearer invisible to the eyes of those who are not looking at him. Really impressive!

781.descriptionId: This superb cloak once belonged to the Great Stratequerre. This renowned and expert strategist lord of war, hungry for the universe conquest, soon gave up his plans after having arrayed himself in the cloak. Really strange!

782.descriptionId: This very special axe was originally designed to teach budding lumberjacks the art of chopping. When it is well used, it can split a young carefree Treechnid in two, provided that such a Treechnid exists.

783.descriptionId: This amulet, made exclusively of precious wood, is highly prized and loved by lumberjacks who usually exaggerate its abilities to offset the cost of the material.

784.descriptionId: Mulish Cat was a renowned Ecaflip, and the most stupid in his class. In combat, the only match for his nonexistent intelligence was his bewildering luck.

785.descriptionId: The tradition of passing this ring down from grandfather to grandson gives it incredible power. This one is but a pale imitation of the original, but even so, it is much sought-after by collectors, whether they are Enutrof or not.

786.descriptionId: The jeweller's hand slipped while shaping this amulet, which imparts more intelligence to the wearer but in exchange, imparts a tear-inducing migraine, making it almost impossible to see anything.

787.descriptionId: This strange little ring can increase the Agility of the wearer in exchange for Chance points.

789.descriptionId: This belt is all the rage among young Amaknians. A follower of Sadida, couturier by trade, is behind this fashion. When he sold it for the first time, he said: "Life is short, play hard!"

790.descriptionId: The magic effects of this cape are often overestimated, which inevitably causes heavy losses in adventurers, such as the notorious minstrel Jon Lemon.

791.descriptionId: This is a staff made of living Treechnid Roots. But watch out... it has a tendency to turn on its master. When it does decide to attack the same target as you, it can be very deadly.

792.descriptionId: This syrupy sap is useless unless you are prepared to wait for it to harden and eventually turn into Amber. People say that a shrewd and particularly attractive Enutrof has found a way to speed up this process.

793.descriptionId: This potion speeds up some chemical processes, like the formation of precipitates. It's just like a very powerful yeast, without the musty taste.
