6963.descriptionId: These incredibly big balls are delicious. You'll think there's no end to them, but isn't that a good thing?

6964.descriptionId: This rice-based potion enables Brakmarians to return to their hometown instantaneously. Thankfully, Bontarians can't use it.

6965.descriptionId: This rice-based potion enables Bontarians to return to their hometown instantaneously. Thankfully, Brakmarians can't use it.

6966.descriptionId:
(Double-click to learn the spell)
This scroll will teach Srams the class spell Jinx.

6978.descriptionId: From a distance, this creature looks just like a bow wow. A simple glance at its face and you can see it has been through some terrible trials, which have convinced it to become a vegetarian. Thus, it will only eat vegetables and plants that grow on Pandala. Obsessed with the Goroku, this creature has stuck to you like glue ever since it smelled the seeds you're carrying.

6980.descriptionId: This Dofus was laid by a dragon that decided to remain anonymous. The wisest adventurers still wonder why.

6981.descriptionId: The blade of these daggers is made of ice. Reminds me of an old incident that had the detectives working overtime... A fella called Tum Sellick stabbed his buddy with one of these things over a couple of kamas... Nice crime... They found the novelty ice-cube maker in his house though... NICKED!

6982.descriptionId: These daggers are soaked in the blood of various evil creatures, such as children. They are very special.

6983.descriptionId: Only sharpened once every ten years, these daggers retain their lethal edge because of the dark magic that possesses them. They can sometimes be seen walking the streets at the weekend, playing loud music and staring threateningly at passersby.

6984.descriptionId: These daggers belonged to a Sadida whose dazzling ascent will be remembered forever in Amaknian history. From a young age, this Sadida dedicated his humble life to Gobbly hunting... the villagers found it hilarious... word spread and soon folk came from all around to watch him hunt those ridiculous balls of wool. His revenge was terrible and long-lived. When the price of Gobbly skins skyrocketed, he became so rich that he paid to have every last villager who mocked him hunted down and murdered. He's storing their skins too, but the stock market isn't going his way.

6987.nameId: Risky Soul Stone for Small Souls
6987.descriptionId: You'll have a limited chance of capturing level 50 souls using this soul stone.

6988.descriptionId: The sister of a wild Xelor who was kidnapped by unscrupulous slave drivers used to wear this thing for her nightly shows, the nature of which I will not repeat here.

6989.descriptionId: This hat was made a long time ago by apprentice tailors who wanted to protect themselves from the violent fits of rage of Mirko, their boss. This fine business man was often forced to kick his apprentices in the head when they didn't work fast enough. From what I've heard, that was far too good for the lazy bast.

6990.descriptionId: This hat is a tribute to the distant cousins of the Moskitos: the Moths. A lot bigger and a lot kinder than the Moskitos, the Moths took such good care of their livestock that they soon became extinct from self-inflicted famine. From this tragic story, we have the common insult 'Moth' as in, 'Poor bloody Moth', which describes a fellow who discovers his spouse is devastatingly gluttonous.

6991.descriptionId: This strange-looking hat looks like a big dehydrated rotting fruit... A bit like you after a night out at the pub.

6992.descriptionId: An improved version of the famous Kanniball Mask, the Kannipiwi will make you look like a real Piwi hunter to your friends.

6993.descriptionId: Lonard Kohen, the famous minstrel with the voice of a castrated Crackler (which is still incredibly low) was burnt alive in front of the bank of Bonta after causing a moral scandal with his latest, and last, song "Tower of Thong". A full recording was made of his cries of agony, which he had the vision to frame in C#m, modulate to Fb, and resolve in a risqué but manageable G#. Nice.

6994.descriptionId: This hood-cloak hybrid is just amazing. If it were made of leather, Captain Chafer would have loved it.

6995.descriptionId: You just can't stay inside this cape; it'll throw you out whether you want to go or not.

6996.descriptionId: Stradamus was an old drunken Enutrof who could read the future in pints of beer. Legend has it he was buried standing up in a wall of the Brakmar inn upon his own request, "so that no drunkard can ever spill his beer over my grave". This has been told at least once a week by every drunk in every inn in Brakmar.

6997.descriptionId: The woman who created this ring was convinced the end of the World was near due to plummeting food supplies. She used to spend entire days engraving messages on wooden tables with her motto 'No steak but what we bake'. Time proved her wrong.

6998.descriptionId: This small wedding ring will fit an Eniripsa's little fingers perfectly. For Iops, however, it's almost unusable. Their fingers are too fat and they can't get it into their heads that it's not a bracelet.

6999.descriptionId: Lahilama was a great spiritual guide who kept his temple right in the heart of the mountains. He was so bored that he spent his days sewing little yellow hats for his disciples. They just had nothing to talk about. They all slowly went mad years of awkward conversation.

7000.descriptionId: This ridiculous little piece of bamboo has got strange magical powers. It used to be carried by young Pandawas, once they'd been through puberty. You might want to wait a while before you start wearing it round your neck...

7001.descriptionId: "I, I am the kheeng, you, you are the quheen, whee can be heeroes just for one daaaayyyy..." Davyd, the famous minstrel, was singing his head off on his way back from Moon Island.

7002.descriptionId: This amulet of Bamboo resin will spread a nice smell all around you. It comes in handy when you're practising your Wind of Panic.

7003.descriptionId: This Talisman was created with stardust and precious stones, encased in Ancestral Treechnid Amber. The mixture can be quite explosive, so it is not recommended you try to make it yourself. Leave it to a jeweller you don't like.

7004.nameId: Risky Soul Stone for Average Souls
7004.descriptionId: You'll have a limited chance of capturing level 100 souls using this soul stone.

7005.nameId: Risky Soul Stone for Big Souls
7005.descriptionId: You'll have a limited chance of capturing level 150 souls using this soul stone.

7006.nameId: Risky Soul Stone for Huge Souls
7006.descriptionId: You'll have a limited chance of capturing level 200 souls using this soul stone.

7007.nameId: Regular Soul Stone for Small Souls
7007.descriptionId: You'll have an even chance of capturing level 50 souls using this soul stone.

7008.nameId: Regular Soul Stone for Average Souls
7008.descriptionId: You'll have an even chance of capturing level 100 souls using this soul stone.

7009.nameId: Regular Soul Stone for Big Souls
7009.descriptionId: You'll have an even chance of capturing level 150 souls using this soul stone.

7010.descriptionId: This soul stone contains the souls of a group of monsters whose only wish is to come back to life to tear your body to pieces. It can only be used in special arenas, located in big cities.

7011.descriptionId: This cloak is made of red beard hair... it is quite unique. Animated by extraordinarily powerful magic that renders it all but living, it adores playing practical jokes on the unfortunate bugger who puts it on. It's favourite trick? It unfindably conceals itself when it senses you need it most. If you do ever manage to discipline it, it can be very powerful in fights. As the Wabbits like to say it's a "weal good instwument of wawfawe".

7012.descriptionId: This amulet is, in fact, a candy. It might have been edible if it hadn't been carefully rolled under female Bworker armpits for 36 generations as part of some bizarre ritual.

7013.descriptionId: Unlike reed, bamboo can break when bent. Most of the time, it's the teeth of a careless adventurer that will break first. These bloody dentists even have nature on their side... I tell you.

7014.descriptionId: You wouldn't think to look at it, but this wood is sacred. Normally, only the finest Pandawas can get their hands on a piece but sometimes, sometimes, lumberjack tourists take a little souvenir of their trip to Pandala island. Bloody tourists.

7015.descriptionId: Being completely tasteless, these bamboo shoots are not a popular foodstuff. You should cut them down with a well-rusted scythe and marinate them for a couple years in Greedovore juice before you serve them up to your friends. Another tip from unscrupulous restaurateurs willing to feed you anything at all.

7016.descriptionId: Walloh, a young Pandawa, once asked his father, "What's the difference between Bamboo and Dark Bamboo, Daddy?" His dad slapped him in the face for asking such a stupid question. Everyone knows that the difference between Bamboo and Dark Bamboo is the size of their seeds.

7017.descriptionId: Walloh, a young Pandawa, once asked his father, "What's the difference between Bamboo and Golden Bamboo, Daddy?" His dad smacked him for asking such a stupid question. Everyone knows that the difference between Bamboo and Golden Bamboo is the size of their roots.

7018.descriptionId: Either sticky or slimy, rice is a long-time favourite with young, starving Pandawas.

7020.descriptionId: Some say it's the oldest known flower. It symbolises fertility as well as detachment since it can submerge itself in water without getting wet. Some Pandawa Chiefs use this symbol to make their followers understand they have to live their life in the World without falling under its influence.

7022.descriptionId: This Staff belonged to Sangroku's grandfather, Sangrokrane, famous for his big head. Legend says this magic staff has the ability to stretch to any length desired... use it to flatten your enemies or stick it down your pants, you're always a winner with this thing.

7023.descriptionId: This stone is usually found around Pandala Island. Pandawas are convinced it has special powers. Just like the rumours about Iops and their hidden intelligence, no one has proven this myth.

7024.descriptionId: Batches of this weird-looking stone were once used to feed the young Crackrocks of Pandala breeders. Believe it or not, the stones are now endangered, so this practice has been discontinued.

7025.descriptionId: This stone has been named after a Pandala river in which great quantities of it used to be found. But times have changed and the intensive exploitation of the past now means it is difficult to find.

7026.descriptionId: This precious, slightly blue, transparent stone is so bright that it can hide the most ravine-like wrinkles when worn as a necklace. Pandawas even tell tourists: "With this stone, keep your man happy and watch with pity the ravages of time misshape your loved ones." A nice way to kill two birds with one stone!

7027.descriptionId: For some dubious reasons, Topaz is still the most popular jewel among jewellers. It attracts quite a lot of Crobaks in the Cania Plains.

7028.descriptionId: This stone has been named after a very famous female Pandawa: Agathe Pahtes. She could be found in places of debauchery such as the Sufokia Pirates' Pub, where she spent her last years dancing, chained up to a big mast in the middle of the pub.

7029.descriptionId: Sangroku ate way too many magic beans one time. Forever more, it was a constant struggle to restrain the winds of panic that erupted from his britches without the slightest warning... Those very same winds made him famous the length and breadth of Amakna.

7031.descriptionId: Poor Flooey lost his mind after a terrible fight against Many. Fortunately, his amulet didn't suffer. It kept both its mesmerising properties and its laxative powers. To be taken only when absolutely necessary.

7032.descriptionId: This ore probably comes from the depths of the Pandala island mines where Gardan Framine fell head over heels in love with a female Pandawa ghost. Love really doesn't know any boundaries!

7033.descriptionId: Irko, the Dark Miner, had great respect for Dolomite. 'The hard and unbreakable rock' he used to call it.

7034.descriptionId: Passed down from generation to generation, this misshapen helmet was even worn by Crail himself. Many adventurers think it has mysterious powers. As with many divinities and modern heroes, the magical powers of this helmet have all the potency of a shoe.

7035.descriptionId: This alloy was used to forge blades which wouldn't rust when in contact with the blood and drool of its victims.

7036.descriptionId: A shiny alloy, Brassic is tolerated by bankrupt jewellers who can't afford precious stones. They usually make very competitively priced alloys. Comes in handy when you want to marry for money.

7037.descriptionId: This stick used to belong to Granny Candy, one of the three famous Love Priestesses. Sharpened at one end and shiny at the other, this stick is renowned for its versatility and its annoying tendency to turn up just about anywhere. None can resist its power.

7038.descriptionId: This crown belonged to the famous King Jellix, renowned for his unbounded romanticism and his seductive power which left its mark on many female Jellies. Some even say he is the father of all the Jellies of the region of Amakna, proof (if needed) of his stamina and legendary fecundity.

7039.descriptionId: Famous Sunday fighter Frank crossed over into martial arts after he failed miserably at his stone-cutting apprenticeship.

7040.descriptionId: This bow belonged to Kuri, the famous Love Priestess and left-hand woman of Granny Candy. Never turn your back on a Love Priestess. One arrow from this bow is enough to tear your heart to shreds, or your arse if you have actually turned around.

7043.descriptionId: Legend says that this magnificent Dofus came out of the frozen hole of the Water dragon Aguabrial. Legend does not say if he had a cold that day, though it's highly likely.

7045.descriptionId: Pandaburg is a tasty drink which could very slowly make you blind, mute and deaf. How convenient! Pandawas aren't the speedy kind.

7046.descriptionId: According to the erudite Hel Munster, this genuine nectar delights the goddess Pandawa herself, making her completely euphoric. Any true Pandawa should give his Pandapilers away to the venerated goddess.

7047.descriptionId: One of the more sensible Pandawan traditions goes like this: Clink glasses with your neighbour, throw sugar on your hair and burp the following line - "Pandapils, Pandapils, tralalalaHIHOO!".

7050.descriptionId:
Give a Pandawa a fish and he'll eat all day. 
Teach a Pandawa how to fish and he'll spend his days in a rowing boat drinking Panduvel (old Pandawaiian saying).

7056.descriptionId: This unique hat used to belong to a Xelor grandmaster, known the World over for his explosive theories and his incessant meddling with time. His death was as explosive and untimely as his life... Jealous of his neighbour's hat, whose magic powers were said to be even greater than his, he rashly unleashed a Wind of Panic to remove it forever, forgetting about his own. He was blown into a million little pieces when his hat exploded like a giant firecracker.

7058.descriptionId: This headgear is made of dead dried Kralove leftovers. Be careful, it can come back to life if you use it as a bathing cap.

7059.descriptionId: This humongous seed is filled with a heavy but magical oil. Its shell is said to be unbreakable and many craftsmen use it to enchant their weapons. Others stick wiggly eyes on it and put it on the dashboard of their cart.

7061.descriptionId: The water from the Bow Meow Spring temporarily turned you into a Bow Meow. The slightest shock will make you go back to normal.

7068.descriptionId: This flour is perfect for making cement or even bedding for your dog.

7077.descriptionId: This porous but absorbent yellow shield was made from the remains of a creature who used to live in a Pineapi Mask at the bottom of the sea.

7102.descriptionId: The Ice Knight was famous for being one of the greatest sword smiths in all of Amakna. Only Liche the unmerciful refused to recognise his talent. Offended by this creature's ignorance, the Ice Knight stopped working, refusing to forge so much as a teaspoon until she agreed to publicly recognize his talent. The Ice Knight worked the bars around Amakna for a couple of hundred years, but the local economy never crumbled as he had expected, nor did Amakna's military influence waver... as he had also expected. When he finally took up his rusty hammer once more, he found he'd completely forgotten his former skill. This ridiculous sword was his last usable creation.

7103.descriptionId: This Wand was used to behead all the ninnies in Amakna. Suffice to say, it's seen a lot of action. It's interesting to note how much it resembles a staff or even a walking stick. It might even have been used to satisfy the wicked fantasies of the owner who named it. No one will ever have the final word on this sordid story.

7104.descriptionId: These flee-flops were used to practice various martial arts. Not quite revolutionary and artistically speaking, a failure, they were only good for running away, a bit like yourself.

7106.descriptionId: With this Larva head round your neck, you look like Stive Irween, the famous modern-day larva tamer.

7107.descriptionId: You probably never dreamt of putting your feet right inside the guts of a Larva... But here is your chance... Seize it!

7108.descriptionId: This plain bag used to be very fashionable a very long time ago. It is the best example of your ancestors' bad taste.

7109.descriptionId: You finally have the chance to look like a real larva. You will be able to openly show the World your larval lifestyle.

7110.descriptionId: This terrific Wand is made of larva guts which are firstly dried, then enchanted and finally rehydrated. It's totally shapeless. A bit like you, except you're not even enchanted.

7112.descriptionId: The only way to get an egg like this is to force a black dragon to mate with a white dragon. Although some people paint ordinary eggs this colour at home... You may have been tricked.

7113.descriptionId: This Dofus is worryingly similar to a wild Dragoturkey egg. For once, appearances might not be misleading.

7114.descriptionId: Dark as the shadows, hard as rock, Grougalorasalar the Black Dragon created the Ebony Dofus to keep him company. Quite simply, he had forgotten that eggs – no matter how magical they may be – do not talk.

7116.descriptionId: The enchantment in this ring is very strange - once around your finger, the only person you'll be able to talk to will be the jeweller who made it.

7117.descriptionId: A particularly talentless group of cosmopolitan minstrels used this type of ring to keep time at their shows after their original drummer left them. They would all put a ring on a toe, and beat in time. Needless to say, it was the percussion that always let them down.

7118.descriptionId: This big moth-shaped ring won't make your hands pretty, but isn't that a good thing?

7119.descriptionId: The jeweller who created this masterpiece is no relative of the famous sword smith, despite appearances. No one ever understood what the designer said about using the ring.

7120.descriptionId: Contrary to common misunderstanding, this ring has nothing to do with the beautiful Karin, whose regular live shows at Sufokia Pirates' Inn raised many a visiting spirit from the dead. The namesake of this jewel is a musician who breeds Tofus in his spare time... so what, you ask. Well, with this ring, it'll sound like there's a dying tofu attached to your finger.

7121.descriptionId: This living ring has a terrible curse that makes even the toughest of adventurers seriously ill. They say it was originally designed to heal the person who wore it, but since warriors brought it to the most disreputable locations in the land, its sense of dignity led it to become more and more dangerous and aggressive.

7122.descriptionId: This ring is made for tearful novices. It also symbolises some ancient, unspeakable traditions. It's made for you! Perfect.

7123.descriptionId: For experienced adventurers only. It might shock your family and friends to know it's composed of young, innocent creatures.

7124.descriptionId: This Dofus has exceptional power: it can make you drool with joy.

7125.descriptionId: This Dofus has exceptional power: it can make you drool with joy.

7128.descriptionId: Spiteful gossips claim that this ring is the most useful fashion accessory in the World. The wings attached to it can be quite a pain when you need to get a tissue out of your pocket. Now, Iops neither have tissues nor pockets... so, it's just fine.

7129.descriptionId: Don't underestimate this chocolaty treat - not only does it taste fantastic, its shape gives it even more flavour as well. Try a chocolate Ouassingue and you'll understand what I mean.

7130.descriptionId: The recipe for the Chocolate Dofus is a must if you want to impress your friends.

7131.descriptionId: Many other adventurers dreamt of getting their paws on this jewel long before you came along. Indeed, it's said to have many powers, such as the power to turn fierce warriors into good-for-nothing dreamers. It says in my book to never put it near fire. Doesn't say why.

7132.descriptionId: This ring owes its name to the last words pronounced by its creator: "O' Ring Ami! You're such a friend!" he said in a painful but bewitching rattle. It is interesting to note that this Bamboo ring was actually made before Bamboo evolved. Another mystery which will not be solved for another ten years or so!

7133.descriptionId: As any Wabbit will tell you - if you don't want to see red, avoid Myxomawosis like the plague.

7134.descriptionId: Some say Rabies completely changes the affected beings. Warriors become docile, and calm persons become aggressive. However, persons who dribbled will not change.

7135.descriptionId: This is a disease transmitted by Moskitos from tropical regions. Maloria is so called because the disease can be transmitted by Moskito spit as well.

7136.descriptionId: This medal used to belong to a famous Pandawa master at an old martial arts school who taught his disciples the principles of defence using their opponents' strength. His school finally closed down because his opponents were no longer strong enough.

7137.descriptionId: This Cape was hand-sewn for one single reason: to stop you from sleeping for weeks on end. It is so rigid that it will keep you standing still and upright no matter what happens. Just don't try to tie your shoelaces.

7138.descriptionId: Worn by the most important people in the World, this cloak is famous for its legendary softness which means you don't have to put on underwear in the warm season. An elegant way to expose yourself...

7139.descriptionId: The shoemaker loved strolling in the fields, looking for improbable love. Instead of finding her soul mate, she died falling into a huge ditch full of filth, close to the Pig Zone. Her body was found seventy years later, when they finally emptied the ditch. Her brother apparently said: "We all have to go sometime", before falling into the ditch himself.

7140.descriptionId: Contrary to appearances, Xena was not a warrior, but a shoemaker. Her generous figure and her unlimited passion for housework strongly suggested a brilliant career in the inns of Amakna. But it wasn't to be.

7141.descriptionId: This strange hat will protect you from sun beams, especially when its dark. Be careful though, every thirty years it comes to life and tries to suffocate its owner... It doesn't say when the last time... I wouldn't worry about it.

7142.descriptionId: This hat was used by some Xelors to hide their hereditary baldness. Enutrofs used it to hide their bills. In short, a useful way to hide two major issues of daily life.

7143.descriptionId: The Solomonk hat was worn by the Chief of a Pandawa tribe. Experts in laxative potions, low-ranking Pandawas were often obliged to test the potions for the alchemists. When banished to the jungle for these trials, this hat doubled as a chamber pot, reducing their load considerably.

7144.descriptionId: This wedding hat has gone out of fashion, its lace is no longer considered stylish. If it was recycled into knickers and worn on a hairy head, it might still get a reaction out of a Chafer.

7145.descriptionId: Gaddie, a strange creature from an imaginary World, always stood out for its incredible cunning, its total aversion to plants and its ability to fast for days on end in times of war. A creature that's complex to understand was obviously impossible to control. It was abandoned in the depths of the bottomless Kruup mine where its only friend was an old, Gobbly devouring Liche.

7146.descriptionId: This headgear looks like any old wig, but it is powerful indeed. It has one prior owner who had the strange and despicable habit of dressing up as other people, and conning the elderly into signing over items of tiny value. Once he convinced a gentle old man that he was his dead wife returned to life, proceeded to 'remarry' him, had six of his children (which even I can't explain) and then, ten years later, just as they were about to renew their vows on a scenic cliffside, he broke the news. It is said he ran off with three party poppers and a half-eaten ball of Stracciatella ice cream, laughing wildly... still laughing as he tripped and fell over the cliff and laughing to this day if you believe the popular but unlikely sea shanty, 'The crazy fool took my Stracciatella'.

7147.descriptionId: Made with bamboo milk, this chocolate is a delight for kids and grown-ups so.

7148.descriptionId: Are you dreaming of a white chocolate like the one you used to know? Here y'are then. Just eat in moderation to avoid getting fat and unhealthy.

7149.descriptionId: Directly extracted from cocoa beans, this square of dark chocolate is very tasty. Be careful not to eat too much of it, it'll give you the spotty skin of a 13-year-old, chain-smoking truck-driver.

7150.descriptionId: This hat, strangely named, belonged to a poor Ecaflip who became mute after a traumatic event. An artist through and through, he was compelled to follow a Brewer training. When he turned 14, he drowned in a barrel of beer and tears. Fortunately, beer was not wasted as the priest who was in charge of the funeral fell into an alcoholic coma for many years before he could take his office right where he had stopped it.

7151.descriptionId: On the box of this helmet, it said: 'This imposing clay helmet will turn you into a giant with a head of clay'. Upon further inspection, you realise the helmet is not made of clay, but of lead. Every year, many adventurers die, trapped under this helmet like nipples under a Chinese fire cup.

7152.descriptionId: This basin-shaped hat was used by the firemen of Amakna when there were fires on cereal fields. Nowadays it is mainly used by brewers and pub waitresses who are treated like walking barrels.

7153.descriptionId: This huge hammer makes a very loud noise when hitting a Iop's skull as it tends to amplify sound. As surprising as it is effective.

7154.descriptionId: This light hammer is designed for small beings. Xelors used to find great pleasure in squashing Arachnees with this implement. Its use quickly changed and it became a little toy for young Iop Handymen.

7155.descriptionId: For fifty long years, the famous Captain Haddock'n'roll used this terrible Hammer to slay anyone who got in his way – including women and children. In spite of his legendary bad temper and his addiction to alcohol, he won the respect of all warriors – both friend and enemy.

7156.descriptionId: This rusty hammer is perfect for all your smashing needs - pulverising maple trees, atomising Moskitos, this hammer can do it it all.

7157.descriptionId: This hammer was used to sound the bell of the Church of Amakna every Sunday. In these times of war, it's used much more often than that.

7158.descriptionId: This hammer was crafted by a famous alchemist during his sentence in the prison of Brakmar. He planned to steal his competitors' secrets and get rich when he got out. This hammer was the first in a collection of devilish instruments.

7159.descriptionId: As the Enutrof philosopher Traincartes once said, "I think, therefore I hammer." It sums up the way this greedy bunch sees the World.

7160.descriptionId: Many ages ago, this Bow was occupied with a very dark magic, a mysterious force that strikes fear into both its owners and its targets in equal measure.

7161.descriptionId: This bow was mainly used to hunt Plain Boars. Indeed, it is so powerful that it can kill several young boars with one single arrow, provided that they stand still in a line. Well it could happen!

7162.descriptionId: This Bow belonged to an independent group of Minstrels mainly famous for their war cries which destroyed their enemies' ear drums. They were firstly banished to Pandala, but after driving generations of Pandawa nuts, they were finally brought to the Great Sorlok to be slowly digested for more than 752 years.

7163.descriptionId: This bow was used as a dissuasive weapon. The owner of the Runaway Bow claimed that he was using poisoned arrows so any cowards he met would take off instantly.

7164.descriptionId: Light and fragile, this bow appeals to adventurers who are more concerned about appearances than substance.

7165.descriptionId: This explosive wand was dipped into the lava of an erupting volcano before being sculpted, and then enchanted. It goes without saying that it's very powerful, despite its ridiculous appearance.

7167.descriptionId: The craftsman who created this wand had many apprentices. He made them work all day long. He was supposed to teach them the tricks of the trade but as it turned out, he was a terrible teacher. He always started sentences but never finished them.

7168.descriptionId: Once sculpted, this wand was soaked in beer for many decades 'to put a few magical powers into it', as the people who made it said. Unfortunately, it started to rot, but it has a few magical properties... it can lure worms to the earth's surface for example. Are you into fishing by any chance?

7169.descriptionId: Ideal for lighting a fire, or indeed lighting up a dreary party. With this wand, you just might get the chance to shine once in your life. An opportunity not to be missed.

7170.descriptionId: Creizy the pastry chef was nuts... he married Stufh the Lumberjane and choked her to death the very next day with his fat-stuffed pastries. Ever since, the phrase "Creizy Stufh" is used to express an unhappy surprise after a great celebration.

7171.descriptionId: The designer of this wand kept forgetting to pick his kids up at school. Conscious of his absent-mindedness, he sculpted a wand that would come to life everyday and remind him to pick his kids up. After a while, he kept thinking the wand was waking him up to remind him to go to the bathroom. His children were taken away from him not long after.

7172.descriptionId: This magic wand is still used today to empty septic tanks, clean out ditches and pick noses. Most informed sculptors will tell you that it derives all its magic from all the filthy waste it's been dragged through... in reality, it's the dirty gunge from your snout.

7173.descriptionId: This terrific Wand can wrap itself round your opponent's neck and strangle them slowly but surely. An original and distinguished way of killing enemies you don't respect.

7174.descriptionId: This cloak is essential if you want to practice the art of Pandawushu.

7175.descriptionId: This medical certificate is essential if you want to practice Pandawushuka.

7176.descriptionId: Frank, a master staff carver, was the fellow who created this little wonder. It can darken the sky with raging clouds and draw the blood of your enemies, even if they don't have any. Legend says it took him nine years to carve. Even your enemies will have to compliment you on this beautifully crafted weapon.

7177.descriptionId: With this Pandawushu Headband around your skull, you'll be able to scare away young Lenalds pretending to be martial arts Masters. Don't forget to bawl a bit of a war cry to be more convincing.

7178.descriptionId: If it wasn't for the incessant arguing over whether this thing is a fruit or a root, it would be an excellent weapon.

7181.descriptionId: Red was a young Sadidette. She loved singing, though she had a terrible voice. She always dreamt of travelling to Chili. She was often sent packing but never got anywhere...

7182.descriptionId: Mel was quite unlucky. Her husband was a lazy cad, incapable of assuming his status as the head of the family. She was convinced that incessant nagging was the way to go. "You'll get no strawberry jelly if you don't go harvest that barley" or "You'll get no tobacco till you've sheared those Gobballs" and so on. Obviously, this story has nothing to do with this very powerful root, unless it starts to nag you too.

7183.descriptionId: This Root has a purity that is the essence of perfection for some wide-eyed craftsmen. I can tell you from experience that this root is the single greatest cause of marital breakdown in the entire region.

7184.descriptionId: This terrible root is mainly known for its capacity to provoke climatic disasters at the exact place where it's been used. Avoid using it to kick your enemies around. It is an abuse which could see you and all your friends burnt to a crisp, drowned in a flood, blown to bits, frozen solid, misted to... well the last one wouldn't be so bad, but just don't use it okay!

7185.descriptionId: Using this root during a fight is supposed to be very easy. Nevertheless, it can happen that the root somehow comes to life and does whatever it wants... that's generally when the owner yells "This is not the usual Root 'Een, is it?". Well, it is indeed the usual Root 'Een.

7186.descriptionId: This piece of paper is stamped with the date you last earnt a new Pandawushuka level.

7187.descriptionId: This bow is reviled the land over for leading its archers into battle at the slightest sign of unusual behaviour. Drinking loudly, shaking hands for longer than is proper, and wearing hats - a few examples of what can make the bow start shooting wildly.

7188.descriptionId: These Daggers are often used for cutting lemons, or the ground right out from under your enemies' feet. An original way to surprise them which often comes to a messy end.

7189.descriptionId: This unusual staff is an improved version of the well-known God Rod. It was designed and crafted after the God Rod had been thoroughly tested by the Priestesses of Love. This model was even used and abused by Kuri herself, which makes it something of a unique item.

7190.descriptionId: When a precocious Sramette princess couldn't find a single dagger that suited her, she offered a challenge to the dagger smiths of Amakna: the one who forged her a set capable of killing a Tofu in one blow would spend three nights in her bed. Unfortunately, not a single smith took up her challenge. By the time she found a willing craftsman, a retiree of the trade who never should have started in the first place, she'd been advertising her offer among other things on the streets of Madrestam for 17 years. Let's just say that time hadn't been kind to the proud Sramette.

7191.descriptionId: Ramougre was an old Sram who became a jewellery master. He used this setter to perfect his creations as well as to murder his clients when he got bored. He was known for his bad temper, sometimes destroying his setter and his most beautiful creations. Today, when people with these daggers get angry, they pay tribute to Ramougre by cutting off some family jewels.

7192.descriptionId: Grizmine never succeeded in properly using this Claw - he was always too drunk.

7193.descriptionId: No one but Dark Vlad himself can use this sword properly, but if you carry it round town at least people will know you're not one of those pathetic fools who died under its blade.

7194.descriptionId: This bow is proof that combining technology and magic can yield incredible results. Yet it quickly fell out of favour for reasons that are still poorly understood. The crafter who created this bow even had to shut down his shop, leaving many of his former customers profoundly distraught.

7195.descriptionId: This legendary sword was forged early one morning by a drunken Enutrof army, deep in the mines of Grimoth. It has a very powerful aura as well as a potent hum of beer.

7197.descriptionId: This hammer was used to break chocolate blocks into dust for so many years, it eventually gained a delicious flavour. One more reason to give your enemies a taste!

7198.descriptionId: Any old Enutrof will tell you that a well-maintained beard is every woman's dream. This razor is so sharp it'll even take care of that thick, curly back hair.

7199.descriptionId: This sword belonged to a butcher called Franky Abatz who used it to disembowel his enemies for sausage meat. I used to go to that stall... Believe me, I made sure the dirty mongrel paid for every sausage he ever sold.

7200.descriptionId: This magnificent sabre is used by Pandawushuka disciples when they reach the Shodanwa level alive.

7201.descriptionId: This magnificent Sabre is used by Pandawushuka disciples when they reach the Nidanwa level alive.

7202.descriptionId: This magnificent sabre is used by Pandawushuka disciples when they reach the Sandanwa level alive.

7203.descriptionId: This magnificent sabre is used by Pandawushuka disciples when they reach the Yondanwa level alive.

7204.descriptionId: This Staff is normally used by Pandawushuka disciples when they reach Shodanwa level without losing the use of their arms in the process.

7205.descriptionId: This Staff is normally used by Pandawushuka disciples when they reach the Nidanwa level without losing the use of their arms in the process.

7206.descriptionId: This Staff is normally used by Pandawushuka disciples when they reach the Sandanwa level without losing the use of their arms in the process.

7207.descriptionId: This Staff is normally used by Pandawushuka disciples when they reach the Yondanwa level without losing the use of their arms in the process.

7208.descriptionId: This Axe is used by Pandawushuka disciples when they reach the Shodanwa level. It makes short work of Bamboo Forests, including anything that may be hiding in the undergrowth.

7209.descriptionId: This Axe is used by Pandawushuka disciples when they reach the Nidanwa level. It makes short work of Bamboo Forests, including anything that may be hiding in the undergrowth.

7210.descriptionId: This Axe is used by Pandawushuka disciples when they reach the Sandanwa level. It makes short work of Bamboo forests, including anything that may be hiding in the undergrowth.

7211.descriptionId: This axe is used by Pandawushuka disciples when they reach the Yondanwa level. It makes short work of Bamboo forests, including anything that may be hiding in the undergrowth.

7212.descriptionId: Equipped with this light and elegant axe you'll be able to progress more easily through the Bamboo Forests of Pandala. It will serve as sufficient protection against the warlike Pandis who never get tired of attacking lone lumberjacks who wander through their lands.

7213.descriptionId: This Shovel is supposed to cut through the soil at an incredible speed. Those who know how to handle it usually split their enemies' skulls open instead.

7214.descriptionId: These Sandals belonged to the Macians, an Ouginak tribe, which became extinct. They were so close to the Pandawas that, as the generations passed by, their fur slowly changed colour. One day, they were all killed by a horrible woman who wanted to make a coat out of them.

7215.descriptionId: These thong sandals were formerly used by female Pandits to seduce lost adventurers and lure them into traps.

7216.descriptionId: Those sandals are given to sick Pandawas for those special emergencies... we're talking the dreaded McSheth, which usually comes a knocking when they drink too much down at the Inn.

7217.descriptionId: Pandawas have always been attracted by alcoholic beverages. As time went by, they discovered how best to conserve and flavour them. These sandals were made especially for alcoholic Pandawas. They're ballasted at the sole so that you can keep your feet firmly on the ground, most of the time. Good for fighting, terrible for running away.

7218.descriptionId: Adin was a young Pandawa who loved collecting lamps, but he was far from being a genius.

7219.descriptionId: Those sandals were awarded to young Pandits at the end of religious rituals. Nowadays they are mainly used for tap-dancing championships.

7220.descriptionId: Between your fat little fingers you're greedily clutching a superb Lottery Ticket. Hold on to it. You might be the lucky winner at the great draw!

7221.descriptionId: Tanukouï Sans wear this collar from early childhood. Given what these monsters are capable of, it's no wonder this jewellery is so valuable.

7226.descriptionId: From a distance, you'll look like a Pandawushuka from Akwadala Village wearing this hat. Up close, you'll look like an idiot.

7227.descriptionId: From a distance, you'll look like a Pandawushuka from Terrdala Village wearing this hat. Up close, you'll look like an idiot.

7228.descriptionId: From a distance, you'll look like a Pandawushuka from Feudala Village wearing this hat. Up close, you'll look like an idiot.

7229.descriptionId: From a distance, you'll look like a Pandawushuka from Aerdala Village wearing this hat. Up close, you'll look like an idiot.

7230.descriptionId: This cloak comes from Akwadala. It can be used as a doormat or even as a floorcloth if you've just come out of water.

7231.descriptionId: This cloak comes from Terrdala Village. It can be used as a doormat or even as a towel if you've just come out of the water.

7232.descriptionId: This cloak comes from Feudala. It can be used as a doormat or even as a towel if you've just come out of the water.

7233.descriptionId: This cloak comes from Aerdala. It can be used as a doormat or even as a floorcloth if you've just come out of water.

7238.descriptionId: Pandawas from Akwadala always watch their figure. If you tighten this belt as much as possible, you should finally get some results with your flabby belly problem.

7239.descriptionId: Pandawas from Terrdala always watch their figure. If you tighten this belt as much as possible, you should finally get some results with your flabby belly problem.

7240.descriptionId: Pandawas from Feudala always watch their figure. If you tighten this belt as much as possible, you should finally get some results with your flabby belly problem.

7241.descriptionId: Pandawas from Aerdala always watch their figure. If you tighten this belt as much as possible, you should finally get some results with your flabby belly problem.

7242.descriptionId: These wooden Geta were made by the best shoemaker in the village of Akwadala. Let your warts take a breath of fresh air and enjoy the landscape.

7243.descriptionId: These wooden Geta were made by the best shoemaker in the village of Terrdala. Let your warts take a breath of fresh air and enjoy the landscape.

7244.descriptionId: These wooden Geta were made by the best shoemaker in the village of Feudala. Let your warts take a breath of fresh air and enjoy the landscape.

7245.descriptionId: These wooden Geta were made by the best shoemaker in the village of Aerdala. Let your warts take a breath of fresh air and enjoy the landscape.

7246.descriptionId: This Wedding Ring comes from the village of Akwadala. More likely to be a lucky charm than a magic relic, you'll still be able to make your friends believe you found your soul mate.

7247.descriptionId: This Wedding Ring comes from the village of Terrdala. More likely to be a lucky charm than a magic relic, you'll still be able to make your friends believe you've found your soul mate.

7248.descriptionId: This Wedding Ring comes from the village of Feudala. More likely to be a lucky charm than a magic relic, you'll still be able to make your friends believe you've found your soul mate.

7249.descriptionId: This Wedding Ring comes from the village of Aerdala. More likely to be a lucky charm than a magic relic, you'll still be able to make your friends believe you've found your soul mate.

7250.descriptionId: The only people allowed to wear this amulet were the inhabitants of the village of Akwadala, as it was considered to be one of the most important parts of their traditional costume. Seen close up, you have to ask yourself why.

7251.descriptionId: The only people allowed to wear this amulet were the inhabitants of the village of Terrdala, as it was considered to be one of the most important parts of their traditional costume. Seen close up, you have to ask yourself why.

7252.descriptionId: The only people allowed to wear this amulet were the inhabitants of the village of Feudala, as it was considered to be one of the most important parts of their traditional costume. Seen close up, you have to ask yourself why.

7253.descriptionId: The only people allowed to wear this amulet were the inhabitants of the village of Aerdala, as it was considered to be one of the most important parts of their traditional costume. Seen close up, you have to ask yourself why.

7254.descriptionId: This staff was used to give young boisterous Pandawa a trashing. Three raps on the knuckles, fifteen lashes across the back, sixty blows to the head, two pokes in the eyes, that would be enough to calm them down a bit.

7255.descriptionId: This axe was designed for one thing only: cutting living beings. So be careful, as a single miscalculation and you could be cut in half!

7256.descriptionId: As sharp as Moowolf claws, these daggers will turn you into a perfect apprentice assassin.

7257.descriptionId: This Sabre was forged by Hotari Honza himself. It's said to be one of his last creations before he took an intensive cooking course and became a chef. A collector's item for sure!

7300.descriptionId: This thick hide provides excellent protection against cold air and draughts.

7313.descriptionId: Every practicing Pandawushu should know this book by heart.

7339.descriptionId: This Kitsou cap can only be worn by adventurers who've lost their sense of smell. Don't ask me why.

7340.descriptionId: This wrap is river-washable, even though it might fade after the third cycle.

7341.descriptionId: This small Kitsou ring will protect you from casual troubles.

7342.descriptionId: This Kitsou Amulet will draw attention to your double chin.

7344.descriptionId: This certificate celebrates the date of your last victory at the Dojo.

7345.descriptionId: This certificate celebrates the date of your last victory at the Terrdala Dojo.

7350.descriptionId: Aermyne is now in your custody and needs to be delivered safely to jail.

7351.descriptionId: Rok Gnorok is now under your control. You can take him to jail.

7352.descriptionId: Musha the Oni is now under your control. You can take him to jail.

7353.descriptionId: Marzwel the Goblin is now under your control. You can take him to jail.

7354.descriptionId: Zatoishwan is now under your control. You can take him to jail.

7356.descriptionId: Water from the cursed Bwak Spring has temporarily turned you into a Bwak. The slightest shock will bring you back to normal.

7357.descriptionId: Water from the cursed Young Wild Boar Spring has temporarily turned you into a Young Wild Boar. The slightest shock will bring you back to normal.

7368.descriptionId: The designer of this wand wanted to use it to destroy the shooting stars that kept him awake at night. The legend goes that one night, as he left the tavern after one too many, he decided to test the wand, but mistook the moon for a shooting star. The wand, which really was incredibly powerful, split the moon clean in two, and one of the halves fell into the middle of the Asse Sea, thus creating Moon Island as we know it today. Another little anecdote he can tell the grandkids...

7371.nameId: The Dofus Era - Found Fragments IV
7371.descriptionId: Part IV of the Fragments of the History of the World found by the erudite Acidrik Gutsplitter and rewritten by the same.

7413.descriptionId: Use this scroll to learn the Point emote, either to show the way or to tell on cheaters.

7414.descriptionId: This fluffy ball of hair scratches, bites, and pinches everything that comes close, including the hand that feeds it! It's a terrifying yet irresistibly likeable and fascinating creature. Any resemblance to famous (or infamous) people (living or dead) might possibly be entirely intentional. Be careful, not only is it quick-tempered, it's also quite picky about its diet. It only eats fresh meat from hunted creatures.

7415.descriptionId: This odd little creature only eats fresh fish. But don't worry – its wholesome company more than makes up for its dehydrated-fish breath.

7417.descriptionId: This certificate describes the characteristics of the Peki Peki that you left at the Bow Kennel.

7422.descriptionId:
This exotic, fruit-shaped mask is a real collector's item. It is absolutely useless, but you'll look original and tasty. People appreciate the effort.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

7423.descriptionId: As strange as it may seem, these Golden Larva Eggs are not laid by Golden Larvae but by more common sorts - green, orange or even blue. Nature is full of disappointing surprises.

7496.descriptionId: This potion enables you to resurrect all the allies present around you.

7497.descriptionId: This potion enables you to free the souls of your enemies to send them directly to their cemetery, without giving them a chance to be resurrected.

7498.descriptionId: This potion enables you to heal all allies present on the map.

7502.descriptionId: This Potion allows you to create a rallying point so that aligned adventurers can join you for either the attack or protection of a village. This magic potion also allows you to save the position of anyone who joined you so they can return to their starting point quickly.

7505.descriptionId: This Potion will make you unlearn the profession of Costumagus.

7506.descriptionId: Use this potion to forget the profession of Jewelmagus.

7507.descriptionId: Use this potion to forget the profession of Shoemagus.

7508.descriptionId:
This rune allows the best craftsmen to put their signature on their creations.
(To be used along with the ingredients when crafting items.)

7513.descriptionId: Titude, a modest Enutrof shoemaker, was even smaller than a Xelor. Legend says he created these sandals to be able to kiss his lady-love, a legless Eniripsa, on the lips.

7514.descriptionId: Harry was an old wise man who spent his days fishing on the docks of Sufokia. His great moustache made him look like Danous Kwaide, famous actor of a theatre company that used to play at the Amakna Tavern. All this was only a prelude to incredible beer and meat ball orgies.

7515.descriptionId: This cape doesn't come from your Galaxy but it seems to match the colour of your Gobbly-wool fishnet stockings all the same.

7516.descriptionId: It was an old, unlucky, bitter Enutrof who first discovered this terrible hat, hidden at the bottom of a crevasse in the Bimd'Oule Caverns. Later, the Enutrof exiled himself far away from the lands of Amakna to escape boredom and discover new horizons. Legend tells that he comes back to his native land once a century to make fun of his old friends... but we all know he's just a bit nostalgic.

7517.descriptionId: This beer is so acidic it can hardly be drunk. Indeed, the acidity gives the pint the shelf-life of an overweight Moskito...

7518.descriptionId: This surprising creature comes from the afterlife and isn't willing to go back there unless it takes you with it.

7519.descriptionId: This little dragon's skin is as pink as a bodacious Bwork's backside. That makes it a risk-free and cheap thing to fantasise about, or just a nice reminder of happy times. Luckily for the dragon, it's not just something for you to lust after. It is also a very wise and powerful creature. A word of warning, however: its hunger for other pets is as great as a Chafer's wickedness during the full moon, and it only feeds on other pets' ghosts.

7520.descriptionId: A retired toy soldier, this metal creature suddenly came to life one day. It will follow you everywhere you go, risking its life to save yours. All you have to do in return is feed the little guy regularly. Don't expect it to fight your fights for you, though – it won't be replacing the low-level adventurers of Astrub anytime soon.

7521.descriptionId: If you shake this object vigorously and hold your ear to it, you'll hear a strange noise... like a tiny animal weeping... yeah, actually maybe you don't want to shake it... Ahhh, just open the damn thing. You'll find a wonderful pet inside it, as well as some food and healing Eniripsa powders.

7522.descriptionId: Tamed and cleaned, this baby Minotoror can be approached and petted without fear of losing fingers or hands. Don't let down your guard, though, as sometimes nature can reclaim control, and the creature's destructive instincts will take over just when you need its help most. To avoid such nasty surprises, raise it like a child in need of a very strict education.

7523.descriptionId:
No tomcat – not even the most indifferent – can resist this lovely ginger creature!
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

7524.descriptionId: This surprising creature is the result of crossbreeding a white bow meow and a black bow meow. It only eats fish.

7525.descriptionId: If you hold this gift to your ear, you'll hear a strange noise which reveals the presence of a living creature inside. Open it, and you'll find a wonderful pet, as well as a book explaining how to raise it, some food and some healing Eniripsa Powder.

(WARNING: this gift is very heavy. You might be overweight when you open it. Remember to take your heavy items off, or to ask a friend to help you.)

7552.descriptionId: Sometimes, when true love joins a warrior and a Dragoturkey, weird things can happen. This cape proves it since there are Dragoturkey wings sewn on it. The Dragoturkey sacrificed itself for the making of this cape offered to the famous minstrel Pol Akartney on their wedding day. Apparently Jon Lemon even wrote a song about it.

7553.descriptionId: If you ever dreamt of looking like a turkey, this is your chance! However, if you want to remain healthy, we advise you not to wear this hat on the streets of Amakna during the Christmas season.

7554.descriptionId: Your friends are definitely going to be jealous. Those boots will take you all the way to the ambassador's party for one of those wonderful little golden chocolates.

7556.descriptionId: This gift contains one part of a famous costume. It will definitely make your Dragoturkey friends jealous.

7557.descriptionId: This key made of Treechnid wood could take root in any warm and humid microsystem... like a Bwork's briefs, for example.

7558.descriptionId: These hairs won't stay in your bag for long. Well, I really hope not, anyway.

Yes, I lied to you once again. Hahaha. I love this job.

7704.descriptionId: This squirrel is a real acorn twister. It'll tickle your monkey nuts one minute and break 'em the next. This pet only eats seeds.

7707.descriptionId: This wild little piggy has an immeasurably large snout, particularly suited to sniffing out big acorns. By chance, it seems to have found you quite easily.

7879.descriptionId: Domen's Colossal, Immoral, Unusual Annals will send shivers down your spine. Must be read according to prescription. Side effects: cold sweats and bed wetting.

7880.descriptionId: This Amulet was worn by adventurers who said they wanted to make tea, not war. Each to their own.

7881.descriptionId: This ring will enable you to cause even more pain when doling out those well-deserved spankings to your little darlings.

7882.descriptionId: This hammer is great for expressing your pacifism... all over your enemy's face.

7883.descriptionId: Stuffed with Gobkool wool, these boots are just fantastic. Light and warm for the cold season and cool for the hot one, they will please even the pickiest of adventurers.

7884.descriptionId: If you're the kind of person who always thinks positive, this cape is made for you. It's so thick and comfy that it can be used as an improvised bed when you feel extremely sleepy. Its smoked Kaliptus odour even repels insects and other unwanted creatures.

7885.descriptionId: Wrapped around your hips, this belt will give you the appearance of a peace-loving adventurer. This enables you to surprise your enemies with a dagger in their back.

7886.descriptionId: Let's be honest, as headwear goes, this cap is about as fashionable as a mullet hairdo. You never know though, look what happened to drainpipe jeans.

7887.descriptionId: This headgear once belonged to the famous Koolich, renowned for his clay feet and his legendary good mood.

7888.descriptionId: The Koolich uses this bag to keep his Kaliptus leaves fresh or to suffocate Koalaks that are a bit too enterprising.

7889.descriptionId: These boots used to belong to the Koolich - even if you can't tell, you can smell! These boots are so comfortable that you'll almost forget how miserable your existence is.

7890.descriptionId: This staff is really an emptied bone of one of the Koolich's ancestors. Pierced on both ends, it can be used as a Kaliptus pipe but also as a shepherd's stick. Ahhhh... sticks, eh! What would we do without them?

7891.descriptionId: This little Wabbit is in fact a secret son of the notorious Wa Wabbit. Maybe one day it'll get to wear its father's crown.

7892.descriptionId: Willy Peninzias is a nasty creature indeed. From what we can tell, he had a particularly difficult childhood. Count on him to follow you around and scare your friends away.

7893.descriptionId: This Mini Wa Ghost hasn't left the living world yet. Will you find a way to resurrect it or cowardly abandon it once and for all?

7894.descriptionId: This Willy Peninzias Ghost hasn't left the living world yet. Will you find a way to resurrect it or cowardly abandon it once and for all?

7895.descriptionId: This certificate describes the characteristics of the Mini Wa that you left at the Bow Kennel.

7896.descriptionId: This certificate describes the characteristics of the Willy Peninzias that you left at the Bow Kennel.

7897.descriptionId:
If you hold this gift to your ear, you'll hear a strange noise which reveals the presence of a living creature inside. Open it, and you'll find a wonderful pet, as well as a book explaining how to raise it, some food and some healing Eniripsa Powder.
(WARNING: this gift is very heavy. You might be overweight when you open it. Remember to take your heavy items off, or to ask a friend to help you.)

7898.descriptionId:
If you hold this gift to your ear, you'll hear a strange noise which reveals the presence of a living creature inside. Open it, and you'll find a wonderful pet, as well as a book explaining how to raise it, some food and some healing Eniripsa Powder.
(WARNING: this gift contains very heavy items. You might be overweight when you open it. Remember to take your heavy items off, or to ask a friend to help you.)

7902.descriptionId: An old legend extracted from the famous old book titled "Everything You Need To Know About Women" says that this belt once belonged to a golden lady, a lot more interested in wealth than in power. In the non-censored version of this book, we also learn that she was keen on cracking dirty jokes. I guess she wasn't that different from most women.

7903.descriptionId: Delicately inserted in nostrils, these leaves will unblock any nose. Some tribal legends even say that this technique works for other orifices.

7904.descriptionId: When you burn it, this flower gives off a thick hallucinogenic smoke. When you chew it, it tends to make you impotent. And if you use it to make an infusion, it will have great laxative effects. The best thing to do would be not to touch it at all.

7905.descriptionId: This wool looks like Gobball wool but isn't. This wool doesn't smell.

7908.descriptionId: This key of bone will enable you to enter the Koolich Cavern even if you haven't been invited.

7911.descriptionId: This little Koalak seems harmless, but that's far from the truth. Tortured when it was young, it frequently received boomerangs in the face, or even the bum. It has positively loathed boomerangs ever since and gobbles them up without bothering to chew.

7913.descriptionId: This mysterious item, forgotten by the World, used to belong to a great magus. People say it gives you the ability to speak to certain animals.

7917.descriptionId:
To make up for the recent problems that you've encountered, the Amakna Team offers you this gift-box including:
- 5 Wise Compensation Candies
- 5 Lucky Compensation Candies
- 10 Energy Compensation Candies
- 10 Eniripsa Powders

7918.descriptionId: This key, made of Tofu feathers, can tickle the inside of many locks into hysterics of opening. It will grant you access to Farle Ingalsse's Tofu House.

7919.descriptionId: You can probably exchange this beautiful token for precious gifts at the Trool Fair.

7920.descriptionId: This modest wand allows Game Masters to teleport adventurers into areas reserved for tournaments.

7921.descriptionId: This crown is almost impossible to hold... No surprise, it belongs to the Royal Tofu! Doesn't seem to suit your small head, though. I think it just might be out of your league. LOSER!!!

7922.descriptionId: This stuffed Sacrier Dopple is just perfect for young Sacriers. It's great for mopping up blood and can even be washed at high temperatures.

7923.descriptionId: This stuffed Pandawa Dopple smells like alcohol and wet Pandawa hair... Ah, just like mummy.

7924.descriptionId: This wonderful key will allow you to get into the Labyrinth of the Minotoror. It won't help you get out again, though.

7925.descriptionId: This scented wood can be used to build nice-smelling houses even if their owners stink. It's a pity it isn't supple enough to make underwear.

7926.descriptionId: Use this key to meet Lord Crow himself. If you're lucky, he might invite you to share a piece of cheese in his company.

7927.descriptionId: This key is almost unbreakable but it is a little worn from opening so many doors. It looks like it's been created from the intimate parts of a Crackler.

7929.descriptionId: Reminder of the basic principles to master to become a hero, by Ganymede.

7930.nameId: How to Make Friends and Keep Them
7930.descriptionId: Some advice and tips to make nice and loyal friends, written by Ganymede.

7931.descriptionId: Part III of the Fragments of the History of the World, found by the erudite Acidrik Gutsplitter and rewritten by the same.

7934.nameId: How to Travel Without Ever Losing Your Way - Volume I
7934.descriptionId: Wally Elconom wrote this book for adventurers who don't know their compass from their Zaaps.

7935.descriptionId: This jewel was stuck in someone's hair for months. The inscription on it explains that it can be used as a key once reunited with its cousin brooches.

7936.descriptionId: This jewel was stuck in someone's hair for months. The inscription on it explains that it can be used as a key once reunited with its cousin brooches.

7939.nameId: How to Become the Perfect Recruit, Brakmar Edition.
7939.descriptionId: How to align yourself with getting aligned, or rules to follow to live the life of a Militiaman by Ganymede.

7940.descriptionId: How to align yourself with getting aligned, or rules to follow to live the life of a Militiaman by Ganymede.

7999.descriptionId:
Some adventurers say that this cape is as rough as a Crocodyl's skin, and still others say that it's even rougher than a Bwork's bottom. Be sure to wear it the right way round if you don't want to be pared to a point like a pencil.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

8000.descriptionId: This small creature is a Bwork that was locked inside a jar for several decades. It took the shape of the jar as it grew, and will now be a dwarf the rest of its life. Its legendary good humour makes it the perfect companion when you know you're going to die soon, or for boisterous social occasions. Be careful, because it's a fan of appetizers, but it can only handle walnuts, hazelnuts and the occasional acorn.

8003.descriptionId: This amulet does not look like any other amulet, simply because no other amulet looks like it.

8004.descriptionId: This beautiful ring is worn by the most foolhardy of all Koalaks... the ones who stole it in Astrub.

8005.descriptionId: This bow enables you to steal your opponents' life and sometimes, to steal your opponents from life. (Don't spend too long trying to understand, that doesn't mean anything.)

8006.descriptionId: These boots are in fact real Koalak feet that were brutally pulled off their owners, then emptied of their content before being padded with Koalak hairs. Both terrifying and attractive, these boots will make you the terror of Astrub.

8007.descriptionId: This cloak will protect you from most attacks, but not from being ridiculous.

8008.descriptionId: This Kaliptus leaf belt diffuses a delightful smell that will hide all others. Besides, this belt is perfect for hiding your chubbiness.

8009.descriptionId: This headgear is adorned with huge Koalak ears which can amplify any sound within hearing distance. Be careful, it can destroy your eardrums if your friends are fond of the Wind of Panic.

8010.descriptionId: Enables you to reclaim any piece of equipment installed a paddock.

8011.descriptionId: Some great stories about cults that will delight the aspiring mystic.

8012.descriptionId: This powder will bring a ghost pet or petsmount back to life, provided you know how to feed a ghost pet or petsmount this time. Oshimo, at the Astrub Bow Kennel, might be able to help you.

8013.descriptionId: You've been transformed into a ghost to be able to get in the Pet Sanctuary.

8016.descriptionId: This Bloody Koalak Ghost hasn't left the living world yet. Will you find a way to resurrect it or cowardly abandon it once and for all?
