11041.descriptionId:
Heavy, clumsy, dull and ugly, just how was Goultard able to become such a formidable fighter using this mediocre sword? Wielding it yourself will not improve your skills: it will just make you look ridiculous.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

11042.descriptionId: This belt was given to Goultard by his father for his 5th birthday. It is more solid than its appearance suggests, and will keep your trousers snugly around your hips. It can also be used as a washing line, or even a skipping rope.

11043.descriptionId:
This hat is so tight-fitting that it compresses the skull and causes hallucinations. Fortunately, Goultard wore it when he was young, and what's more, he has quite a small skull, which betrays his roots.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

11044.descriptionId: A few mouldering bones and some funereal jewellery is all that is left of Goultard's family.

11045.descriptionId:
Goultard wore this mantle until he discovered the three sisters, then he left it in the back of an old cupboard and forgot about it.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

11046.descriptionId: This cursed necklace's aura is so powerful you're having difficulty getting rid of the damned thing.

11047.descriptionId: Da Rorc has given himself up, escort him to Lethaline.

11048.descriptionId: A simple map and an intelligence potion. Even Dark Vlad should be able to escape from his maze with that.

11049.descriptionId:
Slap this hat on your head, peel it for a few hours, and eventually, if you're lucky, you might find a tiny pip.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

11050.descriptionId:
The cape, which releases a pleasant citrus aroma as you walk, will transform you into a powerful Moskito trap.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

11051.descriptionId: If you dip this amulet into your glass, your tasteless water will be transformed into a delicious, citrus-flavoured beverage.

11052.descriptionId: The soles of these boots are made from the tough skin of fruit harvested on an island whose very existence remains unknown to mere mortals.

11055.descriptionId:
Padded with Bow Meow hair and covered with bark, this hat is extremely flammable. You should not sit on it if your pants are on fire.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

11056.descriptionId:
In hot weather, this cape's scales spread open to help your sweat evaporate. When it rains, this cape's scales spread open to let the rain in and rinse your posterior.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

11057.descriptionId: This belt is composed of scales arranged spirally in accordance with the Vibronacci suite.

11058.descriptionId: Who were you hoping to seduce with a ring like this?

11071.nameId: Extract from the Origins of Goultard
11071.descriptionId: Stained, spotted and wrinkled, these few pages are almost illegible. However, through the thick layer of grime you can still make out some words. These pages are an extract from a forgotten book detailing Goultard's origins.

11077.descriptionId:
When it comes to sounding out his opponents, Lonne Jenone has more than one string to his fiddle – he uses it as a hammer. One thing is certain: sparks will fly!
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

11078.descriptionId:
This leather cape, though light, will accompany you on all your incredible rides on the back of a Dragoturkey.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

11079.descriptionId:
Before being worn by Lonne Jenone, this hat belonged to Sergeant Payper, who was a rather quiet chap rarely prone to sticking his oar in.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

11080.descriptionId: This versatile pair of boots will guarantee full freedom of movement, which is the reason that Lonne Jenone wears them when he dances with Boowolves.

11082.descriptionId: These boots were specially designed to destroy your opponents' shin pads, and then their shins, and then your own toes.

11083.descriptionId: You can use this ring to puncture the Gobbowl Ball when you want to quietly enjoy a break in play.

11084.descriptionId:
Gadget was one of the most creative handymen the World of Twelve has ever seen. Unfortunately, he was also one of the most daft. They say he mistook his wife's head for his anvil on more than one occasion, although she didn't complain, apparently.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

11085.descriptionId: If you wear this belt upside down and press on it hard enough, you may be able to activate its integrated retromagic module. It has never worked, but you can activate it anyway. Then you can then sell it on to someone even more naive than you.

11086.descriptionId:
Gadget made this cape in the hope that it might enable him to fly and thus more easily escape the beatings administered daily by his wife.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

11087.descriptionId: Worn by several generations of handymen, this ring will protect your knuckle from hammer blows. Unfortunately, it is never sold in packs of five.

11088.descriptionId:
Grillian was a great magician. He is most famous for having reinventing the wheel, having forgotten how to manufacture them.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

11089.descriptionId:
This cape is supposed to protect your posterior from carnivorous plant bites.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

11090.descriptionId: This is a wanted notice for Lethaline Sigibul.

11091.descriptionId: Grillian the magician traded a magic ring for this pair of boots. It seems that he lost out on the deal, as they aren't even padded.

11092.descriptionId: Grillian wore this amulet around his neck when... when... Oh, what does it matter? He died, and now this amulet is yours.

11100.descriptionId:

11102.descriptionId: Hardened to Frigost's harsh climate, this flower is much more resistant than its delicate appearance would suggest. That said, to preserve the alchemic properties of such a rare plant, it must be handled carefully when harvested.

11103.descriptionId: This enormous sack contains an impressive quantity of Snowdrops.

11104.descriptionId: In levels of sheer idiocy, the Tofu, the Gobball and even the Iop can't hold a candle to the Quaquack.

11105.descriptionId: This Improved Quaquack Ghost hasn't left the living world yet. Will you find a way to resurrect it or cowardly abandon it once and for all?

11106.descriptionId: Spines as sharp as Bworker's blades, scales as thick as Soft Oak bark, and eyes as black as Crobak feathers. This fish may be formidable, but served up on a plate it is quite simply delicious.

11107.descriptionId: This tree appears to tremble when you touch it. After all the axe blows you've dealt it, it's not surprising it's scared of you.

11109.descriptionId: What's surprising about this cereal is that, in addition to its resistance to Frigost's extreme climate, it gives any milk it comes into contact with a delicate chocolatey flavour.

11110.descriptionId: Hard enough to scratch glass and dark enough to sap your morale, this rock has lost all of the heat of the lava from which it came. It would be perfect as a tombstone, as long as it's not your own.

11111.descriptionId: This enormous sack contains an impressive quantity of Icefish.

11112.descriptionId: This enormous sack contains an impressive quantity of Aspen Wood.

11113.descriptionId: This enormous sack contains an impressive quantity of Frosteez.

11114.descriptionId: This enormous sack contains an impressive quantity of Obsidian.

11115.descriptionId: Spring is here, you can smell it. Well, it's either Spring or the rotten Uridnac that's attached to you.

11116.descriptionId:
This little fish is very fond of people and attaches itself to them easily.
However, its biological rhythm is peculiar: it is only active in the month of Aperirel when Silouate warms the fresh water where the fish thrives.

11117.descriptionId: Mastogobs need to be shorn once a year, just like the armpits of Pikokos.

11118.descriptionId: There isn't the tiniest piece of edible meat left on this bone, so there's no point you gnawing on it.

11119.descriptionId: Frigostians normally eat these ears with vinaigrette because they taste awful, and Frigostians love vinaigrette.

11122.descriptionId: The most reckless Frigostians have fun with sleeping Mastogob Warriors by attempting to throw three metallic rings around each of their horns without waking them up. Unsurprisingly, no one has ever made it to the end of the game alive.

11123.descriptionId: You pulled this tooth from the jaw of a still-living Mastogob. What's wrong with you? Are you crazy, or something?

11124.descriptionId: These entrails froze as soon the second you pulled them from the body cavity you found them in.

11125.descriptionId: As if it wasn't bad enough already that he has no arms, what's going to happen to the Pingwin whose foot you tore off?

11126.descriptionId: How can a skull be ethereal? Having thought about it a lot, you find yourself laughing at the answer to that question.

11127.descriptionId: This tear symbolises resilience in the face of oppression.

11128.descriptionId: Instead of wetting, this tear burns any combustible material it comes into contact with, so there's no risk of your makeup running when your boyfriend leaves you for his Dragoturkey.

11129.descriptionId: Extract of Snowfoux musk is enormously popular with the female Snowfoux population, and makes a great gift for your suitors or rivals.

11130.descriptionId: This lump of lichen was frozen solid by the cold. Once defrosted, you can use it in a Frigostian variant of Black Pudding Pizza.

11131.descriptionId: You'd have to be a real dork not to understand how useful an item like this is.

11132.descriptionId: Because you stole his spoon, that poor bear has to use his fingers to eat. You're a monster.

11133.descriptionId: Following the example set by the Royal Tofu, certain Pingwins grow a vibrating feather that is chock-full of magic. As for its usefulness...

11134.descriptionId: There's something trapped in this cube of ice cut from Frigost's Frozen Lake. You've got two options if you want to find out what it is: wait until the ice melts, or, like any self-respecting brat, hit it until it shatters.

11136.descriptionId: It's dirty, but venerable. Kinda reminds you of someone.

11137.nameId: A lump of Faded Stunted Rat
11137.descriptionId: This is all that remains of the Stunted Rats from Grandfather's cellar. You certainly didn't pull any punches, did you?

11138.descriptionId: Nope, that's not a Mastogob Brain you're holding in your hand, it's a Pea Seed. The difference is obvious: the Pea Seed is cold to the touch.

11139.descriptionId: Emmer is an ancient version of the wheat that is currently cultivated in Amakna. Anyone would think time stands still on Frigost.

11140.descriptionId: Once used as flour for biscuits, the cultivation of this seed was banned following a stupid bet. The former mayor of Frigost bet an Ecaflip that he would only eat one cookie made from Granola Flour. He lost the bet, and his fortune.

11141.descriptionId: This tiny seed comes from a mature Pynekone.

11142.descriptionId: Placing a Lentil Seed on each of your eyelids won't make you see better, but you'll certainly look more stupid than usual if anyone sees you doing it.

11143.descriptionId: Sparo wasn't worth his salt, and that's why he ended up in a barrel. Don't say you weren't warned.

11144.descriptionId: Pull the stalk out, count to two and throw this seed as far as you can. If it lands next to an Atomystique he'll explode with rage. Young militiamen finish their Grenhayde Seed training pretty quickly.

11145.descriptionId: Slum-dwelling children attack civilised people with these seeds. You may be wondering how that works, but it's better not to know, really.

11146.descriptionId: This seed has undergone a massive increase in temperature followed by extreme cooling, which has made it brittle and fragile.

11147.descriptionId: This seed has a high carbon content and when there's a full moon, it makes a strange noise. You'd have to be really stupid or a Iop to believe such nonsense.

11148.descriptionId: An old legend tells that the flour made from this seed was used for making the bread of Demon Steak sandwiches, favourite dish of the demon lord Rushu. Even today, Frigostians are wary of it.

11149.descriptionId: If you like piling on the slap, and singing in the shower, this seed is for you. Eating it will have you wiggling your hips in front of a roaring crowd. Be careful, however, as its effect is very temporary.

11150.descriptionId: If you happen to swallow this bean, it will make that time you had the McSheth seem like a magical, unicorn blessed, rainbow filled, 8 week long summer holiday.

11151.descriptionId: Vicia is a genus of about 140 species of flowering plants commonly known as vetches. It is in the legume family (Fabaceae). Among the closest living relatives of vetches are the lentils (Lens) and the true peas (Pisum). There. You'll go to sleep a little less stupid tonight.

11152.descriptionId: So you think you're funny, and blessed with a sense of humour that would make Oto Mustam laugh? You need to get yourself some new friends, the ones you have at the moment are totally insincere.

11153.descriptionId: It was written in the stars that you'd get your hands on this seed.

11154.descriptionId: This seed has the distinction of being made from honey. Mixed with Mimilk and served at breakfast time, it's a real treat.

11155.descriptionId: Who knew you could make flour from lupin beans? I certainly didn't. You learn something new every day!

11156.descriptionId: This flower was popularised by the town crier Jorg Farmboy, and all the other town criers hate him for it.

11157.descriptionId: Powdered and boiled, ingesting this tulip is recommended if you want to lose weight quickly. The disadvantage is that the weight of your wallet diminishes just as quickly.

11158.descriptionId: Discovered by the famous botanist Yosef, this rose gives off the heady scent of sweaty Frighog dung, and reminds you of your most intimate moments.

11159.descriptionId: This flower casts a shadow in the shape of an Osamodas.

11160.descriptionId: The stems of this flavoursome rhubarb are hollow, and once appropriately arranged, produce a sound when blown into that's not unlike unaccompanied vocal music characterised by consonant four-part chords for every melody note in a predominantly homophonic texture. Or so the story goes, anyway.

11161.descriptionId: The person who discovered this exquisite flower quickly went around proclaiming it to be the most beautiful ever discovered, and I, for one, wholeheartedly agree.

11162.descriptionId: A Xelor Lord of Time discovered this beautiful flower, but was tearfully forced to part with it.

11163.descriptionId: They say that this rose is blessed by the gods, something that they don't say about you.

11164.descriptionId: The petals of this hellebore smell like dry-roasted peanuts.

11165.descriptionId: There was a time when chewing this flower was fashionable amongst Iop high society. They thought it made them look smart, which might have been true, if Iops were capable of thinking.

11166.descriptionId: The name of this flower is a tribute to Sander, the famous admiral of the Frigost fleet, who died hitting his head against the walls of the house of his rival, Al Hiartus.

11167.descriptionId: The pollen of this lily has the peculiar property of bringing some people out in a terrible rash, or invoking a euphoric sense of happiness in others.

11168.descriptionId: Don't be fooled by the smell or sparkling appearance of this plant, its flavour is even worse.

11169.descriptionId: The properties of this weed are still a mystery.

11170.descriptionId: This plant is used to decorate the kitchens of boats. It's a miracle she survived the ice age.

11171.descriptionId: This plant gives off a smell that attracts hens from miles around. Fortunately, it doesn't wake you up in the morning crowing.

11172.descriptionId: When you're alone and life is making you lonely, you can always go to the pub.

11173.descriptionId: This plant smells wonderful and makes a delightful herbal tea, but you're not sure if it's supposed to taste sweet or sour. Curse your uncultured palate.

11174.descriptionId: Use this key to enter the greenhouse where the Royal Mastogob hides.

11175.descriptionId: This key contains high levels of asbestos and as a result floats very well on water and on salad dressing. You can also use it to enter the Royal Pingwin's excavation.

11176.descriptionId: Battered by the waves, this key smells of iodine and rotten seaweed, like a chain-smoking Enutrof who has let himself go. It is, however, the only way of entering the Wreck of the Hesperus.

11177.descriptionId: This worn key was once used to access the Frigost mines. Nowadays, it can be used to enter the Obsidemon's Hypogeum, where the bodies of adventures foolish enough to have crossed its path are kept nice and warm.

11178.descriptionId: It smells a bit like frozen, damp Bow Wow, but it'll get you into the Snowfoux Den.

11179.descriptionId: This strangely shaped key shines at night. So if you happen to get lost in the Petrified Forest, instead of helping you find your way, it'll help the monsters find you instead.

11180.descriptionId: Nope, it doesn't matter how hard you stare at it, you won't get an answer. This isn't the key to the gates of paradise.

11181.descriptionId: Any self-respecting Frigostian can blab on for weeks about the many virtues of honey. Rather than listen to the gassy old windbags, why don't you have a look inside the hive yourself? You might even get the chance to see the inside of a Bearbarian's stomach while you're at it.

11182.descriptionId: Well, one thing's for certain. Without his wig, the Royal Mastogob certainly loses some of his authority.

11183.descriptionId: The Royal Pingwin himself used this Icefish against you. Regardless of where it came from, however, it will just end up on the barbecue like any other Icefish.

11184.descriptionId: This may well look nothing more than a vulgar hook to you, my friend, but during the time of Buck Anear, it was considered the bleeding edge of prosthetic technology.

11185.descriptionId: As incredible as it may seem, this skull survived the ambient heat inside the Hypogeum. The same can't be said of its meeting with the Obsidemon.

11186.descriptionId: This coupon serves no purpose, pharmaceutical or not.

11190.descriptionId: If you shake this gift vigorously, you'll find that it isn't empty. Perhaps the gods are finally smiling down on you.

11191.descriptionId: Their soles may be worn but these boots are very comfortable. They have trampled the soil of the most dangerous dungeons as well as the heads of the most vicious monsters.

11192.nameId: Legend of the Dungeons Boots Gift
11192.descriptionId:
If you shake this gift vigorously, you'll find that it isn't empty. Perhaps the gods are finally smiling down on you.
This gift can only be opened on a DOFUS 2.0 server.

11193.descriptionId: A handyman could use this plank to make something delightful - a coffin, for example. Just bear that in mind.

11194.descriptionId: This flour dissolves in mimilk, giving it a delightful chocolate flavour. The inhabitants of a lost island, preferring frozen desserts, like to dissolve it in water.

11195.descriptionId: You need to get treatment before you get any worse.

11196.descriptionId: Unable to strike new currency because of a lack of metal, Frigostians carve kamas from the ice and trade them for various local items. This coin has no value outside of the island.

11197.descriptionId: The vaccination campaign against this disease has already cost Frigost Village the modest sum of 2 billion kamas and has had no significant result. The Frigostians may as well just throw their kamas out of the window.

11198.descriptionId: This vaccine provides effective protection from the Lurgi, but its effects wear off quickly. It needs to be renewed every week.

11199.descriptionId: This seed, cold to the touch, releases a powerful chocolate aroma.

11200.descriptionId: If you shake this gift box vigorously, you'll find it's not empty. Perhaps the gods are finally smiling down on you.

11201.descriptionId: You took this sample from a Mastogob suffering from the Lurgi.

11202.descriptionId: Herr Peece needs this water for his research into a cure for the Lurgi.

11203.descriptionId: This weed is well sought by alchemists, Eniripsas and Eniripsa alchemists. A plant similar to this one can be used to make a powerful liqueur popular with sailors, Enutrofs and Enutrof sailors.

11204.descriptionId: You went to great lengths to get this blood sample. Let's hope it was worth it.

11205.descriptionId: You have a meeting with Cap'n Tankerous at the inn, any time from 1am but before 4am.

11206.descriptionId: You have a meeting with Cap'n Tankerous at the inn, any time from 4am but before 7am.

11207.descriptionId: You have a meeting with Cap'n Tankerous at the inn, any time from 7am but before 10am.

11208.descriptionId: You have a meeting with Cap'n Tankerous at the inn, any time from 10am but before 1pm.

11209.descriptionId: You have a meeting with Cap'n Tankerous at the inn, any time from 1pm but before 4pm.

11210.descriptionId: You have a meeting with Cap'n Tankerous at the inn, any time from 4pm but before 7pm.

11211.descriptionId: You have a meeting with Cap'n Tankerous at the inn, any time from 7pm but before 10pm.

11212.descriptionId: You have a meeting with Cap'n Tankerous at the inn, any time from 10pm but before 1am.

11213.descriptionId: More resistant than a pair of Captain Chafer's Kriptonite Underpants, and more aggressive than a band of Astrubian Hunters, these ticks are a veritable nightmare for their host.

11214.descriptionId: This blood sample was taken from a Mastogob infected with ticks.

11215.descriptionId: This blood sample was taken from a Mastogob Warrior infected with ticks.

11216.descriptionId: This blood sample was taken from a Venerable Mastogob infected with ticks.

11217.descriptionId: This blood sample was taken from a Mastogobbly infected with ticks.

11218.descriptionId: Wogew the Hewmit has asked you to deliver this envelope to Otomai. It contains several useful documents on the ticks that live on Mastogobs, but also on Wabbits.

11219.descriptionId: The Royal Mastogob uses his tail to shoo away Moskitos during the summer months. It's completely useless for the rest of the year though, and sometimes he even forgets it's there.

11221.descriptionId: No one can say exactly when Mastogobs first arrived on Frigost. What is certain is that they've been there a long time, because certain Frigostian households still pass down Royal Mastogob Wool underwear from generation to generation, and there are several examples that date back centuries.

11223.descriptionId: In olden times, Pingwinkles only used to visit Frigost's shores for a few days during the winter, but now the island has frozen over completely, they've decided to stay - which is as good an excuse as any to steal their feathers all year round.

11225.descriptionId: It's very oily, isn't washed very often, and it shines. Nope, I'm not talking about your wig, but this Pingwobble Skin.

11226.descriptionId: This oil was extracted from a Mama Pingwin. It will take you a very long time to wipe the memory of how exactly you extracted it from your scarred mind.

11227.descriptionId: Everyone on Frigost loves to stuff their underwear with Mama Pingwin down. Some people say they do it to keep warm, but only a Iop would believe that.

11229.descriptionId: The Shaman Pingwin's Beard smells of fish and goat musk. This potent mix is used by the bravest inhabitants of Frigost as a Mastogob repellent.

11230.descriptionId: Don't be fooled by its modest size - it knows exactly where it's going.

11232.descriptionId: The Royal Pingwin is well respected by the inhabitants of Frigost, who, blinded by his noble title, think he's probably more important than he actually is, and don't hesitate to kill him as a result.

11233.descriptionId: Don't pretend you don't know exactly which hole this enormous egg came out of.

11234.descriptionId: This survivor from the Lonesome Pine Trails should be escorted to Chief Anbifketf.

11235.descriptionId: This survivor from the Lonesome Pine Trails should be escorted to Chief Anbifketf.

11236.descriptionId: This survivor from the Lonesome Pine Trails should be escorted to Chief Anbifketf.

11237.descriptionId: This survivor from the Lonesome Pine Trails should be escorted to Chief Anbifketf.

11238.descriptionId: Cromagmunks use their tails to balance when they're rolling their acorns along the floor. Cromagmunks seem impervious to ridicule.

11239.descriptionId: Cromagmunks spend the first few years of their lives looking for the best acorn possible. They spend the rest of their lives trying to remember where they've hidden it.

11240.descriptionId: A very serious, progressive scientific study has shown that the teeth of the Sabredon were the very first cause of perforated buttock amongst the Frigostian population.

11243.descriptionId: A Woolly Piggoth's skin pads its angular bones quite nicely, meaning it stays festively plump all year round.

11244.descriptionId:
I followed a hoary Mama Pingwin and she led me to her den, where hundreds of other Mama Pingwins were hiding. It's an opportunity not to be missed. I'm going to head inside and shoot anything that moves, there'll be enough meat for the next decade.
Gerard.

11245.descriptionId: Unlike those of the Moowolf, these family jewels have neither value nor purpose.

11247.descriptionId: A Frighog's ears are pierced all over. Is this because they like piercings, or is it because Jon Lemon's songs can even be heard on Frigost too?

11248.descriptionId: This ear reminds you of one of the favourite songs of young Frigostians: "Kanigloo gloo gloo, Greedoblop blop blop tadada tzum tzum". There aren't many lyrics, sure, but that way a Iop can just about memorise it.

11250.descriptionId: While they were still alive, the Mayor of Frigost's political opponents would tell anyone who would listen that she wore Woolly Bow Meow Hair lingerie.

11253.descriptionId: Before Frigost froze over, Stunted Rats were hunted for their fur, which was then sold on the Amaknian continent under the name "Exotic Kitsou Skin".

11254.descriptionId: Crabeyes are hunted by the fishermen of Frigost for two reasons: their permanent bad temper and their tendency to play jokes on the fishermen by snipping their nets with their pincers. The fishermen get their revenge, and play jokes on the crabs by snipping their pincers off.

11257.descriptionId: Frigostian schoolchildren use these feathers to write with, which is why mother Gullipops always stress to their chicks the need to accelerate when passing a school.

11258.descriptionId:
This receipt shows the date the pines were received.
Show it to Gormor the Mangler to receive your pay.

11259.descriptionId: Chief Anbifketf needs these trunks for the pipework heating system.

11260.descriptionId: This thick and sticky blubber makes an excellent fuel that burns for a long, long time - which explains why Pingwins never feel the cold.

11261.descriptionId: This list shows the missing pieces the fishermen of the Frozen Lake need to repair their equipment.

11262.descriptionId: Damar gave this ring to Valy Domidat thirty years ago.

11263.descriptionId: This fairywork produces a pleasant pyrotechnic effect for a few seconds and burns your retinas for the rest of your life.

11264.descriptionId: This Pingwin skin is in very poor condition. You won't be able to use it to make new underwear for Captain Chafer Day.

11265.descriptionId: This Pingwobble has been trained to be able to regurgitate enormous quantities of Icefish and leave them intact. The only problem is, its digestive process starts after half an hour.

11266.descriptionId: While you were fighting, your Pingwobble was eaten. This is all that's left of him.

11267.descriptionId: This discount will be applied when you rent a room in the upcoming ice hotel.

11268.descriptionId:
This old stuffed toy must belong to someone, but who?
Double-tap to use.

11269.descriptionId:
The gum is of no use to you because your breath is too bad. On the other hand, Mac Gayver, the Xelor, will find a surprising use for it.
Double-click to use.

11270.descriptionId:
This chest contains many heirlooms. In the absence of anyone else, you might be able to claim a reward from its owner.
Double-tap to use.

11271.descriptionId:
This sealed book is in poor condition. Forcing it open to read its contents may make it unusable. You'd better hire a professional, but which one?
Double-tap to use.

11272.descriptionId:
This petrified vegetal key must be for opening a petrified vegetal door in Frigost's Petrified Forest, unless it's for something else entirely. You'll have to search the area carefully.
Double-tap to use.

11273.descriptionId:
This stone, cold to the touch, vibrates constantly. What you're holding in your hands is the precious stone all Frigostian women dream about.
Double-tap to use.

11274.descriptionId:
This magnificent brooch gives off the gentle fragrance of sea air. Who will you give it to?
Double-tap to use.

11275.descriptionId:
This egg contains a Larva from the Bearbarian Hive.
Double-tap to use.

11277.descriptionId: This Pingwinkle doesn't like being adopted and will flee at the first opportunity. In the meantime, you can show it to your friends for them to abuse.

11278.descriptionId: You have defeated a Cromagmunk but unfortunately it has decided to follow you everywhere. Now you have the opportunity to find out if its bad luck is a legend or not.

11279.descriptionId: This saw is used to cut blocks of ice. It will also cut frozen limbs particularly well.

11280.descriptionId: Steel plates are very popular among Frigostians, who use them to manufacture machinery and steel pipes.

11281.descriptionId: This mask is used by workers to protect their faces in hazardous working conditions. It also protects very well from slaps and thrown dishes if you have forgotten your wife's birthday.

11282.descriptionId: These gloves protect items from your grubby little mitts. Certain Srams use them to protect their identity by hiding their fingerprints.

11283.descriptionId:
A swordsmith can create an ice saw using:
- 2 Woolly Piggoth Leathers.
- 1 Pingwin Oil.
- 2 Gullipop Feathers.
- 1 Pingwinkle Feather.
- 1 Kriptonite.
- 1 Aspen Wood.
- 5 Mastogob Wools.
- 10 Whetstones.

11284.descriptionId:
A miner can melt this plate from:
- 5 x Coal.
- 25 x Iron.
- 10 x Tin.
- 10 x Manganese.
- 5 x Cobalt.
- 1 x Aluminite.
- 1 x Sulphur Pouch.
- 1 x Mother of Pearl.

11285.descriptionId:
A tailor can make this hat from:
- 5 x Mama Pingwin Down
- 5 x Venerable Mastogob Wool
- 2 x Kanigloo Ear.
- 2 x Woolly Piggoth Leather.
- 2 x Pingwinkle Feather.
- 1 x Coal.
- 5 x Iron.
- 5 x Tin.

11286.descriptionId:
A Jeweller can make this ring from:
- 4 Pingwinkle Feathers.
- 10 Pingwobble Skins.
- 10 Shaman Pingwin Beard Hairs.
- 10 Sabredon Teeth.
- 2 Cromagmunk Tails.
- 10 Mastogobbly Ears.
- 2 Crabeye Pincers.
- 10 Woolly Bow Meow Hairs.

11288.nameId: Blueprint for a Frigostian Hornbeam Drinking Trough
11288.descriptionId:
This blueprint shows how to build a prototype drinking trough by assembling:
-1 Hornbeam Drinking Trough.
- 10 Kung-Fu Pingwin Tails.
- 10 Mama Pingwin Downs.
- 10 Kanigloo Ears.
- 10 Woolly Piggoth Leathers.
- 10 Crabeye Pincer.
- 10 Stunted Rat Fabrics.
- 10 Frighog Pierced Ears.

11289.nameId: Blueprint for a Frigostian Hornbeam Manger
11289.descriptionId:
This blueprint shows how to build a prototype manger by assembling:
- 1 Hornbeam Manger.
- 2 Pingwin Oils.
- 10 Shaman Pingwin Beard Hairs.
- 2 Frozen Acorns.
- 10 Frighog Pierced Ears.
- 10 Gullipop Feathers.
- 10 Crabeye Pincers.
- 10 Sabredon Teeth.

11290.nameId: Blueprint for a Frigostian Hornbeam Lightning Thrower
11290.descriptionId:
This blueprint shows how to build a prototype lightning thrower by assembling:
- 1 Hornbeam Lightning Thrower.
- 10 Shaman Pingwin Beard Hairs.
- 10 Pingwinkle Feathers.
- 2 Pingwin Oils.
- 10 Kanigloo Ears.
- 10 Woolly Bow Meow Hairs.
- 10 Gullipop Feathers.
- 10 Cromagmunk Tails.

11291.nameId: Blueprint for a Frigostian Hornbeam Slapper
11291.descriptionId:
This blueprint shows how to build a prototype slapper by assembling:
- 1 Hornbeam Slapper.
- 2 Pingwin Oils.
- 10 Kung-Fu Pingwin Tails.
- 10 Sabredon Teeth.
- 10 Cromagmunk Tails.
- 10 Stunted Rat Fabrics.
- 10 Woolly Bow Meow Hairs.
- 10 Pingwobble Skins.

11292.descriptionId: This prototype breeding item still requires a few tweaks before being fully functional.

11293.descriptionId: This prototype breeding item still requires a few tweaks before being fully functional.

11294.descriptionId: This prototype breeding item still requires a few tweaks before being fully functional.

11295.descriptionId: This prototype breeding item still requires a few tweaks before being fully functional.

11296.descriptionId: Here's a dose of vaccine against the Lurgi.

11297.descriptionId:
Fred, if you're reading this letter, it means I am dead. You're probably looking for my booty, so I want you to know that I will never tell you where it is hidden.
Cheers!

11298.descriptionId: Mastoslob is now in your custody and needs to be delivered safely to the Frigost Village Militia.

11299.descriptionId: Mister Penguin is now in your custody and needs to be delivered safely to the Frigost Village Militia.

11300.descriptionId: Katigger is now in your custody and needs to be delivered safely to the Frigost Village Militia.

11301.descriptionId: Pirate Bhey is now in your custody and needs to be delivered safely to the Frigost Village Militia.

11302.descriptionId: The Masked Avenger is now in your custody and needs to be delivered safely to the Frigost Village Militia.

11303.descriptionId: The YeCh'Ti is now in your custody and needs to be delivered safely to the Frigost Village Militia.

11304.descriptionId: Fuji Snowfoux is now in your custody and needs to be delivered safely to the Snowbound Village Militia.

11305.descriptionId: Dremoan is now in your custody and needs to be delivered safely to the Snowbound Village Militia.

11306.descriptionId: The following text is engraved on its pommel: "This sword steals the life of the poor and redistributes it to the rich". It's too bad you're poor.

11307.descriptionId: Az le Tech wanted to trade this treasure for his freedom with the Enutrof conqueror Sétroc. Once in his possession, Sétroc did not keep his word and executed Az le Tech. As he lay dying, he cast a curse that will befall anyone who lays their hands on this treasure.

11308.descriptionId: You stole some of Az le Tech's treasure. Look what happens to greedy people.

11309.descriptionId: Very handy for pinching the buttocks of its enemies or grabbing pickles stuck to the bottom of the jar, this claw is a Talklyka Pirate's pride and joy.

11311.descriptionId: Some pirates can't swim and so they need a buoy. They may eventually beach on the black sand beaches of Alma's Cradle after floating around for several years. Once they're back on terra firma, they're generally thirsty for revenge. But since they can't take revenge on the sea, they take revenge on the weak, as well as tourists, or just simply weak tourists.

11313.descriptionId: Any good pirate always carries a little oil to make sure their helm keeps turning smoothly.

11314.descriptionId: This shell protected the Yuara Pirate from sea spray and guano while it was sailing. Once back on dry land, the shell protects its delicate pupils from the black sandstorms of Alma's Cradle.

11315.descriptionId: Ignorant people might think this is a Spinnaker pole or a bowsprit, while any Frigostian tell you that this is a vertical spar and therefore a mast.

11317.descriptionId: The Harpy Pirate stole this shell from a powerless mollusc. It hasn't made him any more powerful so far.

11320.descriptionId: Vigi Pirates are selected for their excellent visual capacity. They are able to discern a school of tuna during a storm at night with an octopus covering their eyes, guano on their eyelids and the songs of Jon Lemon playing in the background.

11321.descriptionId: Also known as "Buck Lightyear", "Buck Aroo", "Buck Adoaboutnothing" or "Buck Off", this pirate has sailed every sea known to man and beast. The tides have decided that he should end his days on the black sand beaches of Alma's Cradle.

11322.descriptionId: Broken twice by cannon balls, three times from rolling in the sea spray, and four times having slipped on dried guano, this bone made a wealthy man of the ship's doctor, until he was eventually thrown to the sharks for dark tales of gambling, women, alcohol, insubordination, provocations to a duel, treasure theft, scuttling and mutiny. A succession of small things which eventually led to his downfall. You don't mess with Buck Anear.

11323.descriptionId: This stone was levitating around an Atomystique until you tried to avoid it, or levitate yourself - you don't know exactly what happened, but now you've got a headache and you're covered in steaming mud.

11325.descriptionId: How can a vaporous creature give rise to solid waste? This question was first asked 74 years ago during the famous Frigostian contest for the Promotion of Young Graduate Geologists. No participant was admitted that year and the issue still remains one of the Island of Frigost's most terrifying mysteries.

11327.descriptionId: This stone heart fills with steam when the Steam Crackler meets a partner. This peculiarity allows you to quickly determine if you've killed a single Steam Crackler... You just need to see if its heart floats.

11328.descriptionId: Contrary to popular belief, steam eggs are better soft-boiled.

11329.descriptionId: The Fumaroller was waving this huge stone at the end of what appeared to be his tail. He had hoped to intimidate you, until you found his weak point. Unfortunately you failed to memorise it, as your head is full of cotton wool.

11332.descriptionId: Behind this strange name hides a rock with a vascular structure. But you can just content yourself with likening it to a piece of the giant mofette you just savagely split in two.

11333.descriptionId: Even the Obsidemon itself thinks this is junk. Just don't put it in your pockets, especially those that aren't fireproof.

11334.descriptionId: This vertebra contains bone marrow that has already been cooked and is ready to be consumed. What you are holding in your hands is the precursor to an entire line of microwave ready meals.

11336.descriptionId: We don't know how the Snowfoux arrived on Frigost, but we do know that their distant cousins come from Pandala. Now you understand a little better where that frozen McSheth residue that you slept in last night came from.

11337.descriptionId: This leather is thick enough to allow the Snowfoux to withstand low, low temperatures and go sledding without hurting its bum. This fact makes you particularly jealous.

11338.descriptionId: Long used for stuffing the underwear of complex-ridden Frigostians, this wool is now known to give spots to anyone who strokes it. You have just found an excellent excuse to justify your pestilent pimples.

11339.descriptionId: It's difficult to find anything more stupid than the offspring of a Yokai Snowfoux, yet some parents seem to have succeeded. You're trying to work out what that's got to do with this Snowfoux Wool, but you can't see anything, even squinting and shaking your fists.

11341.descriptionId: Ripped straight from the body of Tengu Snowfoux, this wool is particularly warm, and will strengthen your virility if your chest wig is a little sparse.

11342.descriptionId: The completely waterproof leather was used by Frigostians to craft supple, smooth, soft containers to put things in. Some of them even claimed they didn't need to use the containers, as they were happily married.

11343.descriptionId: Rapiat manufactured these boots himself, without it costing him a kama. The same can't be said of two of his fellows, for who it cost their lives.

11344.descriptionId: To this belt's great misfortune, Rapiat's only guilty pleasure were the breads of Danioul Garnioul the Baker. He was actually the only one to continue eating them after learning they were kneaded with the feet, saying that was what gave them their unique aftertaste.

11345.descriptionId: This beautiful amber amulet actually seems to be made of a much less noble material, which explains its foul odour and its low price. But it's the result that counts, right?

11346.descriptionId: This ring helped Ougicle to stop biting his claws. To this day, it still glistens with slobber.

11347.descriptionId: In his youth, Ougicle wore his belt as a loincloth, with no trousers. He stopped the day he realised why people were laughing at him when he turned away from them.

11348.descriptionId: Ougicle especially liked his gold necklace: it amplified his cries so much that the ground around him vibrated. Very handy for flushing out Kolerats.

11349.descriptionId: Ougicle's enemies couldn't help but smile when Ougicle made their blood spurt with his sword. Even in death, some people retain their sense of humour. This weapon is still charged with Ougicle the Ouginak's magic. You may be able to use it to summon him.

11350.descriptionId: The dark Cawwot that adorns Karotz' ring isn't magic, and it's certainly not evil, it's just the same age as him.

11351.descriptionId: The Karotz Amulet is simply a luxury version of the "Wabbit-tooth Amulet", adorned with fur. Too bad it made it less powerful.

11352.descriptionId: Karotz' Boots are light and lined with fur, which makes them very comfortable. Unfortunately, as a Wabbit, he never managed to put them on.

11353.descriptionId: Kakarotz - a friend of Sangroku, and Karotz' father - gave Karotz this staff. Unlike Sangroku's staff, it can't be placed on the floor, it can only get shorter, which is not much use and is a source of inferiority complexes. This weapon is still charged with Karotz the Gwandpa Wabbit's magic. You may be able to use it to summon him.

11354.descriptionId: On the tomb erected in Grouillot's honour, it says that to avoid being burnt to death by his lamp like other Gargoyls, he extinguished his. He finally died of starvation, lost in the darkness of the Field of Heroes.

11355.descriptionId: Grouillot's stone boots slowed him down terribly in spite of the wings that were attached to him. Nobody has ever really understood why this was the case.

11356.descriptionId: Grouillot liked to make his belt speak using his talents as a ventriloquist. No one ever found out how he managed to make the tongue move without using his hands.

11357.descriptionId: Grouillot was able to kill anyone with one stroke of these daggers. But he didn't need them: his opponents died of old age before he was able to finish them off. This weapon is still charged with Grouillot the Gargoyl's magic. You may be able to use it to summon him.

11358.descriptionId: Kubitus was a very versatile Chafer: challenging him from afar meant having to face his great talent in archery, while approaching him within a dozen metres meant facing a horrible death by suffocation. Just like keeping the same boots for decades may have its advantages.

11359.descriptionId: The bone on the front of Kubitus' belt is roughly the shape of a coccyx: he thought that by having two pairs of buttocks, he would be more attractive to the fairer sex. In practice, it simply made him look ridiculous.

11360.descriptionId: This unique amulet, once animated by the same magic as that of Livitinems, insisted on calling Kubitus "Ulna". The latter, exasperated, finally muted it by tearing off its jaw.

11361.descriptionId: Kubitus was finally able to get rid of Diusse the Grossewer Rat, his archrival, with this bow. The weapon is still charged with Kubitus the Chafer Archer's magic. You may be able to use it to summon him.

11362.descriptionId: Piggy Paupe yelled so loudly when he sang that after a while, he became deaf. The magic infused into the ears of his ring helped him hear again. The snout addressed the damage caused by its stench.

11363.descriptionId: The discomfort caused by Piggy Paupe's belt tended to make him adopt a very particular gait, always swaying his pelvis forward or backward. Don't expect to garner much interest from the opposite sex, you don't look attractive, just grotesque.

11364.descriptionId: The shoe that adorns Piggy Paupe's Amulet is that of his wife and muse Yque Paupe, who bought it for him a gift. But Piggy has always thought it was more of an excuse to stop coming to his concerts than proof of love.

11365.descriptionId: When Piggy Paupe sang, he used his trident to try to amplify his voice. Not only did it never work, but it also killed him when he shook his head frantically. This weapon is still charged with Piggy Paupe the Lousy Pig Shepherd's magic. You may be able to use it to summon him.

11366.descriptionId: Rapiat was a rat so avaricious that even in grave danger he used his sword sparingly, for fear of dulling or defiling it. Seeing him fighting with his fists, sword in hand, was one of most grotesque spectacles. This weapon is still charged with Rapiat the Rat Suenami's magic. You may be able to use it to summon him.

11367.descriptionId: This syringe contains a single dose of vaccine against the Lurgi, tested and certified by Kayte Mark.

11368.descriptionId: This Mama Pingwin follows you because she has no choice, but she will flee at the first opportunity.

11369.descriptionId: This seed has been entrusted to you by Getafiks to repopulate the Lonesome Pine Trails.

11370.descriptionId: This drink is very sweet and has the distinction of being made from frozen grapes. This explains its rarity and its unique, refined taste.

11371.descriptionId: Also known as the "Mastogob grass drink", Frigrowka is said to facilitate human contact and address difficult issues. As for Frigostians, they drink it mostly because they like to drink.

11372.descriptionId:
This cape is long enough for you to be able to afford to leave blank lines between each cribbed note you've made before you take that all-important, life-changing exam.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

11373.descriptionId:
The tailor who made this hat had to use 12 powerful characteristic scrolls to craft it. Or possibly 12 sheets of toilet paper.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

11374.descriptionId: There's enough room for one of your friends to write your name on this paper amulet, which is just what breeders do so they know which Gobballs belong to them.

11375.descriptionId: This strong and rigid undergarment is not very comfortable, but then it was made with paper mache, after all. Having the saliva of a stranger on your buttocks does not seem to bother you in the slightest, I notice.

11376.descriptionId:
This huge feather cape accentuates your figure.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

11377.descriptionId:
In some tribes, the wisdom of the Chief is measured by the number of feathers on his hat. Yours has only one, and what's more, it's very small and quite grubby.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

11378.descriptionId: Lighter than conventional sandals, they have only one real drawback, they don't suit ticklish people at all.

11379.descriptionId: This amulet will tickle your neck and make you cough up that frog in your throat.

11380.descriptionId: This wounded hunter needs Herr Peece's medical expertise. At the slightest hint of a fight, he'll take refuge where you found him.

11381.descriptionId: This request was prepared by Djauns for a Sleigh for Snow Bow Wows. Before signing it, he reminded you to hurry because time is running out.

11382.descriptionId:
The last person who tried to use this cape to fly down from a cloud crashed into a bank.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

11383.descriptionId:
This hat isn't waterproof, and as a result, you'll have to use a ridiculous umbrella wherever you go.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

11384.descriptionId: Hook this ring around the neck of any children in your charge, and then connect the ring to a rope that you've hung from a tree. Now you can enjoy yourself and the children can't escape.

11385.descriptionId: Collecting this fur without damaging it was no mean feat when you take into account how badly you fought its former owner.

11386.descriptionId: These boots are perfect for dishing out punishment with your feet so that you don't have to get your hands dirty. The children will adore you!

11387.descriptionId: Escort him to Larry Tutthe so he can become his new assistant.

11388.descriptionId: This crate contains everything that Larry Tutthe needs.

11389.descriptionId: You collected this water from the Tears of Ouronigride for Ogivol Victor.

11390.descriptionId: You found this creature in a pool of mineral water in the Tears of Ouronigride. You'll pick anything up, won't you?

11391.descriptionId: This creature is developing right before your eyes! You'd better hurry up or it'll get so big you won't be able to carry it any more.

11392.descriptionId: You valiantly fought the Snowfoux. These remains are proof of your victory.

11393.descriptionId:
The striped cape belonged to a prisoner famous for his predicament.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

11394.descriptionId:
This striped hat is big enough to hide a skull, especially if it's numb.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

11395.descriptionId: This small chain could pass for an amulet were it not the tip of a padlock.

11396.descriptionId: The man who gave this belt such a stupid name is actively sought by the police. The years he'll spend in prison when they catch him still won't make up for such a lack of creativity.

11397.descriptionId:
This cloak with a ridiculous name is intriguing nonetheless, and belonged to a righteous man who claimed he wanted to clean up the streets of Brakmar. Nobody knows if he was a vigilante or a dustman.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

11398.descriptionId:
This hat will give you the allure of a Borbat. You're single at the moment, right? Yeah, you're going to stay single for quite a while.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

11399.descriptionId: This ring has the following engraved on its inside edge: "For upholders of the law who doesn't afraid of anything". Bless. Did you really think you could use it?

11400.descriptionId: The shoemaker who designed these boots fitted them with Borbat wings so that their wearer could fly. Well, it was difficult to hear anything above the obnoxious din, but that's what you thought the merchant was saying when you bought them from him at the Astrub Zaap.

11401.descriptionId:
This wooden cape grows larger when you lie. There's a good chance you'll trip over it regularly as a result.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

11402.descriptionId:
You can also use this hat as traffic cone should you have an accident while riding your Dragoturkey.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

11403.descriptionId: Transforming into a ghost pirate didn't really suit you; you're definitely not a sailor. You'll feel better in 24 hours, I'm sure.

11404.descriptionId: You've been turned into a ghost so that you can enter the Rebellious Spirit's wreck.

11406.descriptionId: Only educated people know the usefulness of this serum, which is why you haven't got a clue what it does.

11407.descriptionId: If you serve your drinks "on the rocks" and use this special ice cube, they're sure to have an unrivalled flavour and freshness.

11408.descriptionId: Do you swear to tell the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth?

11409.descriptionId: This purse contains enough kamas to help you buy a decent outfit. Given the difficulty of the job, it represents a fortune. You can't use it for anything else, sadly.

11410.descriptionId: Worn to Captain Chafer's Panty Party, this outfit will cause envy amongst men, and especially amongst women eager to taste the forbidden fruit.

11411.descriptionId: Worn to Captain Chafer's Panty Party, this dress will turn your suitors' heads and cause many a stiff neck. Your local physiotherapist will thank you.

11412.nameId: Copy of the Santho family dossier
11412.descriptionId:
This dossier contains a copy of the inheritance duty, property deeds and other paperwork belonging to the Santho family, which show, among other things, the purchase and the legacy of hundreds of acres of farmland south of Bonta. The purchases are spread between the years 551 and 555. They were made possible by the immense wealth of Edmond Santho, who made his fortune by selling huge quantities of cereals of Frigostian origin.
Currently, only one field does not belong to Raymond Santho: that of Robin Marimoni.

11413.descriptionId: The key to Heike Holo's cell.

11414.descriptionId: Heike Holo wants to escape. You must escort her to the boat bound for the Wabbit Islands.

11415.descriptionId: These documents concern the theft of cereals coming from Frigost. The Oatmenu family's boats are mentioned.

11416.descriptionId: This pair of boots was carved out of a tree trunk. Unless it's the opposite.

11417.descriptionId: This ring was made from sawdust and something very sticky, and it's better that you leave it at that.

11418.descriptionId:
Jon Lemon loved this cape to death, which explains why he wears it to each of his funerals.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

11419.descriptionId: Jon Lemon always put on these boots when he had a deposit to make in the hut at the bottom of his garden.

11420.descriptionId:
This old hat is bordering on the ridiculous, and it's how Jon Lemon earned the nickname "The Moustachioed Grandmother". That name tends to put him in a bad mood.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

11421.descriptionId:
Jon Lemon should never have used this blowpipe just after eating. Since that day he's had to use it as a simple staff and as he so often repeats, "It was better before".
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

11422.descriptionId:
If you shake this gift vigorously, you'll find that it isn't empty. Perhaps the gods are finally smiling down on you.
This gift can only be opened on a DOFUS 2.0 server.
