11458.descriptionId: As sharp as Iop's sword, this chisel can be put to many uses. Do not trim your nails with it though, you could lose a finger.

11459.descriptionId: Here's a little tip that very few people know: the chips of wood ejected by this plane make excellent Bow Meow litter.

11460.descriptionId: Made of Kanigloo Hair hardened in Mycos resin, this brush is harder than Crocabulia's scales. It seems perfect for grooming the YeCh'Ti, but nobody will ever know for sure.

11461.descriptionId: This Atomystique, who is looking at you in a very strange way, seems determined to follow you everywhere.

11462.descriptionId: A rose by any other name would smell as sweet.

11463.descriptionId: This beautifully coloured, regal rose sinks when thrown into the sea. Once recovered from the sandy depths, it must be sprayed constantly with water to stop it drying out. Flowers, eh?

11464.descriptionId: Jamie Coggut is afraid to travel alone and will run away if things go awry.

11465.descriptionId: The hair is so long that Eniripsa children could use it as a skipping rope, although they don't really have any use for a skipping rope given that they have wings.

11466.descriptionId: Gummy, sticky and stinky, this Mycos extract is completely repugnant, and yet you still can't help but dip your finger in it. Go figure.

11467.descriptionId: Bea Fortax wrote this letter to her lost fiancé Al Ive, to whom she has remained faithful for more than a century.

11468.descriptionId: A votive amulet dedicated to the worship of a forgotten goddess. It has "Protect your brothers and sisters" engraved around its edge. Well, that's goddesses for you, I guess. Always pampering spoilt brats. And what if we haven't got a brother or a sister? What are we supposed to do then, huh?

11469.descriptionId: "Notes on Dragons: teeth (huge), claws (sharp), breath (burning), greed (phenomenal). Some Dragons can predict the weather. But a dragon is more cumbersome than a frog". Where did Count Harebourg get all this information from?

11470.descriptionId: "The bearer of this ring was supposed to have been the prisoner of a Dragon. If my memory serves me correctly, a Dragon has never been known to hold somebody against their will. It's so easy for a Dragon to make a good barbecue, why would they bother?"- A quote from Count Harebourg

11471.descriptionId: "The wearer of these boots held a grudge against a Dragon. Don't be like him, and make sure you give Dragons the ancestral respect they deserve. And remember that Dragons are big. Very big. And they have no sense of humour."- A quote from Count Harebourg

11472.descriptionId: "This cape is supposed to protect the wearer from the dreams and illusions of the ethereal dimension. Does it really work? We would need to be able to come and go through the dimensions to get to the bottom of it. Apart from Magus Ax on his good days (or the days when he's had a drink or two), not many people have ever boasted about doing so." - A quote from Count Harebourg.

11473.descriptionId: Count Harebourg has engraved the following on this belt: "Whoever wears this belt may pass through time and space!" Theoretical speculation? One thing is certain – it stops your trousers falling down. That's something at least.

11474.descriptionId: "In case of disturbance in the astral veil, pull this over your head pretty quickly". A safety note engraved by Count Harebourg himself! You don't know what an astral veil is, but having slipped this out-of-the-ordinary hat onto your not-quite-as-out-of-the-ordinary head, you're ready to race off on an adventure, or into a wall!

11475.descriptionId: This water, kept in an unstable state of supercooling, is mainly used to instantly freeze any type of food. Some unscrupulous Frigostians say it also works very well with mothers-in-law.

11476.descriptionId:
This leg is so big and fat, it could be one of yours. The only difference is that, unlike yours, it isn't covered with hair.

(This meat can be harvested by level-100 Hunters.)

11477.descriptionId:
This leg is so big and fat, it could be one of yours. The only difference is that, unlike yours, it isn't covered with warts.

(This meat can be harvested by level-100 Hunters.)

11478.descriptionId:
Nothing like a trip into the woods to cut down innocent creatures. This cube of meat would have been a lump if you weren't so obsessive-compulsive.

(This meat can be harvested by level-100 Hunters.)

11479.descriptionId:
What remains of a Pingwin once its skin, entrails and bones have been turned into animal feed? Nothing, other than this exquisitely tender flesh.

(This meat can be harvested by level-100 Hunters.)

11480.descriptionId:
What remains of a Royal Pingwin once its crown and Snapper have been stolen? This flesh, that's all. You stole the rest, remember?

(This meat can be harvested by level-100 Hunters.)

11481.descriptionId:
It's a pity that this Snowfoux meat didn't come out of its defunct owner already frozen. That would have saved you some time.

(This meat can be harvested by level-100 Hunters.)

11482.descriptionId:
This meat is almost completely frozen solid. Almost, but not totally. You still need to take it to a workshop to prepare it.

(This meat can be harvested by level-100 Hunters.)

11483.descriptionId: You know how Donna Kerbabben's favourite saying is "If it isn't for frying, it isn't worth trying"? Well, for Frigostians it's "If it isn't frozen, it won't be chosen".

11484.descriptionId: You know how Donna Kerbabben's favourite saying is "If it isn't for frying, it isn't worth trying"? Well, for Frigostians it's "If you freeze, you're sure to please".

11485.descriptionId: It looks like an Apewicube made from Sabredon Meat, which is your favourite, as it's the one that smells least rancid.

11486.descriptionId: Reduced to a heap of flesh and encased in ice, that Pingwin isn't so smart now, is he?

11487.descriptionId: Reduced to a heap of flesh and encased in ice, that Royal Pingwin isn't so smart now, is he?

11488.descriptionId: Once frozen, Snowfoux Meat can be stored for years. Some Enutrofs wanted to test this method, but out of fear of being stuck with them for years, the ice preferred to melt.

11489.descriptionId: As hard as the skull of a Iop and as cold as the eyes (and heart) of a Sram, this frozen meat can be preserved for a century. The question is, was it was ever edible?

11490.descriptionId: Any wiry, black, curly hairs you find sticking out of this roast haven't come from the Mastogob, oh no. They belong to your sweetheart.

11491.descriptionId: Sink your teeth into this leg and you'll feel like you're biting your mother-in-law. You'll ask for more, though, just you wait and see.

11492.descriptionId: Recommended by the militiamen of Frigost, this cube of meat is the perfect thing to get you back on your feet after a difficult fight.

11493.descriptionId: Just enjoy the gritty crunch, it tastes just like chicken!

11494.descriptionId: This dish smells of gamey meat and rotten fish, but what did you expect? You were warned not to reheat defrosted food.

11495.descriptionId: Eat this meat at every meal for a month and you'll be fat enough to serve as an appetiser for the YeCh'Ti.

11496.descriptionId: What doesn't kill you makes your stronger, which you'll be living testament to if you survive the terrible indigestion this meat provokes.

11497.descriptionId: This oil is good for preserving food and ideal for massages, lending a slight scent of chocolate to all your meals.

11498.descriptionId: Use this meat on the Lonesome Pine Trails to make a starving Sabredon appear.

11499.descriptionId: Lighter and sweeter than conventional Frosteez, this cereal will make you roar with pleasure if you eat it with mimilk.

11500.descriptionId: Unlike traditional Icefish, Frozen Icefish is already frozen (the clue is in the name I guess), which means it can be kept for longer.

11501.descriptionId: This rare flower is named in remembrance of a boy named Savo who swore his love to a shepherdess, using the stars as his witnesses. He gave her a bouquet of these flowers before leaving for Frigost Village where he became a chimney sweep and perished in a fire.

11502.descriptionId: This flour has the distinction of not blowing away when blown on, which is a very useful characteristic when faced with gassy children and blundering Iops.

11503.descriptionId: This bread is the staple food of Frigostians, which explains why they've withstood the famine for nearly a century.

11504.descriptionId: This bread is the staple food of Frigostian aristocrats, which explains why their first bowel movement of the day comes earlier than that of their less aristocratic peers.

11505.descriptionId: This unpalatable potion will force you to make a crucial choice between drinking it to save your life in agony, or dying but suffering less.

11506.descriptionId: This potion will carry you away from the spirit realm, and get you back on your feet.

11507.descriptionId: Use this potion to travel to the stars without leaving your house. Certain gullible Frigostians even claim that it brings good luck.

11508.descriptionId: Once gutted, Icefish look a lot less dangerous.

11509.descriptionId: Once gutted, Icefish look a lot less dangerous.

11510.descriptionId: Once you taste it, you won't be able to do without it.

11511.descriptionId: They say that eating Frozen Icefish makes you smarter. Yet another story told to young Iops to make them eat Icefish.

11512.descriptionId:
Awarded to the victor of a certain number of duels, this gem contains the soul of a monster.
Keep in a cool, dry, dark place, away from strong odours. Shake well before use.

11513.descriptionId:
Awarded to the victor of a certain number of duels, this gem contains the soul of a monster.
Keep in a cool, dry, dark place, away from strong odours. Shake well before use.

11514.descriptionId: With this weapon in your clenched fist, you will cry for vengeance and seek justice. Get your revenge on who? Seek justice for what? It looks like the answers to these questions do not belong to this Age.

11516.descriptionId: A piece of fabric that's colder than a Goblin in the middle of Descendre. One of two things: either your opponent delved into some seedy magic, you know, the strange dimensional kind, or he liked to go for a walk early in the morning. One thing's for certain: he wasn't faint hearted.

11517.descriptionId: A shard of glass that looks pretty ordinary at first glance, but if you look closely, you can see scrolling images on its roughened surface. Memories? They look like events that took place nearly a century ago. This shard was part of a much larger piece, that's for certain.

11518.descriptionId: A seemingly innocuous stone, but completely frozen, right to the very heart of the rock. Even around the frozen island of Frigost, such a thing is strange. Even an Ice Kwak couldn't accomplish such a feat! So who has such power? And how did they get it? A mystery.

11519.descriptionId: Less hairy than the ears of a Stabba, this one at least has the advantage of being clean.

11521.descriptionId: If it weren't for the fact that this eye was still stuck to the lens of the Asploda's goggles, you might have been able to swallow it. What a shame.

11522.descriptionId: Count Harebourg was quite clear: "It's there for sure, under your nose! Just a few pickaxe blows away. Keep looking." So the Goblins tirelessly continued to seek the true nugget of Sakai, deemed to be bigger than the fist of a Trool and heavier than a bowl of Kerbabben Salad. How could such a stone go unnoticed on such a small island?

11525.descriptionId: This bone appears to have suffered several fractures, most probably from the pickaxe blows of other Goblins whose vocabulary is often limited to "Grüüüp" and "Oukk", and whose sentences are punctuated by pickaxe blows.

11527.descriptionId: There's a Goblin shopping list written on this skin in adventurer blood: "Beer, Meat, Beer" - everything needed for a successful party. You should keep it.

11529.descriptionId: This stomach was very firmly attached to its former owner, but then it does take a huge amount of guts to pilot the Bomma's incredible machine.

11531.descriptionId: Clearly this is a rarity. Finding a Drilla Brain in a Drilla skull is like looking for a needle in a haystack or an ant tooth a bag of rice.

11533.descriptionId: Gobshells are mechanical creatures, so it is illusory to think that they hatch from eggs. If one follows the logic of the Goblins, their eggs must also be mechanical. You suddenly understand why Goblins are at the bottom of the ladder in the animal kingdom, right next to Larvae.

11534.descriptionId: This ticket shows when your last battle took place in the cellar of the Frigostian Paradise Tavern.

11535.descriptionId: This ticket shows that you'll walk off with 1,000 kamas if you win.

11536.descriptionId: This ticket shows that you'll walk off with 2,000 kamas if you win.

11537.descriptionId: This ticket shows that you'll walk off with 3,000 kamas if you win.

11538.descriptionId: This ticket shows that you'll walk off with 4,000 kamas if you win.

11539.descriptionId: This ticket shows that you'll walk off with 5,000 kamas if you win.

11540.descriptionId: This soap was once sold by Tyler Dendur, who perished in a dynamite explosion attempting to blow up Frigost Town Hall. Above all else, the Frigostians remember the magnificent fireworks that followed his death.

11541.descriptionId: If you shake this gift box vigorously, you'll find it's not empty. Perhaps the gods are finally smiling down on you.

11542.descriptionId: This sealed letter is for one of Tyler's former disciples.

11543.descriptionId: You'll obtain a Firestone if you crush this Fragment with the three other Fire Fragments.

11544.descriptionId: You'll obtain a Firestone if you crush this Fragment with the three other Fire Fragments.

11545.descriptionId: You'll obtain a Firestone if you crush this Fragment with the three other Fire Fragments.

11546.descriptionId: You'll obtain a Firestone if you crush this Fragment with the three other Fire Fragments.

11547.descriptionId: You'll obtain an Earthstone if you crush this Fragment with the three other Earth Fragments.

11548.descriptionId: You'll obtain an Earthstone if you crush this Fragment with the three other Earth Fragments.

11549.descriptionId: You'll obtain an Earthstone if you crush this Fragment with the three other Earth Fragments.

11550.descriptionId: You'll obtain an Earthstone if you crush this Fragment with the three other Earth Fragments.

11551.descriptionId: You'll obtain a Waterstone if you crush this Fragment with the three other Water Fragments.

11552.descriptionId: You'll obtain a Waterstone if you crush this Fragment with the three other Water Fragments.

11553.descriptionId: You'll obtain a Waterstone if you crush this Fragment with the three other Water Fragments.

11554.descriptionId: You'll obtain a Waterstone if you crush this Fragment with the three other Water Fragments.

11555.descriptionId: You'll obtain an Airstone if you crush this Fragment with the three other Air Fragments.

11556.descriptionId: You'll obtain an Airstone if you crush this Fragment with the three other Air Fragments.

11557.descriptionId: You'll obtain an Airstone if you crush this Fragment with the three other Air Fragments.

11558.descriptionId: You'll obtain an Airstone if you crush this Fragment with the three other Air Fragments.

11559.descriptionId: This stone is elemental energy, solidified and concentrated.

11560.descriptionId: This stone is elemental energy, solidified and concentrated.

11561.descriptionId: This stone is elemental energy, solidified and concentrated.

11562.descriptionId: This stone is elemental energy, solidified and concentrated.

11563.descriptionId: Proudly sporting this amulet around your neck will demonstrate your mastery of all four primordial elemental energies. It will not make you any wealthier, however.

11564.descriptionId: You tore this clump of hair from your enemy with your teeth.

11565.descriptionId: One of the inventory documents written by Nikos Mahdman, Count Harebourg's Superintendent.

11566.descriptionId: This fluffy little creature is fragile but very cute. However, you saw his true nature in the other world. Never again will you laugh at young wild boar.

11567.descriptionId: This method of transport is uncomfortable, that's for sure, but it's the only method you've found for crossing the barrier between Barnaby's worlds. (Double-tap to use.)

11568.descriptionId: Even if you don't start eating it for another hundred years, you will finish this pizza well before Rattedaugue has successfully made Gonztipay laugh.

11569.descriptionId: The crimes you committed and the date on which you were locked up are written on these papers.

11570.nameId: A copy of the pipeline plans
11570.descriptionId: This is a pretty accurate copy of the plan of the pipelines that run near Bambelle's sawmill.

11571.descriptionId: This hat's horns sit directly against the temples of the brave adventurer who dares to wear it. As a result, they resonate at the same frequency as the brain's alpha waves, allowing the wearer to communicate with distant Gullipops without needing to open their mouth or ears, which comes in very handy when trying to infiltrate a tribe of the googly-eyed creatures.

11572.descriptionId: The four huge, glowing balls that adorn this crown are considered by some Frigostian Pingwin experts to be a somewhat graphic representation of the Royal Pingwin's incredible fertility. Where do they get these hare-brained ideas?

11573.descriptionId: Buck Anear wore this hat on the Hesperus to show he was the boss. It didn't stop his loyal crew members nicknaming him "The Prat in the Hat", "Hattie Jacques", "Sonia Head" or, worst of all, "Octopus Tule".

11574.descriptionId: You have to admit, this helmet doesn't make you look very clever. The problem is that without it, you look even less so.

11575.descriptionId: The first thing your opponent noticed before stealing this necklace was how sparkly it was. Funnily enough, that was also the last thing you noticed as your head went tumbling to the floor.

11576.descriptionId: In olden days, Frigostian jewellers used to offer some very good advice when they had heavy pieces of jewellery on sale: place a heavy piece of jewellery around your sweetheart's neck, and it will stop her going too far away.

11577.descriptionId: A legend tells of a motley band of Frigostian cowards who tried to throw this ring into the crater of a volcano to destroy it. Fortunately for you, they failed.

11578.descriptionId: Buck Anear loved hugs and manly handshakes and sometimes both at the same time. Unfortunately for those he loved, he regularly forgot that he was armed with a huge, rusty hook. By dint of scratching, stinging, pinching, cutting or poking out the eyes of his family, he inherited the following nicknames: "Joshua Lackhand", "Hooky Hooky Hookface" or often just simply "Hook Off".

11579.descriptionId: In olden days, Frigostian jewellers used to offer some very good advice when they had lighter pieces of jewellery on sale: don't give your sweetheart jewellery which is too heavy for her hands, or she could have trouble cleaning the top of your shelves.

11580.descriptionId: This cloak would have made a beautiful blanket for a bed had the tailor who crafted it not slept in a hammock.

11581.descriptionId: A little rigid, a little heavy and from a completely different era, this cloak reminds you of a former colleague you used to break rocks with down in the mine.

11582.descriptionId: If you run through the snow wearing these boots, you'll leave Royal Mastogob-sized footprints behind. The only thing missing will be the print of a Royal Mastogob-sized tail.

11583.descriptionId: These boots won't give you a very graceful gait. But since you've never had a graceful gait anyway, no one's going to notice.

11584.descriptionId: This belt was formerly used as a chastity belt, which is quite surprising when you consider how fond Royal Mastogobs are of putting their dungeon keys in a bowl and having a big party.

11585.descriptionId: This belt can also be worn as a loincloth. Without it, Buck Anear wouldn't have been able to hide his most precious, envied and coveted jewel. Sailors jealous of his enormous treasure nicknamed him, for reasons known only to themselves, the "crooked visionary" or the "ravaging buccaneer". When he was hung for the thirteenth time, he cried out to the crowd, "My treasure for someone who understands!"

11586.descriptionId: Just like any real self-respecting pirate ghost, Buck Anear had a sabre to cut knots, heads, and the heads of knots. But he was so sensitive he couldn't stop himself shedding a tear when he did so. His opponents who lost their heads used this anecdote before dying to give him the nickname "The Sobbing Sabre".

11587.descriptionId: Use this key to get into the Archives Room.

11588.descriptionId: This key will open Valy Domidat's wardrobe. It might also work on her chastity belt, but you don't have time to try.

11589.descriptionId: Automatically equips a pre-configured set of items.

11590.descriptionId: This book is in terrible condition and looks pretty ancient - like its content, for that matter. If you read it, you'll certainly know more about Frigost than your rucksack. Well, if you'd arrived a century earlier, perhaps.

11591.descriptionId: An extract of Hazieff Taroun's memoirs.

11592.descriptionId: Frigostine gave you this receipt for the Frosteez.

11593.descriptionId: Jon Burrowman gave you this receipt for the Snowdrops.

11594.descriptionId: Clarisse Tocate gave you this receipt for the Icefish.

11595.descriptionId: Laurent Gebleuh gave you this receipt for the Obsidian.

11596.descriptionId: Al Shab gave you this receipt for the meats.

11597.descriptionId: Chief Anbifketf gave you this receipt for the Aspen Wood.

11598.descriptionId: You know that name they call you in the guild? No? Oh well, wearing this helmet, you'll soon find out.

11599.descriptionId: It's no secret that Frighogs like to make a pig of themselves. Now you can justify doing the same thing.

11600.descriptionId: It's difficult to say if the Yuara Pirate deliberately chose this mask or was the victim of a very violent maritime accident with a sea shell. It's also difficult to say who is the worst-off - the shell or the pirate.

11601.descriptionId: Occasionally called a "limpet head", the Harpy Pirate doesn't like seafood jokes, and he likes jokes involving seafood and his mother even less.

11602.descriptionId: Pope Ory was a Frigostian renowned for hiding anything and everything in his hat, but above all, anything. His hat had much in common with a female adventurer's handbag: they're the only containers whose contents exceed their capacity, defying all known laws of modern Frigostian physics.

11603.descriptionId: This hat only goes with blonde hair. It's a bit tatty, and you should be able to exchange it for a new one with Juss Tafinger's Assistant at the Ski Maker's shop in Frigost Village.

11604.descriptionId: The tailor who made this hat was convinced that the future of Frigost would be very dark. Like all naysaying doom-mongers and their half-baked predictions, he was wrong. The future of Frigost was just cold.

11605.descriptionId: Naive Frigostian tailors believe this cape to be an improved version of the famous Cape Rice. There's an inscription on its label: "This cape takes its name from its ability to become transparent around the posterior should the latter be somewhat on the large side". You've just realised that everyone can see your buttocks.

11606.descriptionId: This cape attracts attention and provides a diversion. If you are ordered to wear it on a battlefield, you'll be able to more accurately estimate your life expectancy.

11607.descriptionId: A bard called Konan Bleating wore this chain when he was younger. All his fans wore the same chain. If you decide to do the same, don't be surprised if even the monsters in Incarnam mock your taste in music.

11608.descriptionId: The maintenance and upkeep of this life-saving talisman is funded by the generous participants of Blop Eater appeals.

11609.descriptionId: Every time you scratch your neck, this amulet will make your vocal cords vibrate and you'll make the following noise: "Dzoing Dzoing". If that doesn't help you attract a mate, there's nothing more we can do for you.

11610.descriptionId: There's no doubt about it. This loincloth belonged to at least one Kanigloo, maybe several. One less, now. However, it appears badly made. You should be able to exchange it for a better one with Juss Tafinger's Assistant at the Ski Maker's shop in Frigost Village.

11611.descriptionId: These pants are best worn with long hair and come with an ash tray and plectrum. Before Frigost's big freeze, they were very popular with the angry young rebels who cut the grass for their own personal consumption. They were almost certainly Mastogob breeders looking to feed their pets.

11612.descriptionId: If you look directly at these pants, moving your head from right to left for several days, you might eventually manage to fall asleep.

11617.descriptionId: These boots are meant to be worn by Frigostians whose parents were Frigostians whose parents were Frigostians and whose parents of their parents of their parents were Frigostians. If you're not Frigostian yourself, we wouldn't recommend you put these boots on.

11618.descriptionId: Legend has it that these sandals are named after a great Frigostian mathematician called Hannibal Gorithm. He always wore sandals, even after the big freeze. He used to walk around in circles in the snow until he found the solution to stopping walking - which was when his toes turned blue.

11619.descriptionId: You'll soon be able to match these sandals to the colour of your hair or the flag you're carrying at your next battle against a Perceptor.

11620.descriptionId: This ring could have prevented some of Buck Anear's maritime disappointments. Instead of having to drink from a cup, he would have been able cut open bottles of Cocalane, the famous beverage that makes everything go by in a blur.

11621.descriptionId: If you don't place it on a finger, this ring will wander off on its own accord. It may also provide you with an excuse if you have wandering hands and can't stop shoving your fingers places you really shouldn't.

11622.descriptionId: The Frigostian artisan who made this ring almost died of exhaustion trying to write something interesting on its label. He preferred to "move on to something else". Which, translated into Frigostian means, "go on a pub crawl around all the taverns in Frigost Village".

11623.descriptionId: This typically Frigostian creation was made by an artisan whose blood never ran cold, not even in his hands.

11624.descriptionId: The blade of this sabre has been specially designed to cut your adversary's braces. Once their breeches are around their ankles, you can easily make them trip over or simply humiliate them by making your mocking laugh the last thing they ever hear.

11625.descriptionId: This axe was a favourite of the butchers of Frigost who wanted to chop the meat into such small pieces that no one would notice their esteemed customers were being sold Gullipop cloacae. This practice would actually go a long way to explaining the prejudices against Frigostian gastronomy.

11626.descriptionId: It's difficult to tell if this is an axe or an anchor. The Talklyka Pirate himself doesn't know the answer to that question. When in doubt, he uses it like an axe on all adventurers he encounters.

11627.descriptionId: This bow uses very simple Frigostian mathematics to calculate the height of certain buildings very efficiently. Unfortunately, it gives no indication of the units of measurement used for the result.

11628.descriptionId: This shovel belonged to a bard. His avant-garde approach to music - pressing the keys of his instrument with a shovel - was not rapturously received by the inhabitants of Frigost Village.

11629.descriptionId: These daggers belonged to a famous Sram who loved to show off in front of the village braves. He was renowned for his many Cider Juggling Championship titles. Cider Juggling is a pretty stupid game which consists of drinking alcohol at a friend's house, attempting to pick up a piece of wood and tipping as much liquid as possible onto the floor of the one hosting the game. A game wholeheartedly sponsored by Frigostian carpet shop owners.

11630.descriptionId: This hammer was built for the sole purpose of being able to give the YeCh'Ti a good walloping. It was slightly diverted from its original purpose when the people of Frigost found out that it works very well on all creatures that have one or more of the following characteristics: long hair, herring breath, a stupid gait, or a baleful eye. Now you understand why you were hit with this hammer in the past.

11631.descriptionId: The Vigi Pirate had a fairly unique approach to fighting. She began by describing her hammer like this: "It's heavy, it hurts and it floats". Her attackers then posed the following question: "It floats? So what?". This left the Vigi Pirate with enough time to crush her adver...*splat*

11632.descriptionId: This wand was crafted by a Frigostian expert in discretion and stealth. The user manual reads: "If you've managed to surprise your enemy by sneaking up behind them to give them a good wanding in just the right part of their backside but are suddenly overcome with the desire to sneeze, quickly push this wand into your odd nostril and count to three." You have to pay extra for the accompanying manual that explains how to tell which one of your nostrils is the odd one.

11633.descriptionId: Everyone knows that the most successful staves are the hardest ones. What can you do with a soft staff, a staff you can't hold? Probably the same thing you do with a soft wand.

11634.descriptionId: It's difficult to believe that this staff's magic comes from the decaying fish head that adorns its extremity. The mystery behind all this should also help to explain the clever ideas coming out of yours.

11635.descriptionId: This stick, equipped with a sharpened piece of shell, can be used as a lance, a harpoon, a javelin, a tent peg or even used to gut your dinner. Just don't ask a Harpy Pirate for a demonstration.

11636.descriptionId: While his men waited to share the loot contained in the Hesperus's chests, Buck Anear spent hours working out which key on this bunch went with which particular chest. His men, fed up of waiting, went off to do something else, which meant Buck Anear could keep everything for himself.

11637.descriptionId: You're finding it difficult to keep hold of this slippery rune. When used correctly, it'll help you get out of difficult situations.

11638.descriptionId: You're finding it difficult to keep hold of this very slippery rune. When used correctly, it'll help you get out of difficult situations.

11639.descriptionId: You're finding it difficult to throw this sticky rune away. It's magical properties will allow you to keep in contact with your enemies.

11640.descriptionId: You're finding it difficult to throw this very sticky rune away. It's magical properties will allow you to keep in contact with your enemies.

11641.descriptionId: You feel more energetic with this rune in your hand. Use it to avoid any kind of lethargy.

11642.descriptionId: You feel much more energetic with this rune in your hand. Use it to avoid any kind of lethargy.

11643.descriptionId: This rune's magic gives you the urge to run. Great for some good times during your morning jog.

11644.descriptionId: This rune's powerful magic gives you the urge to run. Great for some good times during your morning jog.

11645.descriptionId: This rune provokes a kind of lethargy. Powdered, it can be used to send your enemies to sleep.

11646.descriptionId: This rune provokes a kind of deep lethargy. Powdered, it can be used to send your enemies to sleep.

11647.descriptionId: Normally used to treat heavy legs, this rune's effect has been reversed. Basically, don't expect to run like a Tofu when you use it.

11648.descriptionId: Normally used to treat heavy legs, this rune's effect has been reversed. Basically, don't expect to run like a Dragoturkey when you use it.

11649.descriptionId: This rune coats the soles of your shoes with a fine layer of ice. To be used for winter sports or jokes in poor taste.

11650.descriptionId: This rune coats the soles of your shoes with a layer of ice. To be used for winter sports or jokes in poor taste.

11651.descriptionId: Crampons have appeared on the soles of your shoes, which is very useful if you want to avoid hurting yourself should you slip over. Ridiculous at a ball, however. It's up to you when you use this rune.

11652.descriptionId: Large crampons have appeared on the soles of your shoes, which is very useful if you want to avoid hurting yourself should you slip over. Ridiculous at a ball, however. It's up to you when you use this rune.

11653.descriptionId: Your senses have been heightened since you came into possession of this rune. It will allow you to accomplish even more extraordinary feats.

11654.descriptionId: Your senses have been strongly heightened since you came into possession of this rune. It will allow you to accomplish even more extraordinary feats.

11655.descriptionId: Inexplicably, you think this rune is a good luck charm. Perhaps it will help you avoid a spell's ill-effects.

11656.descriptionId: Inexplicably, you think this rune is an effective good luck charm. Perhaps it will help you avoid a spell's ill-effects.

11657.descriptionId: Associated with Earth, this rune will definitely strengthen your mastery of this element.

11658.descriptionId: Strongly associated with Earth, this rune will definitely strengthen your mastery of this element.

11659.descriptionId: Associated with Fire, this rune will definitely strengthen your mastery of this element.

11660.descriptionId: Strongly associated with Fire, this rune will definitely strengthen your mastery of this element.

11661.descriptionId: Associated with Water, this rune will definitely strengthen your mastery of this element.

11662.descriptionId: Strongly associated with Water, this rune will definitely strengthen your mastery of this element.

11663.descriptionId: Associated with Air, this rune will definitely strengthen your mastery of this element.

11664.descriptionId: Strongly associated with Air, this rune will definitely strengthen your mastery of this element.

11665.descriptionId: Not associated with any particular element, this rune will nevertheless strengthen the resolve of the indecisive when making a decision, which is paradoxical.

11666.descriptionId: Not associated with any particular element at all, this rune will nevertheless strengthen the resolve of the indecisive when making a decision, which is paradoxical.

11667.descriptionId: These boots are meant to be worn by Frigostians whose parents were Frigostians whose parents were Frigostians and whose parents of their parents of their parents were Frigostians. If you're not Frigostian yourself, we wouldn't recommend you put these boots on.

11668.descriptionId: Awarded to the victor of a certain number of duels, this gem contains the soul of a monster. Keep in a cool, dry, dark place, away from strong odours. Shake well before use.

11669.descriptionId: Awarded to the victor of a certain number of duels, this gem contains the soul of a monster. Keep in a cool, dry, dark place, away from strong odours. Shake well before use.

11670.descriptionId:
The smell and appearance of this meat perfectly evoke the massacre of Mopeats on Otomai Island in Octolliard 637.

(This meat can be harvested by level-90 and higher Hunters.)

11671.descriptionId:
The advantage of Woolly Bow Meow meat is that you can stroke it safely without being bitten or scratched.

(This meat can be harvested by level-90 and higher Hunters.)

11672.descriptionId:
This piece of meat gives off a smell of guano. It reminds you of your visits to the old people's home.

(This meat can be harvested by level-90 and higher Hunters.)

11673.descriptionId:
Frigostians are unanimous in claiming that this meat is delicious as long as other people are eating it.

(This meat can be harvested by level-90 and higher Hunters.)

11674.descriptionId: A frozen meal can be kept for several years, which is fortunate, because you're not in a hurry to taste this meat.

11675.descriptionId: A frozen meal can be kept for several years, which is fortunate, because you're not in a hurry to taste this meat.

11676.descriptionId: A frozen meal can be kept for several years, which is fortunate, because you're not in a hurry to taste this meat.

11677.descriptionId: A frozen meal can be kept for several years, which is fortunate, because you're not in a hurry to taste this meat.

11678.descriptionId: This dish, presented as a local speciality, was actually developed by Frigostian restaurateurs after the influx of tourists. Playing on the gullibility of adventurers willing to swallow anything, the Frigostians were able to keep their food supplies intact.

11679.descriptionId: This crate could be used to store all kinds of things in, like medicine, tools, or your mother-in-law.

11680.descriptionId: Clarisse Tocate prepared the contents of this basket with love for her cousins Albert Lioz and Moutou Louse.

11681.descriptionId: This toy has been designed to keep lonely adults busy for several hours.

11683.descriptionId: Is this branch capable of healing or summoning? It doesn't matter, because ever since you chopped it off the Soft Oak, it's been perfect for cleaning out your neighbours' nostrils.

11684.descriptionId: This Snow Bow Wow has been trained. We don't know in what, but no one's going to ask you to worry about any of that kind of stuff anyway.

11685.descriptionId: This crate contains all kinds of things, like medicine, tools, your mother-in-law, and even a useful book that says it's time to maybe think about giving the mother-in-law references a bit of a rest.

11686.descriptionId: There's no doubt about it. This loincloth belonged to at least one Kanigloo, maybe several. One less, now.

11687.descriptionId:
Before the big freeze, Laurent Gebleuh was often accompanied by his YeCh'Ti, George. George was sweet, George was cool, but after the big freeze, he became a bit of a pain in the arse. That's why Laurent Gebleuh prefers humbugs to George.
This humbug increases your Prospecting by 25 points for 10 fights.

11688.descriptionId:
Before the big freeze, Laurent Gebleuh was often accompanied by his YeCh'Ti, George. George was sweet, George was cool, but after the big freeze, he became a bit of a pain in the arse. That's why Laurent Gebleuh prefers humbugs to George.
This humbug increases your Prospecting by 50 points for 15 fights.

11689.descriptionId:
Before the big freeze, Laurent Gebleuh was often accompanied by his YeCh'Ti, George. George was sweet, George was cool, but after the big freeze, he became a bit of a pain in the arse. That's why Laurent Gebleuh prefers humbugs to George.
This sweet will increase experience received for 10 fights.

11690.descriptionId:
Before the big freeze, Laurent Gebleuh was often accompanied by his YeCh'Ti, George. George was sweet, George was cool, but after the big freeze, he became a bit of a pain in the arse. That's why Laurent Gebleuh prefers humbugs to George.
This sweet increases your experience received for 15 fights.

11691.descriptionId: This humbug increases your Prospecting by 25 points for 10 fights.

11692.descriptionId: This humbug increases your Prospecting by 50 points for 15 fights.

11693.descriptionId: This sweet will increase experience received for 10 fights.

11694.descriptionId: This sweet increases your experience received for 15 fights.

11695.descriptionId: This beautiful flower reflects the sensitivity of its former owner. Who'd have thought that even the most ferocious of Kanniballs had a soft side!

11696.descriptionId: Not many people know that Kanniball Andchain wears a hood under his mask. Now that you have it in your hands, you'll be able to prove it. The question is, will people believe you?

11697.descriptionId: Whether you deserve it or not, this sample belongs to you now. You should take it to Herr Peece.

11698.descriptionId: Only connoisseurs know the difference between Artisanal Friswein and the Friswein you find in the pub. It's exactly the same with good and bad hunters.

11699.descriptionId: More resistant than a pair of Captain Chafer's Kriptonite Underpants and more aggressive than a band of Astrubian hunters, these ticks are a veritable nightmare for their host.

11700.descriptionId: This pledge, signed by the mayor, certifies the amount of funds to be released for medical research. Too bad you're not a doctor.

11701.descriptionId: Only the most skilled alchemists can craft this potion, the difficulty of which lies in keeping the Cromagmunk alive and conscious during the pressing, which lasts 10 minutes. A pressing that is too hard or too fast produces a slurry that isn't even good enough to feed a Lousy Pig.

11702.descriptionId: This cereal with unlikely effects is the result of many cross-breedings in the greenhouses of Frigost.

11703.descriptionId: This plant with unlikely effects is the result of many cross-breedings in the greenhouses of Frigost.

11704.descriptionId: Consuming these roots in a herbal tea allows the drinker to see the facts as they are, rather than as they should be. Some Frigostians get the same result by spending their evenings down the pub.

11705.descriptionId: This Cromagmunk is alive. It moves, picks its nose and bites the backsides of the unwary. It almost sounds like your little sister, if you ignore its large, furry tail.

11707.descriptionId: The vast majority of the female population of the World of Twelve will think you look like an incredibly cute cuddly toy disguised with this hat. Given that you're more interested in terrorising them with the remains of a monster as ferocious as Tengu Snowfoux, they're wasting their time.

11708.descriptionId: Tengu Snowfoux doesn't have three tails, and neither do any of its Snowfoux cousins, so why did you ask your tailor to sew three onto this cloak? You must have a crippling inferiority complex.

11709.descriptionId: Having snatched enough bandages from Tengu Snowfoux to make this belt, you need a couple of plasters yourself.

11710.descriptionId: Made from Snowfoux pelt, these slippers are comfortable enough for you to squeeze your toes inside. Only three of them, mind you.

11711.descriptionId: Don't you find it slightly sadistic, chopping down wood with a wooden axe? You probably do, which is why you can't stop yourself from killing all those poor Gobballs.

11712.descriptionId: If you've seen the commercial for this cape, you'll remember the catchy tagline: "Not often copied but frequently equalled, this cape is particularly noteworthy for its double stitched seams that make it more solid than the capes that do not copy it but equal it". Hmmm. Suddenly, you smell the subtle odour of scam.

11713.descriptionId:
This amulet was very fashionable on Frigost.
Several centuries ago.

11714.descriptionId: This stench coming off this ring makes you think someone has been wearing it on their toes.

11715.descriptionId: Have you heard the expression "a face like a slapped arse"? No? Take a look in the mirror.

11716.descriptionId: This fur-covered belt keeps your thighs warm, which should melt your love handles a little faster.

11717.descriptionId: Piautre was born on an old collective farm on Frigost, near the Frozen Lake. He created this ring thinking he'd managed to reinvent the finger-mounted lawn strimmer. He only cut his hand 3 times.

11718.descriptionId: When the Celestial Bearbarian fancies a quick sneak out of his hive, he dons this mask to pass himself off as a Mellifluous Bearbarian. Unfortunately, his belly gives him away.

11719.descriptionId: When there's nothing much going down in the Bearbarian Hive, the sticky ursines wrap themselves up in their cloaks and use them as a kind of luge. A thorough Frigostian study into their traits and their mannerisms seems to have shown that they are very bad at avoiding obstacles and they generally protect their hands with their heads.

11720.descriptionId: A delicious, yet frighteningly sticky honey drips from this amulet. If you put it around your neck, you'll benefit from a free, progressive depilation of your entire torso. If you really want to put it in your mouth, you'd be advised to do so before you wear it around your neck, unless you like recipes based on body hair.

11721.descriptionId: There are a few Frigostian hunters who claim to have seen the Celestial Bearbarian actually slip this belt up over his paunch, but they're the same hunters who claim to have seen a YeCh'Ti on Frigost.

11722.descriptionId: The Bearbarians have been working for generations to produce the perfect sole: one that doesn't stick to honey.

11723.descriptionId: Everyone will think you look ridiculous when they see you wearing this hat, but they won't say a word. Now you know what they're thinking though, although they won't know that you know what they're thinking. The most important thing is that you know that they don't know that you know what they're thinking.

11724.descriptionId: Formerly worn by disreputable Frigostian men, this hat has now become an indispensable fashion item. On the label you can read: "This hat will attract all manner of wild creatures that want your body rather than your gold." It is not clear whether these are female Frigostians from Frigost Village or the creatures that inhabit the forests.

11725.descriptionId: Sleepy, lazy, nonchalant, bone idle - all adjectives that can be applied to the wearer of this hat. Mind you, it will certainly lull people into a false sense of security. Your enemies will lower their guard, monsters will ignore you and attack your friends instead, people will treat you like a layabout, you won't be able to find any work, your partner will leave you, everyone will forget about you. And it seemed like such a good idea to wear it at the time :(

11726.descriptionId: Wear this cape around your shoulders and then conspire against King Allister, which will allow you, amongst other things, to eat Brawn Salad more regularly, or even land yourself a parasol. But you must then get out of his sight!

11727.descriptionId: This very rough creation has no shape as such, no aesthetic appeal at all, and looks like it would fall to pieces at the slightest touch. It is, however, extremely powerful. I bet you didn't see that coming.

11728.descriptionId: Before the big freeze, Count Harebourg said that if all of the Eculture Capes were to disappear from the island of Frigost, the World of Twelve would only be able to survive for another four years. He didn't actually say that, it was just a rumour started by Eculture, the cape's creator, who was on the brink of bankruptcy. He has since become immeasurably wealthy.

11729.descriptionId: Cetera was a terribly powerful warrior, but was unable to finish what he started. He mutilated his opponents by the dozen without ever knowingly killing a single one. He died the day they all decided to gang up on him in revenge. You'll think twice next time you're about to spare someone's life now, won't you?

11730.descriptionId: The jeweller who created this amulet was a little mad, and put it together without any respect for the basic rules of Frigostian jewellery, using individual components each more different than the last. By some unknown miracle, he was quite successful.

11731.descriptionId: Equip your Battleflag Amulet, mount your proudest Dragoturkey, equip your shiniest weapon, hold your shield high and guide your men to victory with the biggest demonstration of chivalry the World of Twelve has ever seen! Tallyho! Be careful not to scare people too much if you don't want to end up burnt at the stake, mind you.

11732.descriptionId: For a long time now, Frigostian hunters have pondered the significance of the motif scribbled on this loincloth. After long deliberation, they have concluded that it must be a warning concerning the odour it must hide.

11733.descriptionId: Whether you're standing in a breeze, or wading through a strong current, you'll generate an enormous amount of energy wearing this belt. What you do with it is up to you, except for the fact that this one is all clogged-up and as such, unusable. You should be able to give it to Juss Tafinger's Assistant, in the Ski Maker's shop in Frigost Village, and she'll give you a new one for it.

11734.descriptionId: This belt, which radiates fluorescent green light, will cause any flowers around you to wilt, will make your summons look original, and will kill your enemies (very) slowly. Guaranteed for 4.47 billion years.

11735.descriptionId: The jeweller who crafted this ring, which has been passed down from generation to generation of Cestrals, was certainly no great talent. The "Z" which adorns the seal appears back-to-front when you seal an envelope with it. Actually, you're not even sure it is a "Z". It might be an "N". Will you ever find out? Probably not.

11736.descriptionId: This extremely powerful ring will allow you to manipulate the person who wears it like a puppet. Now's the perfect time for you to save your marriage.

11737.descriptionId: This ring, which appears to have suicidal tendencies, requires your constant attention. If you stop looking after it, there's a good chance it will inexorably roll towards the nearest cliff and throw itself off.

11738.descriptionId: This ring takes its strange name from the exclamation of surprise it draws from young adventurers who see it for the first time, an exclamation among others such as "zomghax", "do want" and "kill self vs wall". The inhabitants of the World of Twelve move in mysterious ways.

11739.descriptionId: When you're running, these boots will help you to keep a constant speed without any extra effort on your part, as long as no one tries to stop you. Unfortunately, they're so heavy you're unable to put one foot in front of the other. You'll make an excellent punching ball. Very stable.

11740.descriptionId: The shoemaker who designed these boots was very innovative. He covered them with many small holes so that unpleasant odours could escape rather than gather in the boots themselves. As a result, you stink to high heaven, but your boots don't smell in the slightest.

11741.descriptionId: These boots have one serious design flaw: they may be perfect for climbing the highest peaks of Frigost, but they're nothing more than heavily-soled socks, and your toes may well fall off if you attempt to climb Mount Scauldron wearing them. They're still great for inflicting very painful low blows on your opponents.

11742.descriptionId: This sword is so short, you'll need to stretch if you want to hit people with it. Sure, it'll be nigh on impossible for you to hurt your enemies, but try to look on the bright side for once. At least you won't hurt your allies any more.

11743.descriptionId: This sword is the preferred weapon of dentists, wild boar hunters and wild boar hunting dentists.

11744.descriptionId: The blade of this sword wilts when your legs start to shake, giving you the perfect excuse to flee like the coward you are.

11745.descriptionId: This strange hammer is supposed to allow your enemies to see their future when you hit them on the head with it. It doesn't seem to be working properly, because the only thing they see is blood. Maybe you're hitting them a little too hard.

11746.descriptionId: This hammer oozes virility, brute force, sweat, and somewhat counter-intuitively, hair. It reminds you of the Minotoror more than anything. It goes without saying that with this little marvel in their hands, even the most delicate of calves would be capable of creating unprecedented carnage.

11747.descriptionId: This massive, honey-covered hammer attracts the greedy and feeds the dying.

11748.descriptionId: Thanos practiced all manner of unsavoury occupations: drill sergeant, banker, moneylender, storyteller and occasional P.A.N.T.S. prophet. He used this staff to punish his apprentices and anyone that would listen to him, a daily habit that certainly kept him fit. This example has been gnawed by a starving Rattedaugue. Juss Tafinger's assistant will happily take it off your hands and give you a new one for it.

11749.descriptionId: This is the perfect staff for protecting yourself from the sun, and will prompt hours of ripe debate amongst your peers. Is it really a sunshade, or an umbrella?

11750.descriptionId: If you've decided to become a furtive, nocturnal dispenser of justice, then this is the staff for you! Coordinating very well with black looks and blacker moods, it has the extraordinary magic power of being completely invisible in total darkness.

11751.descriptionId: An improved version of the Shushette Dagger Nica, this pair of daggers will let you do two good deeds at once: dish out tasty confectioneries, and rid yourself of annoying kids.

11752.descriptionId: These daggers are incredibly exasperating: irregular, unpredictable, treacherous, they remind you in every way of your mother-in-law. You're already looking forward to the prospect of sharing these feelings with your worst enemy.

11753.descriptionId: Aguirre Godswrath was an adventurer in search of conquests and a conqueror in search of adventure. He didn't find what he was looking for on Frigost, but found instead everything he wasn't looking for. He was known to shout his name every time he killed an enemy. He lost his voice after attacking a hydra. How, you ask? Well, its heads wouldn't stop growing back.

11754.descriptionId: This bow, with its most unusual colour and shape, only seems to be appreciated by a small minority of adventurers. They call themselves artists, avant-gardists, or misunderstood, it depends. If you leave them to wrack their brains to find a way that they could be useful in a fight, it should give you enough time to split them in two.

11755.descriptionId: The creator of this bow was well-known, having dedicated his life to creating weapons of excellent quality, although very basic. Reaching the end of his years, and regretting never having created anything out-of-the-ordinary, he carved this bow, his one and only flight of fancy. It may be strange, but you will inevitably find it very useful.

11756.descriptionId: This bow dates back to before the glaciation of Frigost. Old-fashioned, it fell into disuse until very recently, when a small child who had found an old copy in an attic accidentally laid waste to an army of Mastogobs preparing to invade Frigost Village.

11757.descriptionId: This wand enabled knowledgeable Frigostians who were studying the social and cultural characteristics of the inhabitants of Frigost to easily identify each other. It was also an easily identifiable indication to monsters who were on the look out for prey with more brain than brawn.

11758.descriptionId: On this wand's wooden sleeve you can read the following inscription: "The shame of this blonde will last for all eternity". It must surely be a coded message, unless the engraver meant to write: "The flame of this wand will last for all eternity".

11759.descriptionId: This wand is the ideal weapon to berate your adversaries, or to point out the allies you choose to fight in your place.

11760.descriptionId: This axe used to belong to a famous assassin who took perverse pleasure in jumping into haystacks from the tops of the towers of Allister's Castle.

11761.descriptionId: The chances of crossing a Teroid Axe field successfully are only one in three million seven hundred and twenty.

11762.descriptionId: This shovel comes from a mythical land where gold is supposed to abound. It is said that Aguirre himself sought this country for years. He ended his life on a raft with only this miserable shovel to paddle with.

11763.descriptionId:
This shovel goes really well with long hair and pointed ears. It will awaken the magic dormant inside you. It'll also do wonders for your feminine side. 
This masterpiece was revealed to the world during the wabbit hunt organised by the great Wyze (even though his hair is no longer long).

11764.descriptionId: This document confirms your entrance into Kit's dungeon.

11765.descriptionId: This little fuzzball hates being stroked the wrong way, although you're not actually sure which is the right way to stroke it. This creature only eats Frosteez.

11766.descriptionId: This Cromigmite Ghost hasn't left the living world yet. Will you find a way to resurrect it or cowardly abandon it once and for all?

11767.descriptionId: If you shake this gift box vigorously, you'll find it's not empty. Perhaps the gods are finally smiling down on you.

11768.descriptionId: This certificate describes the characteristics of the Cromigmite that you left at the Bow Kennel.

11769.descriptionId: This dehydrated growth hormone can be used to make a powerful potion which will improve the characteristics of a Cromigmite.

11770.descriptionId: Use this powerful potion to permanently increase the characteristics of your Cromigmite. Be careful though, as only one dose will work. Trying more than once will cause disappointing results.

11771.descriptionId:
Yes, it floats. Don't ask.
(This legendary pet refuses to eat, so don't bother trying.)

11772.descriptionId: This Jellifrost Ghost hasn't left the living world yet. Will you find a way to resurrect it or cowardly abandon it once and for all?

11773.descriptionId: If you shake this gift box vigorously, you'll find it's not empty. Perhaps the gods are finally smiling down on you.

11774.descriptionId: This certificate describes the characteristics of the Jellifrost that you left at the Bow Kennel.

11777.descriptionId: This little pet will take care of your nuts by running off and hiding them somewhere. Don't expect to find them again, however, as it won't remember where it's hidden them. This creature only eats aspen wood.

11778.descriptionId: This Cromagmunk Ghost hasn't left the living world yet. Will you find a way to resurrect it or cowardly abandon it once and for all?

11779.descriptionId: If you shake this gift box vigorously, you'll find it's not empty. Perhaps the gods are finally smiling down on you.

11780.descriptionId: This certificate describes the characteristics of the Cromagmunk that you left at the Bow Kennel.

11781.descriptionId: This dehydrated growth hormone can be used to make a powerful potion which will improve the characteristics of a Cromagmunk.

11782.descriptionId: Use this powerful potion to permanently increase the characteristics of your Cromagmunk. Be careful though, as only one dose will work. Trying more than once will cause disappointing results.

11783.descriptionId: Grumpier than a Minifoux but with far less hairy armpits, this pet is renowned for having bitten Dame Antium without breaking a single tooth. This creature only eats icefish fricassee.

11784.descriptionId: This Snowfoux Ghost hasn't left the living world yet. Will you find a way to resurrect it or cowardly abandon it once and for all?

11785.descriptionId: If you shake this gift box vigorously, you'll find it's not empty. Perhaps the gods are finally smiling down on you.

11786.descriptionId: This certificate describes the characteristics of the Snowfoux that you left at the Bow Kennel.

11787.descriptionId: This dehydrated growth hormone can be used to make a powerful potion which will improve the characteristics of a Snowfoux.

11789.descriptionId: Use this powerful potion to permanently increase the characteristics of your Snowfoux. Be careful though, as only one dose will work. Trying more than once will cause disappointing results.

11790.descriptionId: This Voracious Chest is asleep. If you want to find out what it's hiding in its belly, you'll need to wake it up - but you do so entirely at your own risk.

11792.descriptionId: You excel in your mastery of the four primordial elemental energies and you want everyone to know. Be careful though, as this amulet might play tricks on you.

11793.descriptionId: This sample was taken from a body trapped in the ice. Herr Peece will know what to do with it.

11794.descriptionId:
Two copies of this root-containing amulet were created by an eminent Frigostian biologist, and were supposed to help the inhabitants of the Snowbound Village rid themselves of the vegetal creatures from the Petrified Forest.
The biologist disappeared without leaving any kind of instructions as to how to use them, and his son, who went off to find him, never found a single trace. The Frigostian islanders tried to recreate the effects of the two amulets and what you have in your hands is only a rough copy of the original.

11795.descriptionId: This root was created by a Frigostian biologist to repair the damage caused by his past mistakes.

11796.nameId: A Flash of Lightning, a Flashing Scythe
11796.descriptionId: Song taken from a Collection of Farmers' Songs.

11798.descriptionId: Made from 100% vegetable matter, the Nice Kanniball Organiser will be able to use this key to repair his mask.

11799.descriptionId: You can use this key to take a trip around the Haunted House at the Trool Fair. You disclaim any liability for personal injury and damages caused by its misuse.

11805.descriptionId:
There is almost nothing left of the Eliatrope civilisation.
A few ruins, some petroglyphs, faded memories. Since ancient times, important ceremonies were celebrated with a shower of petals. According to Lyrad the Silent, this ritual dates back to the first Eliatropes who opened their initiation with a rain of Wakfu.

11806.descriptionId: This bag contains plenty of Eliatrope Fantasies.

11807.descriptionId: This rare, unholy book, cursed by many and banned from all the libraries, is supposed to have been written by Lyrad the Silent, a charlatan who lived a very long time ago (and who is supposed to still be alive, from what we've heard). The Gods themselves have forbidden their followers from reading it. Even having it on your person is punishable by terrible penalties.

11808.descriptionId:
This little necklace made from island pearls exudes a soft bluish aura that evokes powerful memories of adventures on the beautiful, cerulean sea.

Only the small note on the back of this exquisite piece shatters the idyllic illusion: "Made in IOW".

11809.descriptionId:
This very special, extremely rare rock is excavated by Enutrofs without them ever being able to find any value for it. Dark and crumbly, it cannot be used for construction, or as an ornament, and has very little commercial value. It would seem that its low resistance could make it an inexpensive form of protection. However, the most notable effect of this rock is to plunge the person who carries it into a deep depression.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

11810.descriptionId:
Hives are rare, very rare. Because bees are our friends, because we like to spread our bread with good honey, because our flowers like to be pollinated, we carry our own hives! And from these chambers, the juice of these adorable little things, worthy heirs of the mythical little goddess Beebee, will flow.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

11811.descriptionId: A pair of splendid walking boots tanned in Brakmar.

11812.descriptionId: A strange ring, imitating a cube with unknown properties. Is it a thimble? A die for playing with? A small chest? Nobody ever knew the answer. It was thought, probably wrongly, that it could be an imitation of an ancient, long-forgotten artefact whose shape could have survived the fashions, irrespective of its use. One reason for its success remains the welfare and assurance it provides its wearer, as if protected beyond time and space.

11813.descriptionId:
This collector's helmet is used by the hostesses of Osamodas temples to welcome new candidates to the annual competition of the best trainers in Astrub. The idea of using the Platypus as a mascot for the event came after the pet, known as being indomitable, was introduced to the masses. The trainer who can subdue the animal has definitely earned his stripes. So far, no one has succeeded, the animal preferring to choose his own master and do exactly as it feels. Holders of the cap believe themselves to be rebel elements of a theocratic society known for its rigidity.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

11814.descriptionId: Boostache always had a bit of a complex about not being able to grow hairs on his chin, and in fact, about not having a chin at all, sadly. To compensate, he grew this superb moustache.

11815.descriptionId: No one knows how Boostache secretes this strange substance, or from where it comes. All that's known about it is that it's white, it's sticky, and it glows in the dark.

11816.descriptionId: You're not really sure if this belt itches or tickles. It doesn't matter though, because unless you wear something underneath it to Captain Chafer's Panty Party, it'll drive you nuts.

11817.descriptionId:
This cape perfectly illustrates Percimol's favourite saying: React, resist, and never relinquish!
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

11818.descriptionId:
No one will mistake you for a Scarecrow with this mask on your pudgy little face, unless you're a Xelor dwarf or the person you're talking to is a Iop. Yes, "a" Iop, because it's pronounced Yop. So there.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

11819.descriptionId:
This hammer, which is as heavy as the atmosphere generated when a Rattedaugue tells one of his "jokes", is perfect for crushing the Minotoror's hooves. It is equally effective should you wish to smash other, just-as-sensitive body parts.
Latem Sa will exchange it for you, at the Blacksmiths' Workshop in Astrub.

11820.descriptionId: It took several centuries to build this shovel from gold bar dust, but it was worth the wait. It's very handy for cutting off the heads of monks or slicing a piece of Zoug pie.

11821.descriptionId: If you shake this gift box vigorously, you'll find it's not empty. Perhaps the gods are finally smiling down on you.

11845.descriptionId: This potion contains a small amount of Quadramental Breeze that you cleverly captured yourself with your little handies.

11846.descriptionId: Moutou Louse dropped this crate on the floor as he ran for his life.

11847.descriptionId: This extremely rare plant is mostly made of vegetal sulphur. It is credited with such virtues to make an Osa green with envy.

11848.descriptionId: This perfume makes your eyes sting and even makes your hair hurt.

11849.descriptionId: These boxers shorts are a credit to the reputation of Amaknian shoemakers. Soft, flexible and robust all at once, they are designed to stand up to any "challenge".

11850.descriptionId: These pants form the ceremonial dress of the prophets of P.A.N.T.S. They are the only ones who can wear them without risking being mistaken for a farmer, a travelling tinker or a milkman. That sort of thing.

11851.descriptionId:
This potion has been blessed by the P.A.N.T.S.
It leaves you strangely unaroused.

11852.descriptionId: Wes Rob, the terrifying pirate, planted this flower in the southernmost tip of the Petrified Forest, before he died having drowned in a barrel of beer during a storm at sea.

11853.descriptionId: This document reveals a very well-kept secret. Well, very well-kept until today, that is.

11854.descriptionId:
Fed up of being mistaken for a slob because of his hat, Stroud had the ingenious idea of attaching a kama to it with a piece of Minotoror leather. The result was immediate: people mistook him for a wrinkled old skinflint instead.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

11855.descriptionId: These flip-flops are roomy enough for you to be able to pick up kamas with your toes. Their shape is also suited to placing blows in the sacks of your enemies so that you can recover their family jewels more easily.

11856.descriptionId: You can tuck your family jewels safely into this belt's two enormous sacks.

11857.descriptionId:
This shovel can do everything: dig earth, collect kamas, stun bandits and even repel your mother-in-law. As you can see, it's pretty much indispensable.
Latem Sa will exchange it for you, at the Blacksmiths' Workshop in Astrub.

11858.descriptionId: This tofu fell into a cauldron of cheese fondue when it was tiny. It has grown a little plump, and the other tofus constantly tease it about its weight. So be it. It has decided to eat them all in revenge. This soul-eating pet eats other tofus.

11859.descriptionId: This Plump Tofurby Ghost hasn't left the living world yet. Will you find a way to resurrect it or cowardly abandon it once and for all?

11860.descriptionId: If you shake this gift box vigorously, you'll find it's not empty. Perhaps the gods are finally smiling down on you.

11861.descriptionId: This certificate describes the characteristics of the Plump Tofurby that you left at the Bow Kennel.

11862.descriptionId: This dehydrated growth hormone can be used to make a powerful potion which will improve the characteristics of a Plump Tofurby.

11863.descriptionId: Use this powerful potion to permanently increase the characteristics of your Plump Tofurby. Be careful though, as only one dose will work. Trying more than once will cause disappointing results.
