13911.descriptionId: This bag is full of resources prized by Frigostian craftsmen.

13912.descriptionId: This bag is full of resources prized by Frigostian craftsmen.

13913.descriptionId: Get this horror grafted onto your forehead, and your arrogance will reach new heights. At least, you'll finally be able to see over the top of the desks and tables in the Temple of Scriptures.

13915.descriptionId: You should have gone easy on the poor soul that gave up this leather. Dumples aren't known for their intelligence. In fact, they have very little going for them at all.

13916.descriptionId: This fabric proves that even the stupidest creatures in the World of Twelve can be stylish. Chin up!

13918.descriptionId: This leather was chosen for its wonderful resistance, and not because it was the only scrap left on the factory floor.

13919.descriptionId: This leather smells like straw, and the Asteraw's straw smells like leather. We're back to the old Tofu and egg paradox!

13921.descriptionId: If the Leatherball were a little smaller, it would fit into a mouth. You're so used to the World of Twelve that this image doesn't even shock you.

13923.descriptionId: On his days off, Klime wears a tight-fitting t-shirt that reads "5% leather, 95% moustache". How depleted must he be feeling right now?

13924.descriptionId: Placed carefully over your nascent bald spot, this little treasure will take three weeks off you, easy!

13925.descriptionId: This brute's blood can't even be used to make black pudding. Outrageous!

13926.descriptionId: An eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth - or in your case, a tooth for an uncomfortably large chunk of your right buttock.

13927.descriptionId: Stalaks are eager, messy eaters, and in a confused blur of teeth and flesh, they often bite their own tongues. You did the owner of this ridiculously sharp incisor a favour by pulling it out. They would say thank you, but you killed them.

13929.descriptionId: Not even a vampire would drink this stuff.

13931.descriptionId: The incus, or anvil, is the anvil-shaped ossicle in the Skateman's middle ear. Your mum told me an anvil fell on your cot when you were a baby. I'm guessing it wasn't this one.

13933.descriptionId: The stapes is the smallest bone in the Revish's body. This particular example was shattered into tiny pieces during a recent Jon Lemon concert.

13935.descriptionId: And to think, she didn't even say thank you for the free hair removal you gave her!

13936.descriptionId: Missiz Freezz likes to keep a spare pair of underpants in her pocket in case she gets knocked down by a Skaterman and has to be carted off to the nearest medical centre. Spare or worn, you're just happy to add them to your burgeoning collection.

13937.descriptionId: A thorough analysis of this slobber shows that Nessil should really think about flossing a lot more regularly.

13939.descriptionId: You're almost certain that this tooth is false, because it reminds you of the 'diamond' ring you gave to your sweetheart in the Astrub Tavern. There was definitely a whiff of lavender about that marriage.

13941.descriptionId: You can almost hear the Fecas shouting from here: "But why would a bird that can't fly need feathers?"

13943.descriptionId: A Thermite has six legs, so it's not like it's going to miss one, is it?

13945.descriptionId: Do carnivorous plants taste of meat?

13947.descriptionId: You knew that Nileza wore embroidered pants even before the fight started, and luckily for you, the secret of how you came by that piece of information will now never be revealed.

13948.descriptionId: This strange invention is very handy if you know how to use it, but potentially very painful if you don't.

13949.descriptionId: If you'd have known just how eager Kan-O-Mats are to bite dentists, you might not have killed so many of them.

13951.descriptionId: Woolly Bow Meows adore this Mimilk, and I daresay Clarice Peseay does too. Mac Gayver plans to use it to soften up the suit.

13952.descriptionId: Neither Woolly Bow Meows nor Clarice Peseay adore this Mimilk. Mac Gayver plans to use it to soften up the suit.

13953.descriptionId: Al Shab uses this blubber to keep his foodstuffs nice and warm. Mac Gayver is going to mix it with Frighog Lard to create a thermal insulating material.

13954.descriptionId: This blubber used to be used for keeping foodstuffs nice and warm, but it's too rubbery for that now. Mac Gayver is going to mix it with Frighog Lard to create a thermal insulating material.

13955.descriptionId: Al Shab uses this lard to add a gelatinous texture to his foodstuffs. Mac Gayver is going to mix it with Pingwobble Blubber to create a thermal insulating material.

13956.descriptionId: This lard is well past its sell-by date, and Al Shab isn't a convincing enough salesman to flog it at a fraction of the recommended retail price. Mac Gayver is going to mix it with Pingwobble Blubber to create a thermal insulating material.

13957.descriptionId: These Woolly Piggoth Hairs are all scratchy and rough, but Dutch has a special treatment to make them silky. Mac Gayver wants to make some earmuffs with them.

13958.descriptionId: These Woolly Piggoth Hairs are as soft and smooth as can be. Mac Gayver wants to make some earmuffs with them.

13959.descriptionId: These claws make excellent crampons - Clyde Parker always carries a spare pair when he goes out hunting Pingwins. Mac Gayver intends to transform them into non-slip soles.

13960.descriptionId: These claws are much too fragile to be used as crampons. All the same, Mac Gayver thinks he can transform them into non-slip soles.

13961.descriptionId: This ice looks dirty because it's full of impurities. Mac Gayver is hoping to transform it into glass for some goggles.

13962.descriptionId: This ice is so pure that you can almost see your face in it when there's a full moon. Mac Gayver is hoping to transform it into glass for some goggles.

13963.descriptionId: This fur is as cold and uncomfortable as Gormor the Mangler's sense of humour. It's the main ingredient for Mac Gayver's thermolactic suit.

13964.descriptionId: This fur is still very cold, but much softer than before. It's the main ingredient for Mac Gayver's thermolactic suit.

13965.descriptionId:
This suit will enable you to survive extremely cold conditions in spite of the lack of oxygen.
Unfortunately, the suit is somewhat fragile, due to the poor quality of the materials used to make it.

13966.descriptionId:
This suit will enable you to survive extremely cold conditions in spite of the lack of oxygen.
Unfortunately, the suit is somewhat cumbersome, due to the mediocre quality of the materials used to make it.

13967.descriptionId: This suit will enable you to survive extremely cold conditions in spite of the lack of oxygen.

13968.descriptionId: This suit will enable you to survive extremely cold conditions in spite of the lack of oxygen. Thanks to the superior quality of the materials used to make it, it is less cumbersome than a normal suit.

13969.descriptionId: This suit will enable you to survive extremely cold conditions in spite of the lack of oxygen. Thanks to the exceptional quality of the materials used to make it, it is very good at protecting its wearer from nasty surprises.

13970.descriptionId: This suit will enable you to survive extremely cold conditions in spite of the lack of oxygen. Thanks to the extraordinary quality of the materials used to make it, it is very good at protecting its wearer from the effects of sub-zero temperatures.

13971.descriptionId: Tinkerbears will happily use a fallen comrade's maxilla as a vice when something needs repairing. Not everything can be fixed that way, and particularly not that tattoo you've got on your left bumcheek. Yes, the one you had done as a declaration of love for your sweetheart who left you broken-hearted a couple of days later.

13973.descriptionId: I know you were keen for that Pingwinch to stop sticking its beak in, but was cutting it off really necessary?

13975.descriptionId: This bone was specially designed to adapt to the changing size of Mechaniac ankles. The poor creatures are known for their terrible superiority complex whenever they manage to humiliate an adventurer. You'll probably find this bone very useful.

13976.descriptionId: This small, mechanical ear is incredibly realistic and will filter out any unwanted noises, selectively hearing only what it wants to hear. Its inventor was directly inspired by the ears of her husband.

13977.descriptionId: This membrane hides the Serpulax's most intimate mechanisms, but you were deeply disappointed when you tugged it away. Instead of attempting to seduce you, this mechanical handyman should have stuck to its day job.

13979.descriptionId: This heart doesn't need to be preserved in the fridge; it's already as cold as a Rattedaugue's insincere salutations. Since the disappearance of the Ice Cracklers, hearts like this one have been in great demand by Frigostian organ smugglers.

13980.descriptionId: In days gone by, the Onis haunted the Mystified Forest, where they would torment adventurers by telling them the opposite of what they actually meant. After the big freeze, they all but disappeared, which is why this leather has become so rare.

13981.descriptionId: This Frigostian alloy was frozen solid in a barrel of beer when the curse struck. That explains why not even the best miners can craft it and only master jewellers can use it without cracking it.

13982.descriptionId: This wool kept Sylargh warm while he worked outside until the fateful day he developed a terrible phobia of snowflakes.

13983.descriptionId: This hollow tooth is almost as rusty as your social skills.

13984.descriptionId: The Frigostian bourgeoisie love to pluck these feathers from Bubotrons and use them to adorn their hats. Count Harebourg loves to pluck these feathers from the Frigostian bourgeoisie and uses them to adorn his Bubotrons.

13987.descriptionId: Treadfasts won't hesitate to peck the backsides of anyone who attempts to enter Count Harebourg's castle uninvited, so if you've got flawless buttocks it can only mean one thing - you're either a lamentable adventurer, or you're one of the Count's followers. So which one are you?

13988.descriptionId: Cycloids can spot mechanical defects with an unerring accuracy, so it's no surprise that this eye is staring directly at you.

13989.descriptionId: Sinistro feathers make excellent feather dusters, whenever a Sinistro has nothing better to do than go after dust. The owner of this particular example will be only too pleased to attack you, once it's finished the housework.

13990.descriptionId: You wanted to find out if Sinistrofus can fly with only one wing, so you pulled this off a passing owl and threw the poor bird from the walls of Count Harebourg's castle. The landing looked particularly painful. Now you can rip the other one off and see if it can fly with no wings at all.

13992.descriptionId: When it comes to poultry, there are usually two camps: breast or thigh. You appear to have chosen wing.

13994.descriptionId: This shard of scapula burst through the Count's bandages like ideas pop into your head - painfully.

13995.descriptionId: Icy yet warm, clean yet sullied by insults. You're still not convinced the Count deserved his fate.

13996.descriptionId: Didn't anyone mention the side effects?

13997.descriptionId: Didn't anyone mention the side effects?

13998.descriptionId: Didn't anyone mention the side effects?

13999.descriptionId: Didn't anyone mention the side effects?

14000.descriptionId: This hat was designed by a tailor who adored Bow Meows and was vehemently opposed to the Systematic Termination For Undesirable Bow Meows association. He was assassinated by members of the Pingwin Protection Agency, who were vehemently opposed to the extermination of wildlife from the Frozen Lake area.

14001.descriptionId: Augilol was a non-descript Sram who spent his whole, miserable life in Ogivol's shadow. When Frigost Island was rediscovered, he was one of the first passengers to make the journey, hoping to come into his own and make his fortune. We don't know what happened next. All that's left of him is this cloak.

14002.descriptionId: Inferno used to wear these boots to trample all over his apprentices and the basic rules of good manners.

14003.descriptionId: Styx underwent a bizarre initiation ceremony involving him being ducked underwater in a river. These boots saved his life: if they had slipped off when Fetis grabbed hold of them to yank him out, he would have been swept downstream and lost forever.

14004.descriptionId: These boots allow their wearer to play in seven leagues at once. Mandrin was never that into Gobbowl, so he just wore them to kick Perceptors' rumps and do the gardening in.

14005.descriptionId: Like all great warriors, Will Killson always had something up his sleeve. In his case, it was actually a spare pair boots. Unconventional, but practical.

14006.descriptionId: This ring belonged to Inferno's most beautiful apprentice. She was unlucky enough to die twice, suffering third-degree burns in the fourth dimension of the fifth amendment, after accidently looking her fiery master in the eye.

14007.descriptionId: Five fingers good, three fingers better. That's how Styx explained his punishment for the theft of this ring.

14008.descriptionId: If a Perceptor's head proved too tough to grind, Mandrin tightened this ring around its neck to throttle it instead.

14009.descriptionId: Was it a present from a client or loot from a victim? Nobody's sure where Will Killson got this ring from, and nobody really cares.

14010.descriptionId: This is what happens when you drink too much of Bipup's cordial. No need to pack your trunk and run away to the circus, though. You'll go back to normal as soon as you enter a fight.

14011.descriptionId: Chewing on this Gobbagum gives you 10 Prospecting for 5 fights.

14012.descriptionId: Chewing on this Gobbagum gives you 60 Vitality for 5 fights.

14013.descriptionId: Chewing on this Gobbagum gives you 30 Power for 5 fights.

14014.descriptionId:
Kroketh's followers can be seen furiously chomping on this kind of Gobbagum before Gobbowl matches. Made from desiccated jerky, aromatic herbs and swathes of fur, this chewy candy helps them seize life, and their opponents, by the throat.
It also grants a nice little Prospecting bonus.

14015.descriptionId:
Totot's disciples can be seen enthusiastically chewing on this kind of Gobbagum the night before a big match. There's nothing better for a soft complexion and a peachy glow. Made from fruit of the finest quality, it's 100% pip-free.
It also grants a nice little Vitality bonus.

14016.descriptionId:
Kham's disciples can be seen conscientiously masticating this kind of Gobbagum at the beginning of a match, to make sure their breath stays fresh all game long. Just because you're going to give your enemy a thumping, doesn't mean you want to envelop him in morning breath. 
It also grants a nice little Power bonus.

14017.descriptionId: This Gobbowl Ball contains every Gobbowler's favourite type of candy: Gobbagum! It's so stretchy and sticky that you can even use it to glue on a broken tooth at the end of a rough match. Quick, open it up! Which flavour did you get?

14018.descriptionId: Doctor Hoo gave you this pocketwatch, which is said to have been crafted by the notorious Count Harebourg. Its hands have ground to a halt at 12.12. It may not tell the time properly, but it does tell you that something fishy's going on.

14019.descriptionId: Contrary to popular belief, Kanigloos' long fangs are not made of frozen slobber. If you need proof, take this sample to the lab. It won't freeze, even under very low temperatures. This miracle of nature allows the common Kanigloo to indulge in its favourite hobby, slobbering, no matter how cold it gets outside.

14020.descriptionId: This little spray contains a radical remedy for the Lurgi. There's nothing like a good death to overcome sickness of any kind.

14021.descriptionId: The spooky moans of the ghost pirates haunt you to this day. WHOOOOO... Whooooo... Whoooo... Whooo... Whoo...

14022.descriptionId: This strange particle used to spin at great speed around an Atomystique. You may not know it, but it almost smashed right into your face, which might have compromised your future... There's a temporal conundrum for you to mull over.

14023.descriptionId: P.A.N.T.S. followers hate the cold and, by extension, all things Icy Brockhard-y. You've been elected to rip the hearts out of these frozen fiends. Only an evil witch from a children's fairy-tale would be able to do so without a twinge of remorse, so if it helps, you can consider it an act of involuntary organ donation. Healthcare, after all, is beyond reproach.

14024.descriptionId: This oil has soothing powers and is said to protect its user from excessive heat. Unfortunately, its odour is more reminiscent of the garbage disposal in Gordo McRamsay's kitchen than of the beaches on Moon Island.

14025.descriptionId: Everyone knows that Frosteez is an out-of-this-world cereal, but the ears in this sack really are something to behold. Everything about them - their size, their colour, their texture - seems to suggest that they've undergone some kind of shock treatment. Are they still edible, do you think? The specialists swear blind that they are, but that's probably because they're employed by a huge food-processing guild.

14026.nameId: Eternal Frost from the Frozen Grottoes
14026.descriptionId: You removed this tiny ice sculpture from the grottoes in the Fangs of Glass, and you have a funny feeling that it will never melt. You could use it as a paperweight, or you could give it to Jamie Coggut in the hope of saving Frigost. Being a born hero, you're going to go with the second option, right? Right?

14027.descriptionId: This is an exceptional batch of heavenly honey. The Celestial Bearbarian, fussy eater and god-king of the Bearbarians, is kind of a big deal, after all. Careful you don't eat too much of the rich, sugary liquid, as it can cause buzzing in the ears.

14028.descriptionId: It's said that this claw was ripped from the hands of none other than Djaul. If the stories are true, the protector of Descendre lost it during an epic battle with his arch-rival, Jiva. Whatever the truth is, you should keep it away from direct heat so that it doesn't lose its sharpness.

14029.descriptionId: A heavy, uncomfortable helmet that definitely can't be used in this state. If you want to repair it, you'll have to find someone who's used to dealing with extreme temperatures. If there's a Foggernaut somewhere in the vicinity, he'll probably be able to help.

14030.descriptionId: After expert handling by a Fogger who appeared to know just what he was doing, this diving bell looks to be in prime condition! Now you'll be able to enter the Geofurnaces without being asphyxiated by the sulphur fumes, which is always nice. On the downside, the window barely lets any light through, so you shouldn't wear it for fighting or for any activity requiring good eyesight. And I bet your life's ambition was to wear your Magmatic Diving Bell whilst combing through your mother-in-law's hair looking for nits. Sorry about that!

14031.descriptionId: This part is what guarantees that Pingwinches stay airtight when they dive into icy water. They'd be in quite a fix if their frostmotors failed whilst they were fishing under the surface, not least because they'd be late bringing back fish for Sylargh's supper.

14032.descriptionId: This high-quality material was removed from a particularly dumpy Dumple. As well as being thicker, heavier and oilier than regular leather, it's waterproof and easy to take care of. Do its good qualities never end? Er... Well, it tastes like a slice of mud pie. As long as you're not planning on getting lost in a snowdrift and having to eat your boots to survive, you should be fine.

14033.descriptionId: This helmet is made of cold, hard metal. It was created on a frosty forge, worn by a cold-hearted heathen and used to send many a shiver down innocent spines. If all that isn't enough to put you off it, then I must commend you on your thermal vest. The Frigostians chills will never get you under there!

14034.descriptionId: Nothing is sacred to you, is it? Barging in and ripping off a ghost's clothes like that? The fact that he was already dead is no excuse at all. You should be ashamed of yourself! Thanks to you and your careless behaviour, all the ghosts in the cemetery are shaking in their tombs, convinced that the invasion of the body snatchers has begun.

14035.descriptionId: Bearbarians are very fond of eating this plant as part of a salad, with honey sauce and pine nuts. The greedier bears bulk up their meal with hunks of Mastogob or pickled Larvae. A good Ygrade Plant salad in the morning will provide you with enough pep to stay wide awake all day long, dontcha know!

14036.descriptionId: Mina Spirit says that Celestial Wax can be used to stifle the complaints of tormented spirits. Bearbarians don't have much use for silencing spirits; they prefer to use it for preserving foodstuffs. But where does this mysterious wax come from? The ears of the Celestial Bearbarian himself? Surely not... But maybe. Just maybe.

14037.descriptionId: If the screams of the living dead get right up your nose, the moaning and groaning of ghosts grinds your gears, and you're overly frustrated with the sighing of all those lost souls, then this is the solution you're looking for! Simply stick one of these plugs in each ear and restful sleep will be yours at long last! Keep in a cool, dry place away from sunlight and strong odours. In case of accidental swallowing, consult your local exorcist.

14038.descriptionId: You wove this veil on the loom in the Cavern of Destiny. What is it exactly? You don't really know, but you can feel tears forming in your eyes just by looking at it. When you touch it, you begin to sob uncontrollably. Don't tell me you've finally gone soft!

14039.descriptionId: You gave Klime the Shoemaker a good kicking, and such was the violence of your frenzied attack that he had a nosebleed. Thanks to the Icy Claw, your enemy's blood has frozen solid, which suits you down to the ground, and should suit Nileza as well.

14040.descriptionId: This tear is nothing short of miraculous: who would have thought Missiz Freezz was capable of crying? The Veil of Sadness that you wove must have had something to do with it, but you'd rather believe that the forgemage finally cracked because you defeated her.

14041.descriptionId: Thanks to this viscous liquid, which is the product of many years of research and experimentation, Sylargh's machines continue to function while the plunging temperatures chill the bones of the inhabitants of Frigost. You have to admit, Sylargh is pretty handy, man.

14042.descriptionId: If I told you that the liquid contained within this flask was responsible for stopping time on the island of Frigost, would you believe me? No, you're not that naïve. And yet... you've been staring at it for a good ten minutes now. Or was Xelor's clock simply stuck?

14043.descriptionId: This key won't unlock Missiz Freezz's chastity belt, but it will unlock the door to her dungeon.

14044.descriptionId: You had to wrench this key from that Handyman's hands, the cheeky little monkey.

14045.descriptionId: This key will show you what you can do with some leather, a little imagination, and a great deal of perversion.

14046.descriptionId: There might be some powerful potions in Nileza's laboratory, although they probably taste foul. You'll just have to try them all to find out.

14047.descriptionId: You won't be able to wind up any clocks with this key, but it'll certainly let you wind up the Count.

14049.descriptionId: Copper Nickus was a heretic polymath who dared to suggest that the World of Twelve wasn't at the centre of the Krosmoz. No traces of his body were ever found, and this ring is his only surviving relic. Wear it with care.

14050.descriptionId: All the best costumiers have their little foibles, and Klime is clearly no exception. He may well have a sharp eye for fashion, but he's terribly sadistic, and no one has ever seen him without his mask - no one alive, that is. That probably goes a long way to explaining why Carla Garfield wears those sunglasses all the time.

14051.descriptionId: The lining of this cape wasn't blood red when it was first stitched, it's just been dragged one too many times across the floor of the back room in Klime's private quarters.

14052.descriptionId: A long time ago, Klime would use the needle on this belt to stitch up the broken things he found and they would return to perfect health. These days he uses it to pick apart the healthy things he finds until they're perfectly broken.

14053.descriptionId: This item has served its purpose well. You can trade it in for a new item with Chaga Lachance at the Amakna Trading Counter.

14054.descriptionId: This item has served its purpose well. You can trade it in for a new item with Chaga Lachance at the Amakna Trading Counter.

14055.descriptionId: Stilted Shovels are known for their unusual tendency to refuse to dig. As this is a particularly inconvenient quality for a shovel, the Enutrofs of the Asse Sea strap them vertically to their legs instead. This allows the stumpy treasure hunters to walk freely across the rolling sand dunes, and also makes them appear much taller than they really are.

14056.descriptionId: This item has served its purpose well. You can trade it in for a new item with Chaga Lachance at the Amakna Trading Counter.

14057.descriptionId: Wearing this cape will make you so cold you may as well not bother putting it on, so give it to me instead.

14058.descriptionId: If your ring finger wasn't already a frostbitten stump, it certainly will be now.

14059.descriptionId: No one's sure exactly how this belt works, but it seems to allow male wearers to keep a cool head in even the most stressful situations. It would appear that a thousand years of classical cerebral anatomy was wrong, and the housewives of Frigost might be on to something after all.

14060.descriptionId: Missiz Freezz's helmet is a near-perfect example of her incredible talent for smithmagic and item modification. It's so well made that despite it being infinitely lighter and far easier to carry than a bog-standard helmet, it protects her head just as well.

14061.descriptionId: Missiz Freezz forged this ring herself in a vain attempt to make Count Harebourg jealous. Poor Missiz Freezz - the Count didn't even notice.

14062.descriptionId: These reinforced boots might not give you the ice-cold temperament of Missiz Freezz, but at least you won't notice when someone steps on your toes.

14063.descriptionId: Members of a Frigostian criminal organisation sell this hat to naïve tourists, who are told they have to wear it all the time if they want free travel across the frozen island. It makes them loads more money than their previous racket - selling Mastogob Black Pudding pizzas.

14064.descriptionId: Worn back-to-front, Nileza's cloak can be used as bib to catch your slobber.

14065.descriptionId: The symbol on Nileza's amulet refers to his love of science, his intelligence, his vast knowledge, and more specifically, his mastery of the elements. You'll notice it doesn't describe anything about his mental state, however.

14066.descriptionId: Nileza's Boots are as waterproof as it is possible to get, but when a simple splash of water would cause Alchimeras to grow out of your feet, you'd want them to be as well.

14067.descriptionId: This ring is a little bit too big for you and chafes your finger, which is very painful. It also looks like it's about to explode, which would be even more painful.

14068.descriptionId: This ring disturbs the atomic structure of anything it comes into contact with, so you should avoid scratching your itchy bottom with it at all costs.

14069.descriptionId: This belt isn't called "unstable" because it's about to self-destruct, invert gravity or send you crazy, it just doesn't hold your trousers up very well.

14070.descriptionId: If we excuse Sylargh's antics, his villainy and his impertinence, it's not because he hides behind this hood, but because he's just a child. Whether that makes you feel better or worse tells me everything I need to know about you.

14071.descriptionId: If truth be told, Sylargh doesn't have a cloak. It would be far too big for him, and would trip him up or get stuck between the cogs of his death machines. What you've stolen is actually his comfort blanket. You're a monster!

14072.descriptionId: This isn't really Sylargh's belt, it would be much too big for him. His is actually a rather simple affair, crafted from a single strap and a gearwheel, the Imp's tools of the trade. I bet you paid a fortune for this knockoff, didn't you?

14073.descriptionId: Long, raggedy teeth and a head made of wood, it's as if this Kan-O-Mat Headgear was designed with you in mind.

14074.descriptionId: You'll soon get fed up of people asking you if this cape is machine-washable.

14075.descriptionId: The reverse of this amulet can be opened up to reveal a secret compartment. It looks like you've got washing powder for your Kan-O-Mat Cloak hidden in yours.

14076.descriptionId: Count Harebourg was forced to become a recluse after the big freeze, but even back then, no living soul had ever seen his face. What is he hiding behind this hat, and what transformations has that face undergone after all these years?

14077.descriptionId: This ring allows the Count to channel the surplus energy generated by his incredible powers, which would destroy him if let loose. Fortunately, that's not something you need to worry about.

14078.descriptionId: Between his castle, his soul, his island and his monsters, Count Harebourg's feet are the only things that aren't frozen solid thanks to these boots.

14079.descriptionId: It's hard to imagine Count Harebourg in a hat like this. Mind you, everyone goes through a rebellious stage, and to be fair, his has lasted more than a century.

14080.descriptionId: Looking at this amulet, it's plain to see that very little has changed over the past hundred years when it comes to jewellery.

14081.descriptionId: This belt is the only piece of equipment that the Count was wearing before the big freeze that he still wears now, mainly because the clasp froze solid when Djaul cast his curse, and Harebourg has been unable to take it off ever since.

14082.descriptionId: Like any good aristocrat, the Bubotron loves a good masked ball, but much to his great annoyance, he's never allowed to take part. The doormen always turn him away for not wearing a mask, even though he's quite clearly wearing this one.

14083.descriptionId: Bubotrons can turn their heads through 270 degrees, but are often confused by the sudden rotation. This amulet plays a vital role in allowing the dozy owls to remember the direction they should actually be facing.

14084.descriptionId: Count Harebourg gave this sword as a gift during the Bubotron's dubbing ceremony. It symbolises the owl's rank amongst the Sinistros, but as the Bubotron has no hands, it is of no use to him whatsoever.

14085.descriptionId: This cape was woven from filoplumes, tiny, feathery sensors that allow you to feel the changes in air pressure caused by an enemy sneaking up behind you. You've got to admit, that's pretty coo-owl. Oh come on, that wasn't that bad!

14086.descriptionId: A Sinistrofu doesn't have a neck, so why would it need an amulet? Is this even an amulet at all? You'd prefer not to find out.

14087.descriptionId: Sinistrofus have asymmetric ears that allow them to pinpoint the source of any sudden noise. The only asymmetric thing about you is your feet, so don't attempt to do the same thing or you'll fall over.

14088.descriptionId: Count Harebourg wore this helmet to manipulate time. If you can use it as a welding helmet, it will be an achievement.

14089.descriptionId: This ring, one of Count Harebourg's inventions, can predict when the weather is going to be cold up to a week in advance. Unsurprisingly, there's never been any great call for it on Frigost.

14090.descriptionId: Anything that disappears into the hole in this amulet reappears in another era. No, don't even think about it - the process requires that the "subject" be cryogenically frozen beforehand.

14091.descriptionId: Using the Cycloid eye in this amulet as a monocle might let you see disturbances in the space-time continuum, but you'll look like a complete berk doing so.

14092.descriptionId: This ring tells the time, but sadly, no one knows how to read it.

14093.descriptionId: These boots were made for walking at the rate of one step a second. Great if you want to walk somewhere without expending much energy, but not so great if you're attempting to escape an imminent death.

14094.descriptionId: The Trictus is the Treadfast omen of death. This amulet will predict its appearance, but won't protect you from other Treadfasts attempting to kill you for wearing the remains of one of their brothers as an amulet.

14095.descriptionId: Treadfasts attach the remains of their prey to the razor-sharp claws on this belt, so they've always got something to snack on within easy reach. I'd warn you to keep your hands away from them, if you weren't always fumbling around in your pockets.

14096.descriptionId: As long as your toes are strong enough, you can use the soles of these boots to help you hang upside-down from the branches of trees. Not a particularly useful skill, you have to admit.

14097.descriptionId: The Nocturnowl Amulet is a magical pendulum that swings back and forth from your neck without stopping, which is great if you want to hypnotise your enemies, or even yourself if you're that way inclined.

14098.descriptionId: When a Nocturnowl struggles to digest part of its meal, it spits it out in the form of a pellet. You'll find these pellets all over the Count's castle, and if you pull one apart, you'll find all kinds of things - adventurer bones, Nocturnowl feathers, and the bitter tang of frustration.

14099.descriptionId: The spines on a Nocturnowl's body act as miniature lightning conductors, so you can walk on thick carpet in these boots without having to worry about the build-up of static electricity.

14100.descriptionId:
This shape-shifting meat is chock-full of alchemical products. Eating it raw won't grant you any superpowers, but it will give you horrific diarrhoea and provoke some extraordinary hallucinations.

(This meat can be harvested by level-100 Hunters.)

14101.descriptionId:
Even though you've only just taken this meat from Nileza's Laboratory, it looks like it came from a corpse that's been drying out for several decades. Only a fool or an inveterate gambler would attempt to cook it, let alone eat it.

(This meat can be harvested by level-100 Hunters.)

14102.descriptionId:
These meatballs are full of frosplasm, rendering them inedible without special processing.

(This meat can be harvested by level-100 Hunters.)

14103.descriptionId:
The origin of these meatballs has been the subject of several scurrilous rumours for decades. Recent studies suggest they may have belonged to those who came to court Missiz Freezz, who kept hold of them as part of her plan to repopulate the island of Frigost.

(This meat can be harvested by level-100 Hunters.)

14104.descriptionId:
The meat has the same texture as an old leather sole, and smells just as bad. Maybe boiling it will make it edible.

(This meat can be harvested by level-100 Hunters.)

14105.descriptionId:
This meat looks like the leather soles on the boots of an aristocrat who has spent far too long in a butcher's workshop.

(This meat can be harvested by level-100 Hunters.)

14106.descriptionId:
This greasy meat is as solid as wood, and only the greatest chefs can hope to remove its dreadful laxative effect.

(This meat can be harvested by level-100 Hunters.)

14107.descriptionId:
Sylargh kept this meat in his pocket, wrapped up in a dirty handkerchief.

(This meat can be harvested by level-100 Hunters.)

14108.descriptionId:
This dark meat is only white in name. The fact that this meat exists at all suggests that the Sinistros are more animal than mechanical, but only Count Harebourg knows the secret of how they are made.

(This meat can be harvested by level-100 Hunters.)

14109.descriptionId:
Darker than the gusset of a Sidimote Trool's underwear, this meat comes from Count Harebourg's personal reserve.

(This meat can be harvested by level-100 Hunters.)

14110.descriptionId: This Preserved Alchimera Meat may now be kept for several days before cooking.

14111.descriptionId: This Preserved Nileza Meat may now be kept for several days before cooking.

14112.descriptionId: These Frozen Preserved Armarine Meatballs may now be kept for several days before cooking.

14113.descriptionId: These Missiz Freezz's Frozen Preserved Meatballs may now be kept for several days before cooking.

14114.descriptionId: This Preserved Leatherbod Sole may now be kept for several days before cooking.

14115.descriptionId: This Preserved Klime Sole may now be kept for several days before cooking.

14116.descriptionId: This Preserved Mechaniac Meat may now be kept for several days before cooking.

14117.descriptionId: This Preserved Sylargh Meat may now be kept for several days before cooking.

14118.descriptionId: This Preserved Sinistro Breast may now be kept for several days before cooking.

14119.descriptionId: This Preserved Harebourg Breast may now be kept for several days before cooking.

14120.descriptionId: Each piece of meat in this sauté tastes different, which makes it very popular with ladies who never know what to order in restaurants.

14121.descriptionId: This withered meat in this sauté looks like a rat that drowned in a jar of formaldehyde. Fortunately, it tastes much better than it looks.

14122.descriptionId: Served cold, these meatballs melt in the mouth, releasing a pleasant sensation of freshness, quickly followed by a complete numbing of the tongue and lower jaw. Serve them to your mother-in-law for a blissful afternoon of peace and quiet.

14123.descriptionId: By serving these meatballs to their menfolk, the women of Frigost can finally get their revenge. Once released into the mouth, the millions of tiny organisms they contain will never be able to reach their true destination.

14124.descriptionId: Despite being stewed for hours, this meat is as tough and chewy as it was when you first picked it up. You can't cut it with a knife or bite it with your teeth, so you may as well turn it into armour.

14125.descriptionId: The Klime Sole in this dish is what gives it the flavour. It's probably best not to serve it to Iops, or you'll find them using it as a bungee rope, no matter how many times you tell them to stop playing with their food.

14126.descriptionId: You can now eat this meat without having to equip a set of stainless steel dentures first.

14127.descriptionId: This meat was wrapped up in a dirty handkerchief, and has a unique flavour as a result. It reminds you of that basic survival class you took, when you were taught to find sustenance in the pickings from your nose.

14128.descriptionId: This gustatory delight would tickle the tastebuds of the god Xelor himself, if only he'd sit down for a few moments and have something to eat. There are some words on the back: "Warning, may contain small pieces of clockwork" and "Not suitable for children under 12 years of age".

14129.descriptionId: Nothing else in the World of Twelve tastes quite like this. Nido, the Meridia of Gastronomy, took more than a century to perfect the recipe.

14130.descriptionId: If you wear this belt for long enough, you'll suddenly crave bacon and eggs for breakfast and want to drink tea all the time. You'll take great pride in the monarchy, and develop a strange sense of humour and a fondness for battered fish and fried potatoes. Mind you, you were hardly a shining example of normality before you put it on, so your friends might not notice the difference.

14131.descriptionId: At one time on Frigost, way before the big freeze, these daggers were the height of harvesting technology... until the day the mainlanders arrived with their scythes. They may not be used for harvesting crops any more, but they're perfect for harvesting souls.

14132.descriptionId: If the owner of these daggers wants them to obtain their characteristic odour of blood, sweat and tears, they must remain undefeated throughout countless battles. This pair stinks, so someone must have done all the hard work for you.

14133.descriptionId: This axe will transform any enemy into a docile mount. Plant it firmly between their shoulder blades, use the handle as a saddle, and with a few cracks of a whip you'll be galloping along in no time.

14134.descriptionId: The humble story of a Frigostian shoemaker.

14135.descriptionId: Are you lonesome tonight, down by the riverside? Has a hard headed woman got you crying for the green, green grass of home? Well, a little less conversation, a little more equipping this shovel! Pull on your sequinned jumpsuit, comb some Trool fat through your hair and get that pelvis jerking uncontrollably - you'll be shake, rattle and rolling in no time! Oh, come on, I'm doing the best I can...

14136.descriptionId: These ashes are all that remain of the last artificial elemental creature that you killed. The lazier inhabitants of Frigost use them in place of cheese when they want a toasted sandwich but can't be bothered to turn the grill on.

14137.descriptionId: I'm sorry to be the one to break this to you, but even this robust plank is better at protecting you from sneak attacks than your Feca guildmate.

14138.descriptionId: This weatherproof leather is thicker than the elastic in your underpants, and far more flexible. It has the same rancid odour, mind you.

14139.descriptionId: If you soak a Chafer's Leather Briefs in this ectoplasmic, magic-filled residue, you'll cool his ardours for at least a century.

14140.descriptionId: This high-precision mechanism is good for nothing in this state. You could melt it down and make a button to replace the one that fell off your trousers.

14141.descriptionId: This root, full to the brim with alchemical nutrients, is difficult to harvest as it crystallises in the ground.

14142.descriptionId: Like your brain, this bolt has never been used, but unlike your brain, it will serve some purpose during its short existence.

14143.descriptionId: This little beauty is Klime's genius incarnate. You can use it to zip up a pocket, your leather coat, or that flap in the seat of your pants.

14144.descriptionId: If you look more closely at the fungal spores trapped in this chunk of ice, you can see some tiny pubic lice larvae in there as well. The fact that they were recovered from Missiz Freezz's private rooms is surely just an unfortunate coincidence.

14145.descriptionId: This is an exact replica of the eye Missiz Freezz's first, last and only butler lost when he peeped through her bedroom keyhole.

14146.descriptionId: This vibrating pick is used to shatter rocks, and should under no circumstances be used for vibrating anything else.

14147.descriptionId: Apparently this ore reacts violently to water, not unlike you, it has to be said. Luckily for your peers, the day of your annual bath is fast approaching. This year, remember to take your clothes off, and avoid using this block to scrape the dead skin off your feet. The results would be... explosive.

14148.descriptionId: This block of Taroudium gives off so much heat you could roast a cartful of Mastogob legs with it and it would still be hot. Are you sure it's safe to keep in your pocket?

14149.descriptionId: The trophy Darwin Chester gave you looks like a plain old piece of Leatherball Leather. When you look a little closer... you see it in close-up.

14150.descriptionId: This drink is good for curing stomach aches and headaches. It can also be used to clean mechanical drills, unclog the engines of Frigostian Carriers, dissolve any Chafers you may have rattling around in your closet, or as a colonic for the Yech'Ti.

14151.descriptionId: It's unlikely that the skidmarks on this towel come from the wheels of a Dragokart. The clue's in the smell, basically.

14152.descriptionId: This g-string, made from genuine nasal hair, will protect you from the many parasites that can be found in those darker places that are dedicated to debauchery and decadence. Make no mistake, this is a top quality undergarment, and its owner would be delighted to have it back.

14153.descriptionId: This is an old copy of Voila! magazine, and now you just need to find someone who's interested in reading such a rag.

14154.descriptionId: This letter, sent to a resident of Castle Harebourg, never reached its owner. The postman who was supposed to deliver it no doubt ended his days as a lightshade, a frozen meal, or a stuffed blow-up doll. Still, he brought more happiness dead than he ever did alive.

14155.descriptionId: You have to fill this flask up with liquid from Count Harebourg's Water Clock. The only similar experience you've ever had is filling up pint glasses at the tavern and liquidating your assets... However will you manage?

14156.descriptionId: They say that if you touch a Feca's glyph with the tip of this rapier, you will be able to decipher the symbols written at its heart. Mind you, they also say that carrying it will help you overcome your fear of water, give you the courage to quit your menial job, and that it has the power to burn down houses, so I'd take that with a pinch of salt if I were you.

14157.descriptionId: Do not open under any circumstances - especially not burning curiosity!

14158.descriptionId: Do not open under any circumstances - especially not burning curiosity!

14159.descriptionId: This cape was worn by Adipose, an obese Sadida who liked to use his defeated enemies as stuffing for his mattresses. The countless bloodstains are testament to the terrible punishment the poor souls endured, and Adipose was consigned to history as one of the cruellest beings the World of Twelve had ever seen. To be fair, you get through a lot of mattresses when you sleep for 23 hours a day, and Bubotron Feathers don't come cheap.

14160.descriptionId: They say that as soon as the bearer of this amulet admits to killing defenceless animals for fun, its sinister powers are revealed when it strangles the unsuspecting blabbermouth to stop them from admitting anything else! Mind you, if that were true, there'd be no one left alive in Amakna...

14161.descriptionId: Appearances can sometimes be deceptive, as this powerful cape demonstrates. You're the proof that it doesn't happen very often, though.

14162.descriptionId: Like many men, Epeni loved to compare his belt strap to other men's belt straps. The more he tugged at it, the longer it became, and the more he polished its buckle, the happier he felt. But happiness is fleeting, and if truth be told, Epeni was incredibly lonely.

14163.descriptionId: Usia Sandals conjure up thoughts of happy summer holidays, with the sun beating down on an endless sandy beach and the sea as warm as bathwater. It's a shame that in Amakna, everywhere like that is overrun with bloodthirsty monsters, or, even worse, with tourists.

14164.descriptionId: You may be surprised to hear that this powerful bow, which once belonged to an archon, one of the chief magistrates of ancient Amakna, was never fired during battle. It was considered a coward's weapon so the pen-pushers had to join in the melee with the foot soldiers, rather than staying at the back out of harm's way. Even back then, wars were lost through misplaced egos.

14165.descriptionId: This evil eye is pretty old and battered. Don't count on it to give you any useful insight.

14166.descriptionId: You painted the letters R, I and P on the oversized tip of this sceptre because you think it looks cool, and because you think death is edgy and artistic. The colour matches your nail polish, your eye shadow, your labret, your Evil Tofu key ring, your Bow Meow outfit, your bedroom and your Chameleon Dragoturkey. Well, for this week at least.

14167.descriptionId: The resounding thud this hammer makes as it comes into contact with yet another poor unfortunate's skull can become very addictive, so you'll need to be careful, because once you've run out of enemies, you'll be tempted to start hitting your friends.

14168.descriptionId: If you struggle to find new reasons to stay at home every time your friends ask you out, then this flamboyant cloak is just what you need. Sling it over your shoulders and it'll generate a torrent of excuses, from "I'm washing my hair" and "My Bow Meow died" to that old chestnut "A band of marauding Mastogobs destroyed my house". Mind you, it's so hideous that no one would want to be seen dead with you anyway, so its vocal talents are somewhat wasted.

14169.descriptionId: This amulet has the extraordinary ability to make you believe everything you're told.

14170.descriptionId: Any dork who tries weaing this headband as a belt will receive a high-voltage bolt of electricity to their nether regions, quickly putting an end to such disillusional practices. "Bzzzing! AAAGH!"

14171.descriptionId: There's a secret hidden in the name of these boots, and although corrupted over time, it becomes obvious once you know the dreadful truth - they're made from mechanically extracted Ouginak sausage meat. There'll be uproar when people find out, but it will be a shame if they stop making them for "ethical reasons", because they're so comfortable!

14172.descriptionId: Take this Lost Djaulian to the Snowbound Village Zaap.

14173.descriptionId: This is a page ripped from the journal in which Professor Imagarihs tracked his progress.

14174.descriptionId: This residue is an essential ingredient of the antidote to Biopantie poison.

14175.descriptionId: These leaves look crude and unwieldy, but they have so many uses that absolutely everyone wants some of them in their bag.

14176.descriptionId: These petals are very rare indeed today, because the special fertiliser needed to keep their tree alive has all but disappeared.

14177.descriptionId: Correctly administered you know where, this antidote will end the paralysis caused by the Biopantie's poison.

14178.descriptionId: If you're reading these lines, it means that the Biopantie's poison has put all my basic functions on hold. You must obtain the follow ingredients and then ask Jon Burrowman to prepare the antidote. He'll know what to do. You can get Alchimera Residue from monsters, Chunky Leaves in the plant pots on the walls, and Petals of Siffonia from Bisale Vinlenta. Hurry! Future Me is fading fast!

14179.descriptionId: This box is filled to the brim with explosives. Sab O'Terr forgot to tell you how dangerous this cargo was going to be.

14180.descriptionId: This box is full of tools used by demolition experts. Sab O'Terr will be glad to get them back.

14181.descriptionId: Your mission is to escort Sab O'Terr in order to help him accomplish his own mission.

14182.descriptionId: Bearbarians are very fond of eating this plant as part of a salad, with honey sauce and pine nuts. The greedier bears bulk up their meal with hunks of Mastogob or pickled Larvae. A good Ygrade Plant salad in the morning will provide you with enough pep to stay wide awake all day long, dontcha know!

14183.descriptionId: Bearbarians are very fond of eating this plant as part of a salad, with honey sauce and pine nuts. The greedier bears bulk up their meal with hunks of Mastogob or pickled Larvae. A good Ygrade Plant salad in the morning will provide you with enough pep to stay wide awake all day long, dontcha know!

A good Ygrade Plant salad in the morning will provide you with enough pep to stay wide awake all day long, dontcha know!

A good Ygrade Plant salad in the morning will provide you with enough pep to stay wide awake all day long, dontcha know!

14187.descriptionId: Doctor Gobotnegg is now under your control. Take him safely to Wes of Tubsterville.

14188.descriptionId: Bearendizer is now under your control. Take him safely to Wes of Tubsterville.

14189.descriptionId: The Mekstagob is now under your control. Take him safely to Wes of Tubsterville.

14190.descriptionId: The Psychopump is now under your control. Take him safely to Wes of Tubsterville.

14191.descriptionId: The Ice Knight is now under your control. Take him safely to Wes of Tubsterville.

14192.descriptionId: Erotegg is now under your control. Take him safely to Wes of Tubsterville.

14194.descriptionId: If you shake this gift box vigorously, you'll find it's not empty. Perhaps the gods are finally smiling down on you.

14195.descriptionId: If you shake this gift box vigorously, you'll find it's not empty. Perhaps the gods are finally smiling down on you.

14196.descriptionId: If you shake this gift box vigorously, you'll find it's not empty. Perhaps the gods are finally smiling down on you.

14197.descriptionId: If you shake this gift box vigorously, you'll find it's not empty. Perhaps the gods are finally smiling down on you.

14199.descriptionId: If you shake this gift box vigorously, you'll find it's not empty. Perhaps the gods are finally smiling down on you.

14200.descriptionId: If you shake this gift box vigorously, you'll find it's not empty. Perhaps the gods are finally smiling down on you.

14201.descriptionId: Koolich Aid is a symbol for those who rebel against parental authority, homework, tidying their bedrooms, being grounded, and for some young adventurers on a quest of self discovery, the law. If you ask your parents why they're being so unfair, they'll say they're doing it for your own good, and that it hurts them more than it hurts you. You hate them, and want to cry in a corner.

14202.descriptionId: If you shake this gift, you'll see it isn't just an empty box. Perhaps the gods are smiling on you for once.

14203.descriptionId: The thermolactic outfit that Mac Gayver knocked together was designed to keep you safe from monsters under the Frozen Lake.

14204.descriptionId: The thermolactic outfit that Mac Gayver knocked together was designed to keep you safe from monsters under the Frozen Lake.

14205.descriptionId: The thermolactic outfit that Mac Gayver knocked together was designed to keep you safe from monsters under the Frozen Lake.

14206.descriptionId: The thermolactic outfit that Mac Gayver knocked together was designed to keep you safe from monsters under the Frozen Lake.

14207.descriptionId: The thermolactic outfit that Mac Gayver knocked together was designed to keep you safe from monsters under the Frozen Lake.

14208.descriptionId: The thermolactic outfit that Mac Gayver knocked together was designed to keep you safe from monsters under the Frozen Lake.

14209.descriptionId: It's highly likely that this bag contains a message, and you should open it and find out. The problem is, you're convinced that if you do, something terrible will happen. The skull and crossbones engraved on the lock was your first clue.

14210.descriptionId: This Bow Meowette won't do its business in your rucksack, it won't complain when you forget to feed it, it won't shed its fur everywhere, it won't wake you up at the crack of dawn, and it's available all year round. What's more, you can do anything you like to it and it won't say a word. You may just have found your soulmate.

14211.descriptionId: The only part of this message that you can read is the signature. The rest is in a language that appears incredibly difficult to pronounce, and yet seems strangely familiar. I wonder if you've heard it somewhere before...

14212.descriptionId: Sylargh has written this short message in the language of the Ice Goblins. Did he pick up a few words while holidaying on Sakai Island? Who knows. One thing's for certain, the Imp and Missiz Freezz are up to something.

14213.descriptionId: This very precise map of the island of Frigost, sketched by Sylargh, isn't finished yet. There are several red crosses on it, each marked "invasion point".

14214.descriptionId: This hide is as smooth as glass and almost transparent. You're not sure where it came from, but something tells you you're better off not knowing.

14215.nameId: Plan for the Snowbound Village Invasion
14215.descriptionId: This map, engraved on a magical skin, could lead Missiz Freezz's Armarines straight to their target. It might also lead the inhabitants of the Snowbound Village straight to their deaths, which is a bit of a failing for a map.

14216.descriptionId: This magic candle is capable of warming any hole into which it is introduced. Particularly fashionable at the start of the 16th century, the Frigostian aristocracy would use them to illuminate their evening parties. The secret to their manufacture was lost during the big freeze and only a very small number remain today.

14217.descriptionId: Pashushu was a powerful Shushu that could create violent gusts of wind. Alma imprisoned it in this statue so that he could take advantage of its power, but you need real patience to master Pashushu's many moods. As luck would have it, you put the statue in this box, not because you're scared of Shushus, but because you're so clumsy you might have broken it if you hadn't.

14218.descriptionId: This old lock will find a new lease of life as the clasp to your chastity belt.

14219.descriptionId: This splinter may look harmless, but in the right hands it's a lethal weapon. Stick it in your enemy's finger, wait for the wound to become infected, and then wait another ten years for the infection to finish them off. A simple, albeit long, way of defeating the Frigost dungeon bosses.

14220.descriptionId: You still bear the scars of having contracted Dremoan Rot.

14221.descriptionId: The splodge on the sole of your boot is all that remains of the worm from the Bearbarian Hive that you stamped on. It smells delightfully of honey, so perhaps you should think about using it to mask the stench of your feet.

14222.descriptionId: You took this sample in the Winter Gardens, but you can't guarantee its effects.

14223.descriptionId: When assembled correctly in a workshop, these bits and pieces will give life to an artificial being.

14224.descriptionId: When assembled correctly in a workshop, these bits and pieces will give life to an artificial being.

14225.descriptionId: When assembled correctly in a workshop, these bits and pieces will give life to an artificial being.

14226.descriptionId: When assembled correctly in a workshop, these bits and pieces will give life to an artificial being.

14227.descriptionId: When assembled correctly in a workshop, these bits and pieces will give life to an artificial being.

14228.descriptionId: You're now the proud owner of a prototype artificial intelligence, which, it has to be said, is currently as useless as a gathering of your in-laws. Mind you, unlike your in-laws, it won't stay useless.

14229.descriptionId: This high quality leather was tanned using revolutionary methods, and an expert would surely pay a handsome sum for it.

14230.descriptionId: When the blade of this sword is plunged into your enemy's entrails, it instantly freezes their blood. To avoid misuse by unruly adventurers, it cannot be equipped.

14231.descriptionId: You've contracted Dremoanic Putrefaction. What are you going to look like if it gets any worse?!

14232.descriptionId: You've contracted Dremoanic Putrefaction. What are you going to look like if it gets any worse?!

14233.descriptionId: You've contracted Dremoanic Putrefaction. What are you going to look like if it gets any worse?!

14234.descriptionId: You've contracted Dremoanic Putrefaction. What are you going to look like if it gets any worse?!

14235.descriptionId: You've contracted Dremoanic Putrefaction. What are you going to look like if it gets any worse?!

14236.descriptionId: You found this strange gem in the depths of Grohlum's pockets. When you touch its vibrant surface, you're overcome with nostalgia, without really understanding why. They say diamonds and regrets are forever, so maybe you'd better stop stroking the pebble if you don't want to sink into depression.

14237.descriptionId: This beautifully crafted piece of metal was found lodged in a Sinistro's chest, which explains why the oversized owl was making such a funny noise.

14238.descriptionId: Created by Missiz Freezz in the depths of the Frostforge, this magic alloy appears to be indestructible, unbreakable, incorruptible and untarnishable. Basically, it's hardcore.

14239.descriptionId: According to Henual, the Overseer of Time, this high precision chronomagic device should be able to regulate the currents of temporal flux that swirl around Count Harebourg's Water Clock. Will it work as planned? Well, it's not like you've got any better ideas.

14240.descriptionId: It's not just the watch that's working: destiny is ticking away as well... According to Decimandi, you should be able to use this enchanted pocketwatch to dispel the temporal ice that surrounds the Water Clock's minute hand. Mind you, if you believe that, you probably believe in Granny Capping's Dofus as well.

14241.descriptionId: This is an invitation to a fetish evening in Klime's private quarters. When the party's over, I'm pretty sure you'll be able to think of another meaning for the initials S and M, and not just "sick monster".

14242.descriptionId: Your face is still smarting from the impact made by Djaul's fist. Ow!

14243.descriptionId: The currents of air swirling around your body are a spine-tingling reminder of Jiva's blessing.

14244.descriptionId: Without the three other bits, this piece of key is as useless as a portable fan on Frigost.

14245.descriptionId: Without the three other bits, this piece of key is as useless as a portable fan on Frigost.

14246.descriptionId: Without the three other bits, this piece of key is as useless as a portable fan on Frigost.

14247.descriptionId: Without the three other bits, this piece of key is as useless as a portable fan on Frigost.

14248.descriptionId: Unlike your allies, this key will allow you access to the Water Clock Tower. Just don't expect it to protect you once you're inside.

14249.descriptionId: Didn't anyone mention the side effects?

14250.descriptionId: Unlike other alchemic potions of dubious origins, you know that this is an authentic Nileza creation. How can you be so sure? Well, you were there when it was made. Unfortunately, you also know that it has terrible side-effects, including complete paralysis.

14251.descriptionId: This biscuits are as hard as stone. With a bit of practice, they can be used to knock Gullipops or old people off Frigost pier.

14252.descriptionId: These notes reveal Missiz Freezz's thoughts on how to escape the effects of the curse. She speculates that dying in order to be reincarnated in another body could be a way of leaving the island without suffering any side effects. Strangely, the notepaper gives off the same intoxicating scent as Emma Skulated's perfume.

14253.descriptionId: This notebook is in fact a diary, and Emma Skulated has written down the details of her many missions in it. Judging by the number of pages she's filled, Sram should be very proud of his disciple.

14254.descriptionId: You have Emma Skulated's dark secret in your hands, but you're not sure if it's the fruits of modern science, or the results of a madman's terrible experiments. No one will ever know.

14255.descriptionId: This implement of torture is used to introduce vast amounts of liquid into the bodies of prisoners in a very short amount of time, no matter which orifice is used. Once it caught on in the taverns of Frigost, it was banned, then reserved only for use by qualified alchemists.

14256.descriptionId: Mini Inuits use similar muffs when handling dangerous metals, primarily to avoid cutting themselves and contracting tetanus.

14257.descriptionId: The blade of this leather slicer is so sharp that it can sever verrucae from soles in the blink of an eye, and cut through even the toughest of leathers.

14258.descriptionId: Count Harebourg's workers use this pick almost exclusively during the winter months to shatter ice and the skulls of unfortunate Mini Inuits.

14259.descriptionId: "What's this Xelor magnifying glass for?" is the question anyone who doesn't know the answer asks themselves.

14260.descriptionId: This is a magic marble. You don't know how you know, you just know that you know. What you don't know is how to use it, and sticking it up your nostril doesn't seem to have had any effect, apart from stopping you from being able to breathe. Perhaps that's its magic power!

14261.descriptionId: You kept this as a souvenir from your shell hunts. Is it the slightly rotten fragrance or the moist, pinkish appearance which keeps you coming back for more? Only you know for sure.

14262.descriptionId: At first glance, Vulkanian Shirts look to be plain old Barbrossa Shirts with the labels changed, shipped over to be sold to tourists at hiked up prices. Could the packaging industry really be that careless and/or unethical?

14263.descriptionId: The newspapers are filled with Grozilla and Grasmera's doings, and handbags made with their scales are must-have accessories in high-flying circles. Some say these bags make their owner sprout a third arm; others claim they grant superpowers, or at least glow-in-the-dark powers. It's as if the good old class spells weren't enough for people!

14264.descriptionId: Grozilla had some false teeth cast to make himself look dreadfully frightening. On your small frame, the effect is even more terrifying.

14265.descriptionId: With a couple of these taped onto your back, you might just manage to pass your humpback off as some kind of exotic costume. Sadly, nothing can be done for your nightmare-inducing face.

14266.descriptionId: What was an organic pouch filled with coal doing in Grasmera's oozing guts? Before you ponder this question any further, please wash your hands.

14267.descriptionId: One of the first rituals Zeurg established at the Temple of Osamodas was that of slowly sitting down on this joint until it disappeared completely. Disciples' shrieks could be heard all the way over at the Tofu House.

14268.descriptionId: This organic pouch will withstand even the highest temperatures, which means that you can safely bury your head in it when your ears are burning with shame.

14269.descriptionId: Use this scroll to learn the Spyglass emote. Whether you're mad about Olvido or more Malava's kind of adventurer, you'll always be leagues ahead of your enemies with one eye on the horizon.

14270.nameId: The Folkloric Chronicles of Anne Thrope-Oloji
14270.descriptionId: The must-have guide for anyone who loves a party!

14271.descriptionId: If you're always risking your life on a roll of the dice, then you'll love this necklace, which is just like the one worn by the famous Lucky Bow Meow. It'll even let you use the Kama Baraka in Kerub's shop. You lucky devil!

14272.descriptionId: Certain nasty strains of this chronic illness have to be treated by meditation in rehabilitation centres. Luckily for you, you caught the nice kind. It should wear off all on its own with a little bit of exercise.

14273.descriptionId: Some narrow-minded historians claim that Bonta has never had a monarch. Here is the irrefutable proof that they're wrong. In-depth studies of the fabric seem to confirm that the royal pants were worn on the head as well as on the buttock, which made them very useful for diplomatic meetings gone wrong.

14274.descriptionId: Legend has it that this power-charged weapon was created by Ulgrude of Thunder, Protector of Martalo. In reality, it's far more likely that it's just a shepherd's staff. The Gobbette that's been following you around lately favours this explanation... Unless she just finds that you two have a lot in common?

14275.descriptionId: According to an old wives' tale, anyone who drinks this water will feel obliged to reveal a terrible secret on the town square, in front of everyone. Luckily for you, the refreshing droplets in this flask have been diluted with Crocodyl Tears. Nobody will have to know what you did last summer.

14276.descriptionId: You're going to be an absolute superstar in the sheepfold, and it's all thanks to Kerub Crepin. Just make sure you don't accidentally start a fight, or the illusion will disappear (even if the odour may linger a while).

14277.descriptionId: It's said that this silken belt was worn by the famous Master Nabur, the martial arts specialist. Apparently he enchanted it to alert him when danger was approaching... Unfortunately, this magic seems to have worn off, which is too bad for you, as you could do with being saved by the bell from time to time.

14278.descriptionId: Do as the Dark Miners did! Break the chains that bind you to this life of slavery, tell your masters where to stick it, and wreak havoc everywhere you go! The revolution is now! Also, if anything, well y'know... happens to you during the revolution, these chains will look so cool hanging off your ghost!

14281.descriptionId: This phylactery emits a soft warmth that will bring back fond memories of the sultry night you spent sandwiched between a Dragostess and a Dreggon Warrior. It also attracts Moskitos in the night.

14283.descriptionId: When it was first made, this belt didn't look Vulkanian enough for anyone's taste. Without further ado, it was smelted, soaked in tourist blood three times in a row, covered in soot and riddled with holes to make it look "worn-in". Oh, the whims of fashion.

14284.descriptionId: Raval was the one who lit the burning flame you can see in the eyes of the ghosts of those who fell during the Crimson Dawn. Nobody knows when this flame will go out. Don't count on it to keep you warm on those long, cold, lonely nights, because though it may feed on bodies, hearts and souls, it's as cold as a YeCh'Ti burp.

14285.descriptionId: This heavy helmet will protect your head from falling lava and fluttering ash next time you visit a volcano. Unfortunately, it's not much good against currents of hot air, which will zip in one ear and out the other, sizzling important information to a crisp.

14286.descriptionId: This pince-nez guarantees that you'll bump into a lot more people than you used to. Too bad you feel absolutely no need to be sociable any more, what with the beautiful, shimmering, fragmented view of the world you're discovering.

14287.descriptionId: The metaphysical properties of this expensive crystal allow it to light up in the presence of arsenic. You'll be able to use it as a halogen lamp the next time your alliance has a banquet!

14288.descriptionId: The tyrannical employees in charge of security in Vulkania Park use these wands on tourists to amuse themselves during breaks. What, you've never played Jabble, Prodopoly or Poke 'Er? You've never lived!

14289.descriptionId: This axe feels so light in your hands that you get the dizzying feeling that it could cleave an unsuspecting tourist or a nosy neighbour in half without much input on your part.

14290.descriptionId: This rare stone will give you the influence you need to create an alliance. To destroy one, all you need to do is attempt to share a valuable piece of loot between several members.

14291.descriptionId: "The Lumberjacks of the Apocalypse" was a cool name when you were fifteen and you dreamt of being a lumberjack, but somehow it didn't help much when it came to meeting girls or recruiting new guilds. Pack up the chopping block and start life afresh with a brand new alliance name!

14292.descriptionId: It seemed like a good idea at the time, but face it: nobody can tell that your emblem is supposed to be an emancipated Bwork hunting down his own parents to make a statement about freedom. Nobody. Do the world a favour and change that awful emblem now!

14293.descriptionId: This magical item is the gentleman's (and gentlelady's) way to mark one's territory. It should be used to excess by all those who conquer to pass the time.

14294.descriptionId: The flour ground using Barley is very popular with fans of light, airy bread. The Lousy Pigs, on the other hand, prefer to use it to make a stodgy gruel that not even a starving Trool would touch.

14295.descriptionId: Rye has been considered magical by many civilisations through the ages, but the Lousy Pigs couldn't care less. They just crush the grains between their bum cheeks to produce a rough powder used as an exfoliating scrub.

14296.descriptionId: Only a handful of people have ever tasted the wheat pancakes Lousy Pigs like eating, but the reactions are unanimous: they taste disgusting, serve absolutely no purpose in terms of nutrition, and are as hard and unappetising as a Plain Crackler. The only thing they're good for is skimming on Cania Lake.

14297.descriptionId: It's said that the Lousy Pigs use Malt to distil a very strong alcohol which is at the root of the poor eyesight suffered by many of the species.

14298.descriptionId:
With this shield, you can share your point of view without saying a word. It's brandished by everyone who's anyone during public debates, and the most energy-efficient adventurers equip a Pluswan ring at the same time to show their support with minimum effort. Use with care, lest it take control of your life.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

14299.descriptionId:
This thing can talk... And talk... And talk... And talk! It picks up phrases it likes and repeats them to Witter Beanies in the area. At first, these hats were quite a good alternative to carrier pigeons, until they became so commonly used that the same messages started going round and round in circles, resulting in a permanent hubbub. These days they're also used for a parlour game called Rage K-Witter in which each participant dons a Witter beanie and the one who can stand the noise the longest is pronounced the winner.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

14300.descriptionId: This amulet will give you the answer to the ultimate question of life, the Krosmoz and everything. But you'll need to know how to ask it. Did you mean the cosmos?

14301.descriptionId:
This cloak is very special indeed, as it allows its wearer to display anything at all on his or her back. Most dumb adventurers just use it to show off hunting trophies and count how many people are taking an interest in them, but a few canny wearers have managed to generate a real following with their original ideas.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

14302.descriptionId: This ring starts glowing when it senses hostile plants nearby. If you're going to the Petrified Forest, you may as well take it off... But just so you know, you'll also be wide open to attacks from mutant plants.

14303.descriptionId:
This cloak used to belong to a fellow named Oddrick, one of those scholars who often crossed the fine line between genius and folly. One time, he managed to inadvertently create a species of motorised plants armed with buzz saws! Time has forgotten what became of Oddrick, but traces such as this one remind us of his creations. Rumours do abound that Noo might have something to do with their disappearance.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

14304.descriptionId: This amulet isn't anywhere near as sharp as it looks, which will be a relief to most people... Although perhaps not to the Sacriers who saw it from afar, noticed its resemblance to an instrument of torture, and bought it on the spot.

14305.descriptionId:
If it's dark enough, this shield will hide you from view. Of course, your position will be given away immediately by the whimpers of fear you can't help but emit when you don't have your night light.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

14306.descriptionId: With its strong smell of black pudding pizza, this shield is your VIP pass to skulking around Sphincter Cell's lair without drawing attention to yourself. Sometimes, smelling a rat is a very good thing indeed.

14307.descriptionId:
This mask is a wooden replica of Captain Amakna's, designed for children. But that doesn't give you the right to use it on them.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

14308.descriptionId:
From far away, this shield looks like a giant kama coin. Don't be surprised if you amass a gaggle of whispering Enutrofs over the next day or two. Or if Ecaflips start flipping you in the air to make decisions. Or if Srams start dropping from covert hiding places in the eaves of houses to assault you. This shield might just be more hassle than it's worth.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

14309.descriptionId:
Carried on the wings of justice, you're convinced that all you do is just and good. Don't wear this cloak when you're fighting with Srams or Rogues (even if they're your allies), or you might find yourself stripped of your wings, your sense of righteousness, and your dignity.
(Equip this item in a ceremonial slot to use its appearance.)

14310.descriptionId: With these boots on, "taking somebody under your wing" has a whole new meaning. They enable their wearer much more flexibility when it comes to moving around, which is especially useful when it comes to dodging attacks.

14311.descriptionId: You don't know what the symbol engraved on this thing means, but who cares? It leaves an awesome stamp on the bruised faces of the enemies you defeat. You could always carve your initials in their flesh with the end of your sword, but that takes so much longer.

14373.descriptionId: If you shake this gift box vigorously, you'll find it's not empty. Perhaps the gods are finally smiling down on you.
